title: This chair is a BEAST!
text:
Upon opening the box, we were impressed with the fortitude of each part - it is very weighted and similar to chrome (at least in finish and heaviness). This is much akin to a Chevy Bel Air vs modern cars as far as comparing it to previous desk chairs which I have owned, it is clearly built to last and sustain a lot of weight and use.

I left the assembly to my partner, who said that other than the heaviness of the parts when wrangling them, was incredibly easy. The instructions do suggest that you make use of the box it arrived in to help prop parts as you screw them together because you will need the support, and he did this and said it made it much more manageable.

I walked into the room once it was finished and gaped at how large this chair is. In fact, I felt like a child climbing into the seat, my legs left to dangle and I kept scooting back further and further (You can lower it with the pneumatic lift so that your feet touch the ground, it also has nice rounding of the seat front to prevent your back of knee circulation from being cut off!). The seat is HUGE both front to back and side to side and can comfortably accommodate larger bodies. I never had so much room in desk chair seat before! But the solidity of this chair is what has me in awe - I feel safe and comfortable in it. No teetering, no awkward tilting, nothing bad! The only plastic parts to the structure of the chair is the pneumatic lift handle and the wheels (which seem more like high impact plastic and dense), so no fear of parts breaking under weight strain and movement.

I would say that the only downside to this chair is now my partner is jealous of it and we're going to have to get him one of his own so he that doesn't pilfer mine. Excellent desk chair, an easy 5 stars

title: I am very disappointed with this steamer; design is poor-- it has too many parts – 2.5 stars
text:
I am a steamer fanatic who mostly cooks everything with steam; this is my 15th steamer! Unfortunately, this is not even worth the money I have to lay out for this, in my opinion.

I have been steaming most of my meals for about 30 years. In those 30 years, I owned or previously owned 14 steamers. This is my 15th steamer and it is a whopping disappointment. I put this through the paces and it is one of my least favorite steamers. Yes it works, but it is cumbersome and bulky and has too many moving parts.

WHAT is in the BOX - In addition to the instruction manual, this comes in 11 parts as follows:

- Base unit
- Heater cap (also known as steam guard)
- Three (3) steam tray bottoms
- Three (3) steaming basket "rims" (upper, middle, and lower or what I call small, medium, and large)
- Top lid
- Rice bowl
- Drip Tray

FEATURES
- The steaming controls are LED and it comes with preset times for eggs, rice, fish, chicken/meat, and vegetables. I do not need this but newbies might like it.

- There is a keep-warm function (it is unclear for how long) and a timer function that allows steaming to be delayed anywhere from 1 minute to 12 hours and 59 minutes. I tested both the timer and keep-warm feature and they work well.

- The baskets are an opaque plastic and each basket is two loose pieces.

- The steamer has boil-dry protection so that it turns off if the reservoir is out of water.

LIKES
- The steamer cooks almost equally with all three baskets simultaneously. I usually put the food that gets done the quickest (the most delicate foods like fish) on top away from the intensity of the steam. The uppermost basket does not cook as fast but this is expected.

- It can steam a lot of food since it has three vertical levels.

- I can steam 18 eggs at one time--six in each basket. When I steam eggs, I want them to steam the same. I tested this and the eggs steamed in the top basket were less cooked than those in the bottom basket. However, this is to be expected. Note that I leave the uncooked eggs on the counter for about one hour before steaming so that they do not break during cooking.

- The keep-warm and delay-start features are nice to have.

- When in operation, the steamer is relatively quiet until the food is ready; that is when the beeps sound.

- A full reservoir provides enough steam for at least 60 minutes of steaming which is very generous; most steamers only last 45 minutes on full.

- Descaling is easy just like it is for all the other steamers I own. This steamer will develop mineral build up on the heating element. All that has to be done is to fill the reservoir with equal parts vinegar and water and heat on high for twenty minutes. I actually use almost 100% vinegar in most of my steamers. I have not used this long enough yet to implement descaling.

DISLIKES
- The opaqueness of the baskets makes it difficult to see how the food is doing during steaming.

- Each basket comes in two pieces. It is also easy to have the bottom slip out if not seated correctly. In addition, the top has to be placed on the uppermost basket just right or that will slip off too.

- The LED is awkward in the sense that the on/off button has to be pressed more than once to start the steaming process. I kept thinking the steaming would start and then the unit would turn off. The only way I could tell I got it right was when the two dots (:) blinked.

- There are way too many moving parts. The design of the baskets is very poor. They come apart like a springform pan without the spring.

- The unit with the baskets is also big and bulky and does not collapse into a small enough footprint for storage.

- There is no reservoir refill hole on the outside of the steamer. If I were serial steaming various foods, I would run out of water and would have to handle a hot steamer to refill or wait until it cools. When there is an outside hole for the reservoir, I can use a teapot or something with a spout to refill the steamer during operation or between operations without getting burned. Since the reservoir holds about 60 minutes of water, this issue will not affect me much as I rarely do more than two steaming sessions that go beyond one hour.

- Although this does not affect me at all, beware that the steamer is tall when in use. In addition, the cord is short as is expected of any appliance such as this.

In summary, I am utterly disappointed in this steamer. Although it works, it is cumbersome to use, too bulky, and has too many pieces. The design is not well-thought out. My main disappointment is that each basket is two pieces (a flat removable bottom and a plastic ring for the sided), which makes absolutely no sense to me.

For those who are interested, here are MY STEAMERS - PAST and PRESENT

PAST 3 STEAMERS that eventually broke:

- One small round Black and Decker Steamer (extinct now) which was great and super small but only lasted about two years. This was my first steamer that I purchased in the 1990's.

- One [[ASIN:B00004SPEI Krups Optisteam Plus]]. I had this since February 1999 and it was my most used steamer and very similar to the Oster steamer.

- One [[ASIN:B00073HLMU Oster 5711 Mechanical Food Steamer]], which I used daily for my oatmeal and most dinners until it died.

CURRENT 12 STEAMERS (counts one that I have three of):

- This one [[ASIN:B07ZFKMVL3 AmazonBasics 12.5 Quart 3-Tiered Digital Food Steamer]]. The basket design is poor and it is too bulky. I would pass.

- This [[ASIN:B07H79RGVJ Secura Electric Food Steamer]]. This is my favorite steamer. No plastic comes in contact with the food. It has few moving parts and steams evenly and well. If I had the room, I would buy a second one because, as of this writing, I cannot bear the thought of being without it.

- One [[ASIN:B01MZF7ZFZ Breville Steam Zone steamer]] – this one is large; has an annoying ticking noise during operation and cooks unevenly. The option of using only the steaming tray w/o the pots allows for cooking large items like fillets of fish. I rarely use this steamer due to its lackluster functionality.

- One [[ASIN:B008FX6KH6 T-fal VC133851 Balanced Living Compact Electric Food Steamer, 4-Quart, Silver]] – this one is too small, is discontinued, and its steam is not hot enough requiring longer cooking times. I use this one occasionally for rolled oats or some vegetables.

- One [[ASIN:B00019G8IS Oster 5712 Electronic Food Steamer]] - I use this daily for my oatmeal and most dinners. This is still my GOTO steamer in addition to my Secura. This steamer will fail soon as I have had it almost six years and they usually do not last more than that before it burns out. This steamer also appears to be discontinued which is why a once $30 steamer is now being sold for almost $275.

- Three [[ASIN:B000JJMER4 Richard Simmons EST7 Steam-Heat Electronic Food Steamers]] which I absolutely love. These are very large steamers and are larger than the Breville. They have three steaming chambers and are good for steaming full meals (protein, starch, and vegetable) that FINISH at the same time by counting down in reverse. This remains my other GOTO steamer. This is the type of steamer that is not for everyone and which is why it was discontinued due to lack of customer interest. Because I love it so much, I purchased three as I cannot bear to be without one even though I do not use it daily.

- One rice steamer, the [[ASIN:B00007J5U7 Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 5-1/2-Cup Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer, Premium White]], which is excellent but which I do not use nearly enough. It is also a little different that these other steamers in function so they really cannot be compared.

- One [[ASIN:B003NTXFVG Hard Anodized Non-Stick Wok with Steamer and Lid]]. In addition to this, I also have another very small pot with a steamer on top but I am not counting this one.

- One Stove-top fish steamer similar to the [[ASIN:B0002IBJG4 Norpro Stainless Steel Fish Poacher]].

- One asparagus steamer very similar to [[ASIN:B079DD9115 this one]].

UPDATE: I forgot to attach a picture of the two piece baskets so I am attaching it now.

title: Useful yet.. love it like a piece of added art in the room!
text:
This will arrive is separate pieces- so, if living n an apartment or, place you need to carry upstairs or, by yourself it will be very doable.. even if box looks big- it isn’t too heavy for x1 person..

Overall, a great addition to a room needing a bit more “closet or, hanging” space. It could be a great addition inside a closet without shelving. Great for the odd shape closet under the stairs, or even the laundry room. Personally, I chose our guestroom, which is also, our “return from college summer room” for our daughter.. Yep! When she headed to college we took over her room as our guest space.. boom!

This works a lot of places because it’s not too big- it’s best “creature comfort” for fit, is the height.. this stands as tall as a standard 5 dresser drawer- not near as big OR, long as a rolling rack!! I would consider this best used for extra items or, even temporary hanging space- being made up a bamboo wood… It lacks stronger integrity of holding an entire wardrobe like metal or even oak! But, that is obvious it’s not made for hearty work just by shape, size and material. (we do use an extra rolling rack to hang winter jackets and snow clothes in Utah! But, of course that needs the metal the the appropriate type of support..)

I’ll skip long details of building but, TAKE NOTE: I received wrong instructions They were for a garmet stand- just not this one!!! Also, hardware had 2 screws that were NOT correct length- so, had to hit Store for correct item. (2 screws were too short to go thru 2 pieces of wood- as our screws came all same length?!) What saved me- was looking at the online photos- whew! Also, photos posted by other reviews showed the inside of instruction manual- I’m grateful! This doesn’t come with its own tool. So, a phillips(✖️for any who may not know!) screw driver is needed.. along with a little bit of patience.. **if you have pair of needle nose pliers to help get torque you need on the back side to tighten up for much needed stability/sturdiness. Some screws are set below flush or set into the wood itself- so, it’s difficult, impossible to hold the back side to tighten without something to apply counter pressure for tightening! (Yes! I said I’d spare extra details.. trust me, I did! Just know to have these basics above and some common sense.. any issues with instructions look at reviews, the added help was posted there for myself!) building time = 40 min. After I got correct hardware.

Once assembled it looks nice- but, OMG- it grows on me each time I see it.. CRAZY, right..?!! What’s crazier, this is “a piece that serves a purpose” yet, for me it’s become a quaint, cleaver, accessory and a fun focal point! I’ve put a few wooden hangers on the bar to dress it up along with a few rose gold hangers!! Oh, and 2 woven baskets at the bottom. I am confident I’m going to end up loving this, no matter how much I use!

If looking for a smaller spaced option for hanging, storing or, drying clothing… This is a fun solution- the overall assembly could be better configured and appropriate instructions and hardware sent- and still.. I’m loving it!! (Refer to reviews if wrong info sent..it’s all there.)

Hope this info helps… Feel free to let me know

title: Cool Addition to a Modern Home
text:
I’ve grown increasingly appreciative of artwork over the years and today, I have a greater number of works of art on the walls of my home than at any time in the past. There is no specific type of artwork that I prefer- as long as it catches my eye and matches the décor of a specific room, than it’s a work of art I want. I do, however, seem to be drawn to abstract art work more than others and that is what led me to get this work of art from Rivet.

With this piece of art, you get oval- ish shapes featuring black, silver, and pink. The print is canvas stretched over wood and comes complete with the necessary hardware so it’s ready to hang on the wall of your choosing. I had a place in mind when I decided to get this work of art, but then one of my kiddos stepped forward and claimed it for her room. With its unique color combination, it’s not the type of art suitable for any space. It will only match in certain rooms and décor, so look closely at the different pics here on Amazon and decide where it would go best, before you purchase.

This work of art comes in three sizes. I have the middle, 16 x 24 size, which is just right for the place I hung the canvas- one of my kiddos bedrooms. Her room has a modern flair and this art piece does match up nicely. The black, grey, and pink are a little unusual, but so are the other items in her room, so it matches up well. The ovals almost look like the paw prints of animals and it does get your attention. People who see this art work for the first time often make a first glance, look away, then look back at it again and walk up to the art, to examine the patterns. They are often not sure what they are looking at, but then appreciate the abstractness for what it is.

I like adding art to my home and this work of art from Rivet has proven a nice addition to my kid’s bedroom. She likes the patterns and it does match well with the other aspects of her personal space, and her personality. It’s a cool work of canvas art and a great choice for the modern home.

title: makes nice looking pizza, bakes evenly
text:
We make a lot of pizza. We have some pizza cookware but nothing in cast iron. Since we use cast iron for everything else, I figured it would be nice to try out a cast iron pizza pan. So my husband received this as a gift from me.

The pan makes roughly a 14" pie max. The pan is a little over an inch deep. Not a big pizza, but should accommodate most dough recipes (and definitely if you buy a ball of dough at store).

Most of the pies I have made I have just pressed the dough into the pan, cold. I sometimes spray it with olive oil or refined coconut oil, but sometimes not. If the seasoning is maintained, it shouldn't need any additional oil just prior to use.

It cooks the pizza dough evenly, and I dont feel like I need to keep checking the bottom side. I found that I can get a crisper crust by pressing the dough into a an already hot pan (just be careful).

I like it better than a pizza stone. I like it about same or maybe a little more than a non stick pizza pan (the kind with holes) of equal size. Like all cast iron, the pan is a bit heavy, so keep that in mind.

Cleans up well- just wipe it out, or follow cast iron cleaning instructions (use a scrubber, or some coarse salt and oil, wipe out, keep dry)

I would like to see slightly longer handles or something different in design. I find that I am touching the pizza dough when I try to grab the pan from the oven with pot holders. It is fine if I am making a smaller pizza, but if I am using up the whole pan, then I am more apt to touch the crust when handling the pan (with pot holders).

I don't take the pizza out of the pan when it is done. I keep the pizza on the pan and cut it on the pan. I found the ridges get a little in my way while trying to slice the pizza. It could be a matter of my having a bad slicer- but the ridges keep me from pressing down hard enough to make up for it.

I haven't tried baking anything else in this pan. I imagine it would do alright with other items that can be baked in a shallow pan. Just remember, as seen in the pictures.. that the pan has ridges inside, so don't bother with cookies or such unless you were to line it with parchment paper or tinfoil first. Bet it would be fine for broiled vegetables, too. And bacon. Bacon would do well on this (and you would be seasoning at same time. Win!)

But right now, it is only used for pizza in our house. Now I need to go make pizza!

Hopefully you found my review helpful. If I learn anything new, I will be back to update. Take care!

text: The Ravenna Home Waterloo Modern Slipcover Sofa is practical. It’s not large (I’d describe it as compact), probably about the size of a small loveseat. Two people can fit comfortably. When it arrived, the first thing that I noticed was that it was well packaged. There was lots of padding in the box. Once opened, you will remove the pillows, cushions and 2 knobs from inside the body of the sofa.  The bottom cushions (those that contain the springs) were located in vacuum sealed plastic. Simply open and they inflate. The instructions are pictures/diagrams, but I would suggest that you lay out everything first so that you can visualize. It is pretty easy to assemble. No tools were necessary. My husband used his hands and it took him about 30 minutes to put it together.  It’s perfect for a dorm room or a small apartment. The fabric cover is a nice, slightly textured, gray. You can accessorize with a myriad of colored pillows. That will automatically elevate the look of the sofa. It appears to durable and well made. Because it is dark, I think it will be stain resistant.  And finally, this sofa is affordable and should fit everyone’s budget. This sofa deserves 3.5 stars.

title: Very heavy baskets for linens.

I don't think that this is going to get crushed or damaged in any way, so the benefit is that this is very sturdy, but it's also a little unwieldy and hard to move around. This is not a problem unless you're not expecting it. If you plan to set this into a shelf or linen closet where you mostly leave it in place and put things inside of it occasionally, it'll be just fine. Given the sturdiness of the top frame, it is very easy to pick it up and move it around from the perspective that you have the handle, as long as the weight isn't a problem for you.

title: Pretty artwork but harder than I thought to put up
text:
I was a little surprised to see how heavy this was. Because of the weight, studs, or mollies are definitely needed to hang.
What's nice is that each wood square is 16". Which means the center is at the 8" mark. Easier to hit a stud (16 on center) with each row.
The hardest part, of hanging this, was to figure out exactly how to get each square evenly spaced between the ones around it. Wish some type of instructions came with it to help with hanging ideas.
Took a bit of math, a level, and we used tile spacers in between to get it even. In other words, it took us a long time to figure this out and still couldn't get it up right. I guess a smarter way would be to put it on a thin piece of painted plywood and then hanging it into the studs of the wall. Which is probably the way we're going to go so I don't have a wall of marks and holes.
It's pretty and will look great on the wall we want to put it up on once we do all the extra work. But, I think the work will be well worth having this up on our living room wall.
I'll have to come back and update once we get it up on the wall.

title: Get rid of your old mattress today. You need this in your life!
text:
Our old inner spring mattress needed replaced. The fabric was wearing thin and the springs were starting to poke us in the back at night. Talk about uncomfortable! I was constantly at the chiropractor seeking an adjustment. Plus, I was always tired, because I was always tossing and turning.

However, I had never contemplated getting a memory foam style mattress. I'd heard those can make you hot at night, and I already run hot when I'm horizontal. But when this one became available, we decided to give it a shot and a "test drive."

When the box was delivered to my home, the mattress was rolled flat inside. The box weighed around 75 pounds and took two of us to carry it in. It unpacked easily enough, and as soon as we cut the clear wrap, the mattress began to inflate. I know that some reviewers say you shouldn't sleep on it until 24-48 hours later because there was a strong chemical smell coming off of it. However, we never noticed any scent but the subtle aroma of chocolate. I know, weird right? So we were able to sleep on it the same night it arrived.

Oh, my, God! What a difference a mattress makes! Once we laid down on it, we never wanted to get up. You don't sink down into it very much. It just cradles you very nicely. Also, it gave my back ample support and I haven't needed my chiropractor since I got the mattress. Finally, it doesn't sleep hot at all. This mattress actually keeps me very cool, so I can't imagine I could possible get any better sleep than I do now!

Lesson here? Don't fear a bed without springs. This is the most comfortable bed I have ever been on in my life! You'll love it.

title: It's a 1500 watt electric heater - that's it.
text: Just a few things. I bought one of these 3 years ago, used it for one winter and my sister 'borrowed' it and hasn't returned it yet, so I bought another one. This one is the same but W/O the oscillation.  A 1500 watt heater will only produce 1500 watts of heat, no more - no less. You can spend 5 times as much for a heater and get a nice cabinet and maybe wi-fi access with your phone and maybe a longer cord or whatever, but it will not produce more heat. 1500 watts only produces a finite amount of heat, resistance in this case, and can not make more. Electricity costs vary wildly across the US and around the world, and those costs change from minute to minute. This heater, running on high (1500 watts) will use a LOT of electricity compared to the newer bulbs that most people have in the homes today, about 160 times more that the average  9W (equivalent 60 W) light bulb used in modern homes. Space heaters, because of what they're designed to do - turn electrical energy into heat - use large amounts of electricity to quickly heat your home.

title: Big, Beautiful Table
text:
If you have the room and the money, this makes for a huge and beautiful coffee table that itself can be the centerpiece of your entire living room. The first thing worth noting is the size. Even with "some assembly required" this thing is huge and heavy. Too huge and heavy to ship via UPS, so it will come either by FedEx Ground or more likely via freight. So, I would not lay any bets on getting free overnight delivery, even if you are a Prime member.

The table basically comes in 3 parts. The table top and two parts that make up the "legs". It also comes with the necessary hardware for assembly, which isn't much. It took me far, far more time to unbox and clean up the mess from the packing materials than it did to assemble the product. Just make sure to assemble it where you want it because it is very difficult to move around once the legs are attached.

The wood table top is absolutely stunning and looks hand made. I'm not sure what type of hard wood it is made of, but the material and design are very impressive. About the only downside is the fact that the surface is not perfectly flat, so it can't be used to write on and can be difficult to balance small glasses on, like ones meant for wine or champagne. This is my only real criticism of the table other than it's high cost.

As I said before, if you have a house with enough space and an extra $600 to spend this will make a wonderful addition to your living room. The build quality, materials and design are all excellent and it should last a lifetime, unlike the vast majority of furniture being made today.

Then last night my son decided to make some chicken nuggets in a 425 oven. Suddenly I felt a lot of anxiety and couldn't breathe, it was like every bit of air was sucked out of the house, but no visual "smoke", just a strange chemical smell in the air. He threw the mat he used into water and we had to open windows and air the house out when it was 20 degrees outside! Then after doing some research on silicone mats trying to figure out what that was all about I learned that some cheaper manufacturers will add fillers that can smoke at high temperatures. All silicone is great, but the fillers made for a nasty mat. These are definitely the cheaper version. I am bummed because I bought a bunch as Christmas gifts and now I will have to tell those I gifted them to that they are junk. Buyers Beware. I would be concerned for bird owners, too.

text:
Heater works great, heats area under desk by feet and legs very well. Only MAJOR DISAPPOINTMENT: the INDICATOR LIGHT ONLY SHOWS WHEN PLUGGED IN. In many cases, that will be a one time event in the life of the heater. What I thought it would show is when HEATER IS TURNED ON! That will occur thousands (hopefully) of times. When I go to bed at night, it would be nice to know if I forgot to turn the heater off, AT A GLANCE. Otherwise, it can cycle all night and wast energy. Potentially, some bad things can happen when you are not there to monitor it. Just to indicate if a wall outlet if "HOT" or not wastes its potential. If the indicator came on when the heater is on, testing the wall socket could be accomplished by turning the heater on before plugging it in. Then the indicator light would also show if the wall outlet is "HOT" or not. Disappointed! I am giving it 1 star, to help call attention to this issue, since there is a danger factor and wasted energy if left on and not monitored. My fault, they describe the light correctly, I just did not read it carefully enough..

5 DAYS LATER - UPDATE
I have left it on, accidentally, one night. Probably not enough heat to start a fire, if thermostat works, but wasted energy. I can't send it back, since it was my mistake. Will modify it when I unpack my lab tools, just moved recently. As an electronic design engineer, it will be easy. Just move the "High Side" light wire from before power switch to after switch. 15 to 30 mins. Easy when I get access to required tools.

title: LOVE -- some follow up from other reviews and tips
text:
I love this rack. That is the opener to get you reading more...
This is a typical baker's rack style, and if you are not familiar with them then please follow the assembly carefully. It is very basic to assemble, especially if you are familiar with how baker racks go. Here are some tips for assembly after reading some of the reviews....

1. The black pieces are your 'locking' tabs, and have a TOP marked on them to refer to. Simple, top goes up and two pieces lock together WHEN YOU SLIDE THEM TOGETHER IN A DOWNWARD MOTION TO THE NEAREST INDENT. They will make a slight 'click' sound when they hit the indent on the pole.
2. There are double indents on the poles that are great guides for spacing of the shelves, but you can size as needed. You can even resize as needed.
3. The small opening of the holes at the end of the shelves go up, larger sized hole goes down. (I saw a lot of people review issues with sturdiness....this can solve problems as the larger end needs to go over the locking tabs).
4. This rack is VERY STURDY. I house my Cricut appliances on the wood shelf, totes of products and other heavier items on the lower shelves and would not if it weren't sturdy.
5. The parts list says it there are suppose to be 10 caps, but mine only came with 6. I used 0 of them. IMO They are for looks, and if you want to keep picking them up when they get knocked off. Does not affect integrity or functionality.
6. This rack is nicely sized for standard uses. It is not overly wide, deep, or tall so it fits nicely in my studio.
7. I have moved across the USA, and these types of racks DO disassemble and reassemble very nicely IF YOU TAKE CARE not to damage them. 7 times and going here....
Finally, if you have made it this far, and if you need a nice, sturdy rack then this is your goat. I will be ordering more for other needs. Enjoy!

title: Nice, but lower quality screws
text: Overall, I do really like this garment rack. I got this to hang clothes to dry on, and it works really well for that. I like that the rack is extremely lightweight, but also fairly sturdy. It makes it a great item if you’re looking for something of a good quality, but that you can easily move around by yourself. The bamboo wood and the white pipes look pretty together. It’s both functional and aesthetically pleasing. This rack does come disassembled (as you would expect), and while it’s fairly easy to assemble (it’s fairly straight forward and I didn’t need to intensely follow directions), some of the hardware is of poor quality. A screwdriver isn’t provided, so you’ll need that on hand. Most of the pieces assembled really well. The only issue I had was assembling the bottom part of the rack. The bottom shelf is affixed to the rack legs with 4 screws. 2 of the 4 screws (one on each side) had difficult being drilled into the rack, and because of the low quality metal of the screw, were damaged. The hardware is low quality and if you’re using decent quality tools, you’ll likely damage the screwhead because the metal is so soft. This wasn’t a huge issue. More of an annoyance. Only two on the bottom ended up damaged. Because the other screws and other hardware held up fine, it doesn’t make a huge difference. Plus, you could always just substitute a higher quality screw if you wanted. Overall, I like this rack and will find it very handy in the laundry room.

text: This heater has been in use 6+ hours each workday since its purchase, well worth the money paid.  Because the cord is slightly short due to my insistence on plugging it into the wall instead of my computer's power strip, it warms (a little too much but that's its purpose) either my left side or my feet.  Therefore my face is a bit more flushed on one side BUT I DON'T CARE!  I'm warm.  There is no heat regulator so I turn it this way and that until my overheating dissipates.  As soon as it's turned off, the chills return so there you go.  This is a new work team with a new cube containing frigid air.  No more.  My heater has fallen off my desk quite a few times, demonstrating its safety features and durability.  I love it so.

title: Might Heat a Hamster Very Well

I currently have it on my desk right in front of my keyboard to warm my hands, and the warmth goes nowhere beyond my fingertips. I highly recommend "Oscillating Space Heater, Indoor Personal Heater, Electric Ceramic Heater with Over Heat Protection, Tip Over Protection, 3 Heat Settings, Quick Heat up for Home Office" for twice the price. By contrast, it can heat an entire room very well and keep you all snuggly. I hoped to save a few bucks for a permanent heater at the office, but instead wasted $18.99 on something better suited for a hamster. Save your money and buy one that works. I just ordered a second of the one recommended above. It's THAT good.

These matched my old hangers very well, and I don't think you can tell that I've mixed and matched different brands at all. I love velvet hangers for how my shirts never slip off them onto the floor anymore, which means they definitely have some "grip" and you can't slide your clothes off as easily anymore either. Worth the trade off to me. These add a lot more usable space compared to the thicker plastic hangers and I think they look a lot nicer too. They make our "builder grade" wire shelf closets look nicer than they actually are (paired with some baskets) and I'd definitely recommend making the upgrade. Given that the last set of hangers I bought suffered a slow death over the years, I'm not ready to say that these are the best hangers yet since I haven't had them that long yet, but so far none are broken and I will be back to report if anything changes.

title: Well-made, beautiful bookcase
text: I ordered this bookcase when I decided to flip an unused formal dining room into a game room.  The room is yet to be complete, but this bookcase is my first item for the room I have put together.  The box was delivered with care and packed with extensive care.  Unlike most packed furniture, there was plenty of Styrofoam cushioning the individual parts.  And the best part was the Styrofoam itself was wrapped and sealed by plastic.  Each piece individually wrapped.  When you have built furniture, piece after furniture piece, and Styrofoam cracks, blows, clings to every part of your home, you will be truly transfixed by these Styrofoam pieces NOT exploding everywhere in your home.  Secondly, I was impressed by the weight, craftsmanship, and finishing paint of the bookshelf.  Unfortunately, there was one small chip in a noticeable front side area, but I had a palest antique white paint from another room that matched the the paint of the bookcase with a simple dot of the paint.  That was the only thing that bothered me and it wasn’t a big deal. I got the bookcase upright with the help of my grown daughter, and, once standing, it brought smiles to our faces.  The detailing and the mirrors doors on the bottom give a sophisticated glamour to our soon to be game room.  I will post pictures when the room begins to come together.  For now we are collecting all the puzzles and game boxes around the house and adding them to the bookcase!  Let family game night begin!

title: Nicely padden, large drying mats.
text: These mats are large, very nice and soft. If you're tired of leaning things on your towels, and feeling a lack of confidence in the cushioning protection or the slip resistance offered by your dish towels, these mats may put your mind at ease. I make candles, and often recycle containers for my customers to avoid wasting perfectly good glass containers with lids. I wash and clean 40 containers or more a week. One large mat went to that drying area. The other mat is a bit large for the counter next to the sink, where I dry the glass hummingbird feeders. In the summer I wash those every three or four days so there are always hummingbird feeders there drying. I allowed one side of the mat to fold over the side of the counter since it's too large for the area, and it's working great. The mat is so nicely padded the glass containers are not in danger of breaking if the fall over or something while drying for the next use.  They're perfect for my purposes and are working great.  I recommend them for anyone who hand washes dishes, or if you are into crafts and hobbies.  They are cushioned enough to allow air the circulate up into the containers as they sit upright on the pad. No leaning needed for glasses. Great product and attractive.

It is also really hard to clean out all those tiny holes. Food gets stuck in them. Overall I think I prefer the other style of masher, though if you like this style this isn't a bad masher.

title: Amazon Basics 500w space heater - Depends on your needs
text:
People who complain that it's only good for a cubicle or to warm your feet or hands at your computer likely have bigger rooms or live where the winter is much more severe than here, the S.F. Bay Area.

This winter started early here, i.e. before the solstice, and more severe than most recent winters. I scrambled to keep warm with my several space heaters, concentrating on my bedroom and kitchen. A month ago I bought a Lasko CT22445 from Costco that was feature rich (oscillating, 3 heat settings, remote, thermostat with ECO mode, tip-over protection), bought another 2 weeks later. I eventually decided to return them because I couldn't abide the smell, and did 2 days ago. I shopped space heaters online and decided on this very modest "500w" offering which looks like a toy. My bedroom is not quite 10' x 10' plus a couple closets. I have two overhead lights, one being a 250w heat lamp pointed at the floor. I only turn that on when it's too cool/cold for me. That heat lamp does boost the warmth, but very slowly. It takes a couple hours to boost it 5F. That definitely helps, but when it is really cold it's not enough. Most all of the space heaters nowadays have top heat setting of 1500w (although I imagine they all measure less than that), and a low setting of 900w. Try finding a space heater with 3 heat settings or one with a low at ~500w! I wasn't able to find more than one or two at Amazon, and the reviews scared me away. The Lasko heaters I returned did have 3 settings, but the lowest measured around 750w, which is more than I want for my bedroom (but usable). This Amazon Basics 500w space heater measures 475w on my Kasa KP115 energy monitoring smart plug, less than the advertised 500w, but I'm OK with that. Added to my heat lamp, the room warms 3x as fast as with the heat lamp alone. I can manage with that.

This thing does have a smell, but not annoying like those Lasko heaters I returned, at least it hasn't bothered me so far (couple days, modest use) and I assume that the smell will abate some. The noise? Well, it is more than I anticipated, but I'm pretty used to it already.

This heater is minimal in most every way but does have the tip-over safety feature. It's overpriced for what you get at ~$24, but it is a fit for my usage. I have it on a plate on the floor.

title: Fantastic value for cast iron
text:
I'm giving 4 stars, but the lack of a single star is probably my own fault/problem.

After doing some research, I felt $80 was a terrific price for a 5-piece cast iron set of cookware (and I still do), so I ordered this set.

I can't begin to describe how impressed I was with the shipping packaging. It came in a large cardboard box that was the perfect size to contain all the individual boxes that had the plastic wrapped piece of cookware inside each one. There was absolutely no chance of any piece being damaged while shipping unless the whole thing fell out of the shipping truck and was then hit by another shipping truck. Awe-struck impressed.

Every piece seems to be well made. They aren't too thin, although the handles are perhaps a bit small.

It also comes with instructions on how to use, clean, and care for this product, which based on my knowledge of cooking with cast iron, seems to be in-line.

My only complaint was that the cast iron didn't perform as expected. Despite the instructions stating that it was pre-seasoned, I had a real problem with sticking and cleaning this product. However, I am not convinced yet that this is a problem with the product and not some self-imposed problem that I simply haven't caught up with the learning curve of how to cook with and clean cast-iron.

title: Don't ignore the reviews saying this is a very deep chair!
text:
I ordered the chair in dark grey leather and I'm glad I measured first. I had originally ordered 2 until I saw that they were so huge they would be pushed up against each other in my small space, so I canceled one. It's a very large chair - not tall, low back, but very wide and very deep. For me (5'5" woman) I can't put my feet on the floor and reach the back of the chair. I can stuff pillows behind me or I can scoot back and pull my legs up and kind of lay back or curl sideways in the chair.
It's a bit firmer than I had expected but not at all uncomfortable and I already think it feels a bit less stiff than it did the day I got it.
The color is definitely more of a grayish brown than a gray, like other reviews have mentioned.
Seems to be really good quality and the assembly took me about 30 minutes by myself after entryway delivery, and 20 of those 30 minutes was getting the box and thin foam liner off the chair and out of the way so I could attach the legs. The bottom liner underneath the chair unzips and the legs were inside in a pouch tied with a ribbon and included the legs, 8 screws, 8 washers and a small hex wrench. I gave up on the hex wrench after one leg (I have pain in my hands) and put a matching hex bit in my cordless drill instead to finish up.
There was off-gassing (intense new furniture smell) of the new chair that lasted about 2 days; unfortunately, it was a cold snap so I couldn't open the windows but either it finally aired out or I got used to it. I'm sensitive to strong smells but I got through it.
Both the seat cushion and the back cushion are removable, they can be rotated but not flipped.
I'd say it's definitely more of a lounging chair than a sitting chair, unless you're 6'5" or want to work on your core muscles by not using the backrest. I think pairing it with an ottoman would make a perfect lounging chair so that's what I intend to do when I find an affordable one that matches.

title: Does the job!
text:
Like many, I now work from home more often than not. To my immediate left is a large sliding glass door that lets cold air spill in from outside. Even with slippers and pajama pants, my feet are still freezing while the rest of me is relatively comfortable.

In comes this little heater! It keeps my feet toasty warm all while radiating heat under my desk which rises up around the edges to keep my whole body warm. The 500watt draw is great so your electric bill won't really feel it either. As for noise, it's quiet with a slight "white noise" effect. With music or TV, it's not noticeable. It works perfect.

To place it, I cut a piece of polyurethane board, punched some holes in it, and strapped it to the support bar under my desk. At first there was the worry that the heat might melt the board, but as one can see directly under the heater the temperature is only 84°F (28°C). The heater puts out heat at about190° - 200°F (90° - 93°C) give or take a few degrees. This unit is not capable of heating an entire room, but in a bathroom, or small bedroom it'll definitely take the chill out of the air.

Highly recommend!

title: It works but...
text: This is not the fanciest looking vacuum sealer. But it has a great simplicity that makes it quite functional. It has two settings. One for jarring and the other for bagging. The settings are labeled moist and dry. They are easily toggled between using a single press button. The instructions say that when using the dry setting all you need to press is the vacuum button and that it will vacuum and seal and then turn off. After running an entire slew of tests, I can say that this is definitively not the case. Either all don't, or mine is broken. The vac/seal button only vacuums and doesn't seal. I have to press the stop button followed very quickly by the seal button or else too much air get back inside. It's definitely not ideal. If you can find machine that does both automatically, I'd recommend buying it. This is just a hassle. However, if you're into jarring things, this sealer works great for that.

In terms of comfort, I'd say it's right in the middle, not too plush, though not too firm, either -- which is what I like since everyone in the house seems to have different preferences. The color is nice and goes well with our neutral color scheme. The fabric isn't the softest, though it's very durable, easy to clean/care for, and even held up to the occasional scratch from our cats before they learned it wasn't a new scratch post. It did require some very minimal assembly, which honestly took less than 5 min. The swivel and reclining features work very well, have been using this couch for several weeks now and haven't had any issues, whatsoever. It is mid-sized, compared to other recliners, though my husband is 6'5" and he finds it to be very comfortable, not too small. Overall an excellent product for a decent value, I would definitely recommend this recliner!

text:
After buying some extra forks to flesh out my 30 yr old flatware, I found myself impressed enough to buy 3 four place settings making service for 12 in the Scalloped Edge. In addition to just plain looking nice, the utensils were well balanced, comfortable in the hand, and had no rough edges. They are certainly heavy and rugged enough (spoons pass the ice cream test with no bending). A good buy, I thought, for not much money.
Why three stars? Well, four of the twelve knives keep tarnishing along the serrations, and the whole point of buying STAINLESS steel is so they DON'T tarnish. I would have given this product a full 5 stars if it weren't for the corrosion from the first machine washing. I wash the knives by hand now. There are no issues with any of the other utensils.

title: Good on paper
text:
Looks great on paper, unfortunately lots not working in practice:

* Biggest problem: Adjustable lumbar support doesn't stay put. I have to raise it up to its highest setting every hour because apparently the weight of my back on it is enough to push it back down on its own. Needs a lock or something because it is *way* too easy to push down.
* At their lowest setting, the armrests are different heights, which creates tension in one arm but not the other. Raising the lower one up one notch gets them closer, so that's what I use, but it's still annoying.
* Armrests don't move in towards the body enough for me, leaving my elbows way out wide. Probably makes the chair great for wider bodies, though.
* Armrest material is super hard and uncomfortable.
* Mesh seat is rough and uncomfortable when wearing shorts. I explicitly wanted the mesh back for cooling but didn't think about the seat, which now I know would be better as a traditional padded seat.
* Seat forward/backward setting is not really usable outside the default furthest back setting. At any other setting it's loose and moves a bit if you shift your body weight in the seat. Also if you set it forward there's not much seat left in the back so you end up sitting on the hard edge of the seat instead of the springy mesh center part.
* I couldn't find a maximum tilt angle setting. The only one I found locks the seat at the given angle. I'd prefer a setting that allows you to recline as much as you want *up to* a given angle.
* Head rest is super far back and only tilts up/down so I rarely ever use it.

Unfortunately pickings are slim right now so I haven't returned it yet.

AmazonBasics Step Stool - 2-Step, Sturdy Steel and Wide Pedal, 200-Pound Capacity, White

I really like this step ladder. It's very well constructed and has a nice heavy feel to it. It’s still light enough that it’s easy for anyone to pick up and move around but sturdy enough to feel safe using. Another nice touch is the padding around the top. Not only does it make it easy to grip but it also stops any damage if you need to lean the stool against the wall.

When it’s folded up it’s easy to tuck away and store. So this is one of those things that are just essential in any house. I feel like this will hold up well over time too.

The only difference between this step stool and the other I have is that there isn’t a pull lock that keeps it either folded or extended out. I haven’t run into any issues due to that but it’s just something I noticed when I went to fold it back up.

Overall this is another well-made product for the AmazonBasics line. It’s reasonably priced as well. The other stool I own is a bit more expensive and honestly, there’s no reason I wouldn’t have bought this if it was available at the time. I think this is a good buy personally.

Not good, but nothing I can do about it.

UPDATE:
I started using it under the desk instead of on top, and it really warms that space up well. Sometimes I get a little too warm. Pretty good for a small, inexpensive heater.

When I first got it and plugged it in, I was shocked at the hot blast of air that came out. But, that was the last time that happened. title: Disgrace to the Amazon Basic brand
text: Historically I've bought from Amazon basics because they usually make a product simple but with better quality and at a better design than anything else in a similar price point. This couldn't be farther from the truth with this particular product. This desk is made very very poorly. I used to assemble furniture for a display in stores so I know what I'm talking about. This desk doesn't come with any washers or lock rings so even once it's assembled it's destined to get loose and wobbly. The laminate cardboard composite is poorly fabricated. Why simulate carbon fiber if you're going to skimp on the glue to put it down. Also if you're going to put black laminate on particle board you should at least dye the particle board black. The laminate on my desk is already peeling off without any rough handling and I've owned less than a week. People spend so much money on their gaming rigs why would we want crappy design. And the sad part is it's not even worth returning cuz I had to dismantle the box completely to get all the pieces out. It also has fabrication holes for hardware I didn't receive. My advice is to buy any other gaming desk except for the one that Amazon makes itself. This one purchase makes me leery of the entire Amazon basics line which I was a very loyal customer of previously. Shame on you Amazon

title: Versatile gadget
text:
This gadget works really well for vacuum sealing moderate amounts of food. I think if you regularly package large amounts you'd want to get a more automated machine, but if you're in a small household this could be great. I don't need to process a ton of food so it's almost perfect so far.

The plastic roll inside the sealer is loose and can slide back and forth so it's possible for it to be too far to one side and not seal well. It's possible to seal the first edge of your bag then cut the seal you made right back off again because of how the blade is oriented. The buttons aren't labeled so it's easy to press the wrong one and seal the bag shut without sucking the air out first (I'm making labels). If you cut the bag too short you won't be able to use it at all. It takes a lot of pressure to get the lid to snap down, and sometimes by the time I've gotten it snapped in the baggie has fallen out. The sealer has several quirks that you have to learn but once you get it down you're golden. I haven't used a more expensive one but I've seen videos, and the trade-off with this device does seem to be losing some simplicity for lower cost. But that's my middle name. The quirks are fine for me. The main annoyances I have are that there's no vacuum only button (that's not great for zipper baggies or jars) and the canister tube attachment doesn't work unless you have or buy more accessories. But I'm glad that the set works with attachment tubes because it makes it way more versatile.

I usually avoid plastic baggies but I have had a lot of food loss due to freezer damage so I'm making some exceptions. It's been a really straightforward process and the food looks great so far.

title: Efficient Heating and Adjustable Settings Make the Amazon Basics Ceramic Personal Heater a Great Buy
text:
I recently purchased the Amazon Basics 1500W Ceramic Personal Heater with Adjustable Thermostat for my garage and found it to be an efficient heating solution. The heater is designed to adjust to different temperature needs with two adjustable settings, one for heat and one for output. It's easy to use and has two legs that provide stability.

Although the heater is priced higher than when I bought it, I still believe it's worth the investment. It's a versatile product that can be used in many settings, such as garages, offices, and homes.

One thing I would suggest is to switch the two-prong plug to a three-prong for safety purposes. I noticed that some other Amazon reviewers shared the same concern about the product possibly sparking.

Despite this issue, the Amazon Basics Ceramic Personal Heater offers a lot of benefits. It's compact, powerful, and easy to use. The adjustable thermostat is a great feature, and the heater has a sleek design that blends well in any room. If you're looking for an efficient and versatile heating solution, I would recommend giving this product a try.

title: Updated after 6 months of use.
text:
I was a bit leary of leaving a space heater running in my bathroom constantly. I have no central heating in my home so I needed something to keep the bathroom warm.

So far this heater is working great. I've checked all around the unit for overheating or melting of plastic after days of continuous use and there has been no issues with the unit, the cord or the outlet. All are cool to the touch except the grate in front where the heat blows out.

If you so much as slightly tilt it, it turns off. It also turns off when the room, or the unit reaches a certain temperature. Not sure which, but it doesn't run continuously once the room is warm.

title: Good for small spaces, easy to assemble
text:
Ive had this sofa for about a year and a half so decided its time to write my review.

Part of buying a sofa online as a person who lives alone was me panicking about them not delivering the sofa actually into my apartment and finding it outside on the ground with me having to find a way to haul it inside. So I liked that they had the option to pay an extra 20 dollars to have it delivered into your room of choice. It came in one big box, however the delivery guys didnt open it up for me and take the box away (no big deal though). All you have to do is get the legs that are in a zipper compartment on the bottom and screw them in and the sofa is assembled.

This sofa was perfect for my needs initially as I have a pretty small living room and needed something small but not so small that it looks like miniature or kid furniture. Im 5'2 but ive had friends who are 6' tall sit on it and not feel like it's too small or uncomfortable.

I bought the linen color and to me its a true linen color in natural lighting. When you look at it up close you can see fine threads of very light beige HOWEVER, there are times at night when the lighting in my room makes it appear a yellowish color (not very flattering). Ive asked people what color it appears to them and they've all said a very light grey.

So far I havent had any issues with pilling, stains or seams coming apart. In fact, I once got some pizza sauce on it and it came right out. It seems to repel stains pretty well (at least small ones, I havent spilled anything major or in a large surface area).

My biggest gripe with this couch is that you can not flip over the cushions like you normally would with other couches when it starts to get flat and you want to even out the wear and tear. I'm afraid to wash the covers as well as i think they'd come apart. The back of the couch cushions and seats are a different gray material. I wish they would resolve this or at least have the manufacturer offer to sell replacement cushions and covers.

I have just recently had to buy some cushion support panels as the springs are starting to get squeaky and the cushions are losing their fullness. The legs are still okay. I bought it when it was about 700, but above that price point I would be looking for something else. At this moment it fits my needs but when it comes time to replace I wont be looking at this option.

Now, I can't compare it to the pricier pieces as others have done, but I am satisfied overall with the quality of this dutch oven. Mine arrived safely with no damage or chips (they are very securely packaged in a molded block of Styrofoam), and has held up to daily use these past few weeks, still looking like new.

It's very versatile - I've used it in the oven to bake bread, deep fried in it, browned meats, and made soups. I love how it cooks evenly and holds the heat. I've had no trouble with clean up, nothing that required more than the scrubby back of my dish sponge and a little elbow grease after a soak. I've cooked chili and some other tomato heavy dishes with zero staining.

Though I usually tend to go for a more "serious" anesthetic in my home, I chose the pink version on a whim and I'm glad I did! It's super cute and makes me happy whenever I look at it.

All in all, I'm happy with my purchase and would definitely recommend it to friends or family.

title: wants to hold onto stains but cooks so well
text:
The first thing I used this stockpot for was roast in the oven. It's a tall stock pot so you will probably have to remove one rack in the oven, then place this on the lowest rack, but I didn't find that affected the cooking any.

I was able to achieve a moist, tender roast that wasn't overcooked in this pot, something I was never able to do with the cast iron I've used for years. The meat seared well on the stove top, then it cooked evenly with the vegetables once in the oven, with the lid keeping moisture in. Again, it is a little tall for a dutch oven, but that won't keep me from using it again. I'd given up making roast until I decided to test this out, and I was so pleased at how it turned out I'll definitely be making roasts again once the weather cools down.

We've also used this for soups a few times and it's been perfectly fine, both with making a soup from scratch (browning meat and vegetables first, then adding stock, spices, etc.) and just for warming up leftovers.

My only complaint is that the interior wants to hold on to every little thing that gets inside the pot. The exterior after several washings remains shiny and looks good, but the interior has spots from the meat browning that just won't go away. I've used the dishwasher to clean the pot, hand washed with a plastic scrubby, soaked it in soapy water, and there are small areas that will remain brown forever, I guess.

That's my only complaint. I'm sure I'll be using this pot for years to come.

title: A Set of Five Small Storage Boxes
text:
First of all, don't be fooled by "10-piece set." They're counting the lids as separate pieces. It's really a five-piece set, one larger box (with lide), two smaller one, and two small ones.

They click closed and seal nicely, and nope, didn't have any leaks. The lids have a nice, set-in flexible gasket, so one you lock the lid to the box, you do get a nice, tight seal. You do, however, have to ensure that you really are cleaning that gasket area, so if you don't have one already, you'll need to invest in a nice kitchen brush.

They are indeed dishwasher-safe.

My only real complaint about this set is that the boxes aren't bigger. Increase the size of each box by about 50%, and we'd be in a useful range. With the smallest of the boxes holding about a 1/4 of an average can of soup, what exactly are they useful for? The largest one is a decent size for small storage, but is still too small to pack a lunch into.

Price: This set is currently listed as unavailable, so I can't cite a current price. I would think this set should come in somewhere between $12 and $15. Any more than that and you're paying too much.

Bottom Line: this is a nice little set of sealable storage boxes. They work exactly as advertised. They're only real drawback is that they all need to be bigger.

title: Awesome bakers rack!
text:
I live alone in a studio with a half wall in the kitchen. There's no pantry, very little counter space and the cabinets don't hold much. I was trying to the best with the cabinets and also putting things on top of the refrigerator which I really didn't like doing because it just looked messy. I thought this was the perfect solution to all my kitchen problems and it most certainly is. I actually think it looks really cute in my kitchen and it's really opened up the functionality for a small space! My kitchen kind of feels like a little cafe kitchen or little restaurant kitchen now and I'm excited to cook again. This rack completely freed all my counters which not only made the kitchen appear bigger but now I have so much more prep area for cooking and doing dishes since I don't have a dishwasher. It looks clean and uncluttered but everything I need and want in the kitchen is at my fingertips.

About the assembly and obvious damage...I've put these racks together before which made me a little more confident to go ahead and put it together and see how it turned out. The rack that is damaged thankfully still lays flat so the bend is not in the wrong direction and really didn't have any bad effects for it's purpose. Things are just going to go on top of it and cover it anyway. I can't even see it now that's loaded up with things so I don't care.

The black clips are actually very easy to work with, they just sometimes appear to be too small but they really aren't. Just put them about a 1/4" above the line you want it to go on, squeeze them together as you slide them down and they'll lock onto that line and you will hear a fairly loud clicking sound. Once you have all in place and you slide the rack over the top of them you'll want to have a wood mallet or something to hit the corners of the rack with until it's sitting straight and securely over the black clasps. I didn't have a wood mallet so I just used a regular hammer with a folded up towel so I didn't damage it. My posts were wonky looking too but I knew the racks would straighten it all up. So despite the damage mine came out great. Also no issues with the wood cutting board, it looks nice and durable.

Overall you can't beat this rack for the price and the function! Take your time putting it together and don't panic if you have some minor damage, it might turn out just fine after all. I'm trying to think of where I can put a second one of these in my apartment lol. I highly recommend it! Also I did order it when it said it was unavailable and I received it three days later so it was delivered really fast.

title: Good budget sealer.  Decent value.
text:
This AmazonBasics food sealing unit works as advertised although I have found it to be slower than my older model Food Saver. The difference isn't huge but if you plan to seal a lot of items, the extra time this weaker unit will take will add up. (So far, I have only used it three times and on only several items each session.) The bags included are excellent and work perfectly and not only that, my Food Saver bags also work in this Amazon unit. The Amazon unit feels much lighter than the Food Saver although it seems to operate as intended and nothing appears to be easily breakable.

This sealer is smaller overall (than the Food Saver) and easily stores in a drawer in my kitchen. The unit includes the hose attachment and instruction manual, which is generally good; the unit is very easy to operate once you understand what the buttons and operations are such as the differences between wet/dry and bagging vs. jars. You can buy jars for this kind of machine and I have not done so, only the roll of bags so I cannot comment on how well it seals jars.

Overall, this works well and represents a good value for a basic but complete setup to get started. If you've considered learning canning, you might add to your repertoire with a food sealing system such as this. I prefer my Food Saver sealer because it's faster, produces a stronger suction, and is heavier and seems better built. However, this one does the job.

title: Stylish and modern, comfortable, and reasonably priced for an upholstered swivel.
text:
This is a nice office chair.

No assembly required, the color is a light gray polyester with a wool or felt look accented with a base of four angled legs to a swiveling center post. There is no height adjustment but I find the seat is at a good height for me and the desk it is sitting in front of. I am 6'2" with long arms. The arm rests are slightly sloped and are not wide; they aren't ideal for resting my elbows but my arms rest nicely. The seat is a comfortable length and while the cushion isn't deep, it's firm enough that I don't feel any of the hardware through my backside. I wish the seat had just a touch more padding. The seat cushion has piping around the top corner edge -- subtle and classy as well as adds strength to a seam that will likely get the most stress and friction.

Stitching is tight and consistent. I found no flaws either on the top or on the underside. The fabric texture and weave is consistent with zero slubbing or loose threads, flaws, or crooked alignment. My chair has a little bit of excess fabric on the left arm so it's not quite as tight facing the front.

The legs are solid metal and give the chair a contemporary or mid century look. No feet. The chair is evenly balanced and I detect no lean at any point of the swivel turn, right or left. Action is smooth. The chair does not lean back but the back is angled slightly for comfort.

Simple, well designed, and appears to be a good quality chair that will hopefully last a while. I have mine in front of my second desk (my desks are set up in an L configuration) but this chair could be right at home in many different settings. It's neutral but stylish, reasonably comfortable, and the price is about what you might expect for a better-than-average upholstered swivel chair.

While the length is fine for my purposes, I should note that it's not particularly wide. I tested the rack with all the coats I have in my closet along with a hanging canvas shoe rack. The rack was perfectly capable of the weight but it tipped easily and was harder to move around without it tipping. If you're thinking of ordering this rack for commercial use, you might want to consider a wider model. This is a great size for a walk-in closet.

Assembly is quick and easy and the snap buttons work flawlessly. The finish looks great.

title: Nightmare - But Little One Loves It
text: This bed was a complete fiasco, but it turned out OK only because it’s new owner loves it. But she’s four and didn’t have to suffer through the process. Depends on if you want to spend HOURS on the phone and WEEKS trying to get parts that are not damaged. This entire bed had to be reshipped THREE times. Even then, there were important pieces that show which had scrapes and dents. The worst scrapes were on each and every headboard in the same spot. The dents were on the guard rails and headboard. Amazon customer service was excellent, especially when I went up to the supervisor level. Because of the holidays and arriving company, and because we had already taken down the toddler bed to make room for this (and it was weeks, as each shipment took at least 5-6 days), we settled for the best parts out of three beds and a price adjustment. Amazon actually removed it from availability at one point due to the issues. I had crib rail covers that were like new and had the idea to use them on three sides to cover some of the damage. It also makes it a bit cozier. Assembly wasn’t difficult, but it’s important to lay out all pieces before you start. Many are almost identical but wouldn’t work if you mixed them up. I used removable stickers to mark each piece by the corresponding letter in the instructions. However... the instructions are inaccurate in several spots, so you have to pay attention and use common sense. Overall, the bed seems sturdy and has been the perfect height for tucking in at night. I plan to check and tighten all of the screws again soon. There’s about 38.5” under it, which is plenty of room for a short dresser or for kids to play. We’re using the crib mattress underneath for a reading spot. Since this picture, we added a strand of white led lights (made for a Christmas tree) and a clip on light for reading. I wouldn’t buy it again and go through the huge hassle, but I’m glad she loves it. Thanks again to Amazon for great service. I did suggest to the supervisor that Amazon be more selective about the items they identify as “AmazonBasics”. Even if they don’t mean to, it conveys a certain expectation that, while not fancy, the product is reliable and a good value. I would not describe this bed that way due to the obvious problems with quality control.

title: Comparable in size and utility to the Wilton set. I still prefer the Wilton but this works
text:
Received and use these today. The basics. They are all slightly larger and have taller sides than the similar Wilton 3 pack of baking sheets. They are easy to clean and work well baking cookies. Absolutely no stick even with very low butter/fat content cookies. One thing I did notice is that where the sheet metal is rolled over on the edge of just one of the three trays (the smallest), the metal is SHARP. The other two sheets do not have this problem, but I'd urge buyers to be careful. I happen to grab it in exactly the spot where the sheet is notched before it is rolled over and I could feel it pressing into my finger before I moved my fingers, but if you hand wash --like I did and move your fingers fast -- it could easily cut your finger. This clearly was NOT a problem with the other two, so I'm not sure that all buyers would find this with any or all of their sheets.

Other than that one problem they cooked and handled well and were extremely easy to clean with a soft sponge, no scrubbing required. As always these should be used with silicone spatulas and tools to prevent scratching and extend the life of the product.

Overall I still slightly prefer the Wilton's (I have the comparable 3 piece Wilson set), but I assume this cost less and for that you get pretty much the same thing.

There are a lot of minor imperfections...a slightly uneven finish here, a tiny dent or ding there...holes drilled where there's no logical reason for there to be holes, like they drilled the wrong side during manufacturing and rather than scrap the whole piece, they just flipped it over and drilled the other side too. I almost think because of the price(significantly lower than in the Ashley store) and these minor defects, that they are factory "seconds" not quite good enough to be sold at full price, but not bad enough to end up in the scrap bin. BUT, unless you are the one who assembles these chairs or are closely inspecting them LOOKING for defects, you won't even notice these small flaws.  As far as assembly, super easy. Standard Ashley Furniture...bolts with 2 washers, tighten with an allen wrench. Each chair will take less than 10 minutes. If you're not a perfectionist and you happen to catch these at a great price like I did, $89/pair(they went up to $130/pair the day after I ordered them!) then go for it.

title: Good electric steamer, has good amount of space for steaming, easy to use and clean.
text:
I've never used an electric steamer with plastic parts before, used to using a stainless steel pot with a steaming section on top of it so something like this is new to me. This looks like a simple product that is easy to use. The instructions are easy to understand but you should also play with the selections to get an idea of how this steamer works.

There are three tiers, with a good amount of space and they come in two pieces each. There's also a window to show how much water you have left in the steamer when it's in use, a nice feature to have. I have used this to steam veggies like broccoli, carrots and corn and it works very well. I have also used it to steam buns and rice cakes. A signal alarm goes off when it's done steaming, another good feature.

My counters have cabinets above but I am still able to use all three tiers since there is enough space closer to the edge where the cabinets won't get in the way. I like how a rice bowl is included, though I have stopped eating rice as a staple, this will come in to use in case I need it but then again, I do have a rice cooker for that, maybe it'll save me some time if I'm steaming veggies and making a small serving of rice at the same time.

This full steamer, when stacked together, is very lightweight. It is easy to clean by washing the steaming baskets with soap and water and wiping down the inside of the housing base since it cannot be submerged in water. The only items that are dish washer safe is the rice bowl and drip tray.

Pros:
Easy to use and clean
3 Tiers offers lots of space for steaming
Electric
Window for water level
Alarm when steaming is complete

Cons:
None

Overall, I found this steamer to be easy to use and clean, is lightweight, the three tiers offer lots of space for steaming food and this is electric too. It's another alternative to having a steaming pot set that's used on the stove. Everyone does have their preferences, and I would say that I'm used to steaming on a stove so this electric steamer would be my second go to.

title: Makes Ikea Assembly Look Like an Encyclopedia
text:
The instructions were SO bad, I was cursing like a sailor, froth and spittle gathering on my lips, being expelled in assorted directions, as I threw cardboard, styrofoam and plastic bags anywhere but near me. Oh. My. G*d. The pictogram had items labeled with letters. TOO BAD THERE WERE NO MATCHING LETTERS ON THE ASSORTED PARTS. I had to take it apart and start over at least twice! More cursing and frothing. Styrofoam bits EVERYWHERE (why are you still using styrofoam for packing materials!? It's 2020 FTLoG!). The pictograms were completely useless, you may have left them off. I recommend that in the future. The pamphlet can be repurposed for bird cages, cat boxes, or toilet paper.

That said--once I FINALLY got it put together, it not only looks fantastic, it holds a lot of my stuff (see above). It also lets light from the window pass through the bars. The bookcase I had there before blocked the light and made the room darker. This was everything I wanted a baker's rack to be--and looked for for months, both new and used--and I'm so glad I purchased this one, even if the directions were a nightmare. Persevere, it's worth it in the end. Use your own best judgment, not the "instructions." Exhale.

Regardless of the looks, it just works really well. It heats up frothed milk/half & half and makes a lovely thick foam and warms it so that it doesn't immediately absorb into the espresso. Works every time too. Clean up is the same as on any of these (expect some residue from the sugars in the milk/cream, requires you to wipe it down to remove it). For $27 shipped brand new this thing does the same thing as the more expensive units. The base is nice. It's stable. The frother doesn't feel delicate, it's a good robust thick piece of equipment and the buttons feel good with a good snap to them. The device just plain works really well. Awesome froth for your drinks!

The workspace is the same, with a removable wooden slab on top. My slab arrived a little warped, but I was able to make a solid sturdy surface by adding a small shim under one corner. It works great for kneading, rolling and forming dough and mixing ingredients. The storage shelving is adequate for most of my baking equipment (pans, bowl, scale, baking stones, utensils, baking mats, etc.). The bottom of each leg has a rubber foot that screws into the bottom of the tub, allowing for unscrewing as needed to stabilize the rack on slightly uneven surfaces. I am pleased with the efficiency of size and design, and extra workspace it provides. A very functional rack at a very reasonable price.

title: Two months with this pan, and I love it!
text:
After discarding all our old cookware after buying an induction-top range, I wanted a nice, induction-friendly stainless frypan to compliment our T-Fal non-stick sauté pan. This pan was a nicely priced option with some great reviews, so I thought I'd give it a try.

If you're asking yourself, "Why two pans?" I'll give you three reasons why. The first is non-stick pans wear out and wear out really quickly if you cook over high heat, like when you sear meat. This pan doesn't deteriorate when you heat it on high and will last a lifetime. Non-stick pans also don't work well for recipes where a sauté is deglazed into a sauce. Finally, as non-stick surfaces wear out, they deposit chemicals in the food you cook on them, and that bugs me.

So I have this non-stick frypan, and I am very happy with it. It has a nice heft to it, heats evenly, does a great job of everything from searing to sautéing, and is genuinely easy to clean. We do a lot of home cooking here and, two months in, it still looks like new.

I thought I'd show you how easily this pan cleans up. The first picture I took was after a dinner where I sautéd all the vegetables for a veggie-heavy, one-pan zucchini-tomato-chickpea curry, then scooped up the leftovers and used a spatula to get the last of the sauce into two leftover storage containers. If you take a look at the picture, the pan was pretty clean even before it hit the sink. The second picture was taken a couple of minutes later after a drip of Dawn dish soap, some water, and few really quick swishes with a scrub brush cleaned it out, and this is what it looked like. No elbow grease was required. It shines!

Here's one more cool thing about this pan: The lid for our 10-inch T-Fal E93897 non-stick pan is a great fit for this one, too. Having a well-fitting led comes in really handy so, if you're looking for that perfect pair of 10-inch standard and non-stick pans, this and the T-Fal might just be your perfect set.

Pros:
* Induction friendly.
* Cooks evenly at every temperature.
* No problems with warping.
* Really great pan for not a lot of money.
* Has been super easy to keep clean.
* Mates well with the lid for T-Fal's 10-inch non-stick sauté pan, E93897.

Cons:
* I couldn't think of any!

title: "The same as..."
text:
These AmazonBasics Silicone Baking Mats are nearly the exact equivalent of the more expensive French brand without the logo or color scheme. They function exactly the same! So if you are making candy with hot (or warm) sugar solutions, like maybe nut brittles, you know how essential this type of non-stick, heat resistant surface is. Pour the hot brittle (or caramel) onto the mat, let it cool, and it peels off easily. While I prefer using disposable parchment paper for much of my flour based baking, including cookies, biscuits, and rolls, silicone mats--unlike paper- provide the same type of non-stick surface and can withstand higher oven temps (up to 480F according to the product information) without any damage.

For the price, and the value 3-pack for these Silicone Baking Mats, AmazonBasics has a winner. Even if you do not make candy on a regular basis, you may find yourself wanting to try a quick and easy batch of peanut brittle just to see how much you have been missing!
