title: Only 7.5 cup capacity
text:
One month update: this thing is a mess.

Even when you stick to the fill limit of the coffee basket, it overflows, plugging the valve and leaving grounds into the filter holder and the coffee carafe itself - every, flipping, morning, I have to clean it.

Yes, starting with a freshly cleaned filter. Yes, I do use coffee specifically ground for a filter machine.

Also the warming element cooks the coffee, turns it into a gas station bitter swill in no time flat.

I wish I had returned it with it the first month.

Initial review: The basket has a maximum capacity of 76g (2.7oz) coffee grounds before it overflows and you have to clean up grounds from everywhere inside.
Using the Peet’s coffee recipe ratio of 1g of coffee per 16g of water, this coffeemaker can only handle 1.2l / 8.5 cups of water. And since you lose about a cup of water to evaporation and absorption into the grounds, this is really only a 7.5 cup maker. NOT 12 cups. Unless maybe you are making weak American style coffee.

text: My husband and I decided to purchase these chairs  online, although we felt a little uneasy doing so.  We had no idea if they would be as good looking as they were pictured on Amazon.com.  We also were afraid they might get damaged during the shipping process.  First, let me say that the chairs arrived quickly, sooner than expected.  They were left on my front porch, but I was able to lift and carry them inside.  I excitingly opened the first package (I ordered 3 pkgs.) and lifted the chair seat out.  How beautiful!  The material is like a thick textured brocade with a deep brown/burgundy and tan/cream color paisley pattern.  So much prettier in person than in the photos online! title: You have to cure these cast iron pots & pans...
text: You have to cure these cast iron pots and pans in the oven every once in awhile-depending on how much you use them, or they will rust.  To cure them, lightly coat the cast iron pot or pan all over- inside and out with cooking oil (do not heavily coat them so that the oil is sticky on the fingers-just enough so that the pots & pans have a dull shine. Preheat your oven to 350 degrees. Place your oiled cast iron pot or pan in the oven for approximately one hour to cure it. Remove the cast iron pot or pan from the oven, and allow it to completely cool. Don't forget to use a pot holder so you don't burn your hands.  Wipe any excess oil from the cast iron pot or pan, and store it away until you are ready to use it.  Cure the cast iron pot or pan again, when you see rust starting to form on them. Cast iron pots and pans are the best pots and pans to cook with, and will last for decades.  However, you do have to cure them every once in awhile-depending on how much you use them.  And, after each time you wash the cast iron pot or pan, you can lightly rub cooking oil on them as needed-but I just wait until I see a little rust or they start to look really dull, then I just cure them again.

title: Black Lint Everywhere- These Will Cover You, Your Clothes, and Your Closet in Black Lint Residue
text:
Very rarely have I been so annoyed with a product that I wrote a negative review. Of the many Amazon reviews I’ve written, offhand I can’t think of any that I gave low scores to because I’m almost always thrilled with products I get from Amazon. The Amazon branded basic products have always been great for me.

These hangers have inspired a review. First, they get five stars for price and durability. They get negative stars, if that was an option, for the black, velvet lint that they are absolutely covered in. I ordered several hundred hangers, ecstatic that they were 60 cents cheaper per hanger than the name brand at the store that I had just purchased a box of. I read the reviews where I noticed some people had discussed a lint issue, but I had hoped this was an isolated issue. No, apparently this is a nearly universal issue. The attached picture is what my pants looked like after spending an hour working with these hangers- the bottom left leg of the pant leg (the part that was against the floor while I was getting covered in lint) is flipped over so you can see that my pants were actually pink before being totally covered in black link.

I ordered half the amount I needed in one order, which arrived today, and unfortunately, the other half won’t get to my house until Friday. Had I known the volume of work that would be required and the massive mess it would make I would have just paid for the name brand version. The first box I opened I noticed a bit of lint in the bag holding the hangers, so since I have a lot of light colored, delicate clothing, I figured I would test it out first by running a white cloth over it. The cloth, after being brushed along the hanger, was covered in black lint. Had I just put a white shirt on the hanger, it would have been completely covered in dark lint and likely been ruined. Take into account the fact that my closet has rows, so every time I pulled a shirt off of a top row hanger, the entire bottom row would have been dusted with lint as well.

So, since I was feeling cheap, I decided that I could fix the mess. I gathered a few white, older hand towels that had been washed enough so that they didn’t rub off any white fuzzies onto the black velvet and I basically scrubbed each hanger with a dry towel. If I ever finish cleaning the few hundred hangers I am stuck with, I will probably run a damp cloth over them to get any remaining residue. At this point I have finished rubbing off the majority of the lint residue from about 250 hangers. It takes about 10-15 minutes to do each box of 50, you get lint all over your floor, and anything that happens to be nearby. I had a pale, pink silk shirt that I had laid out to hang up and by the time I was done scrubbing my hangers, the shirt was covered in black lint too, despite the fact that it was 5 feet away from me and about 2 feet over my head from the floor where I was sitting. On a good note, I just shook the shirt and most of the lint fell off, so at least it isn’t overly sticky or static. I am covered from head to toe in black lint, my skin looks like I spent the day in a coal mine, and my clothes look like I rolled around in ashes. Fortunately, the lint doesn’t itch, so it could be far worse.

On a positive note, the hangers are strong. Despite my vigorous rubbing, only one of them broke, so at least I know once they are actually clean they might be helpful to have. If someone would fix the finishing process of these, they would be perfect. For now though, they are an absolute giant mess that will destroy your clothing if you don’t spend quite a bit of time cleaning each individual hanger first.

title: Help For Your Hang-ups In The Bathroom
text:
Summary: Far superior to the Dollar Store run of this sort of item.

AmazonBasics can be a very hit or miss proposition. This one is a definite hit.

Much better made than the average for this kind of cheap accessory. The metal has a slight circular curve to it (picture a length of pipe sawn in half lengthwise) which strengthens it considerably over a flat piece of metal of the same gauge. This will prevent it from easily warping or bending under a load.

The back of the hanger has a soft "grippy" rubber lining so it won't scratch the pain or finish on a door and won't wiggle around in place. The tips of the double hanger have heavy rubbery caps on the ends so there is nothing sharp or jagged to snag clothes and to give some protection if you bump into it. Well thought out.

The metal is a just a bit thick so if you door fits snugly into the frame it may not be closable or might need a bit of extra effort. If this is a problem, a bit of work with a plane along the top of the door should fix it. It's the price of something being made of better than average materials. We've become too accepting of cheap junk.

I have two very heavy Turkish terrycloth bathrobes hanging on it, maybe ten pounds total and no wiggle or warp or sing it won't hold up.

The only negative and it's a petty one is the thing is over-packaged. It came in a bubble pack envelope, then in a fitted box and then the hanger itself was tucked into a cardboard "stiffener" with cutouts to hold it.

A lot of packaging for one item but it will ensure it arrives unbent or crushed. I've had $100 electronics that were not this well protected by the manufacturer.

title: Got some hang-ups about your wardrobe?  Get these!
text:
Good, basic hangars, just right for light or medium weight shirts, blouses or sweaters. They flex just a bit more than I like, thus the four stars.

There's a sort of "velvety" coating on the hangar so items are unlikely to slide off as they do on some palstic and wrie hangars but it also makes it harder to slide stuff *onto* the hangers.

The price is great and buying 50 at a time just makes sense as you almost never have too many hangars.

title: Nice Mobile Laundry Hamper, Not So Great Assembly Assets
text:
I put this together in just under 45 mins. Ideally, this probably could've been done in 15 or less. I just want to point out that even though this include an L hex & a wrench - you will most likely need more tools.

The small wrench was designed specifically for the nut of the wheels, so it's too large for the nuts that attach the legs. For this you'll need a socket ratchet, crescent or pliers to stabilize the nut for the L hex. This particular L hex is pretty cheap - small & made of very soft medal. The hex tip stripped after just two bolts. So, I got a pair of pliers & a better / longer hex wrench to speed the assembly along. After that, it went fast.

The frame of the laundry hamper is pretty good. The wheels are really sturdy & large like a shop cart would have. I was really please with how handy this became. I attached the laundry bag & was able to roll it around the house with no issues. This is definitely going to be handy for when the kids & everyone tries to gather laundry all at once.

Putting the issues of the build aside, this is a quality hamper & frame. I will definitely recommend it to family & friends. I'm only knocking it 1 star for the lack of tools or mention that other tools might be necessary - some people don't have a good set hex wrenches or a ratchet handy.

title: Frustrating assembly, but nice final product. Cat approved. A little scuffed up on arrival.
text:
I received this in exchange for a review, so I can't comment on the final pricing of the product yet.

The assembly on this was frustrating for me and took me more than an hour to get it assembled. The instructions don't do as good of a job as they should showing orientation of pieces, how the pieces are marked, or singular steps. Often, the instructions show five pieces or more being put together at once and it is just a hard piece to follow. A couple pieces were actually not labeled at all due to mistamps so I had to work through that. After it was fully assembled, though, it was easier to deal with. I can say, be cautious about C and C1. It isn't labeled properly and I put in 10 screws before realizing I had used the wrong parts.

The actual finished product is decent. The table is supposed to be wood, and it feels like, but it's not painted and instead has a laminate type of finish on it. The top panel of mine was scuffed up a bit, so it detracts from the look a little. The drawer knob looks nice against the black. The pull out drawer is more of a panel than anything so it doesn't hold much, and the things on it aren't really stable. It works well for a watch, a phone, and a few trinkets. It slides smooth. I mostly wanted this so we could put lamps on the bedside table, and have a place to put books, the clock, and the Kindle.

I like the finished piece, but the assembly is really what frustrated me most. The stability seems good on it. It has a surprisingly heavy weight limit of 55 lbs on top and 35 lbs on the bottom. My two cats tested the top out for a total of 21 lbs, and it is cat approved. I'd get this again, and after assembling it I think it'll be easier on a matching pair. I just wish mine wasn't scuffed on top and that it was paint versus a laminate covering. I felt like it would've been four star based on scuffs, but objectively it really is a five star table for what it is. Simple product, functional, looks good. Works like it should.

title: Awesome infuser bottles. Work wonderful for tea, too! The wide opening does allow some fruit thru.
text:
These bottles work wonderfully. They are easily assembled, and with the two pack I can make two different beverages up and have them in the fridge ready to go in my lunch pale. The top twists off and comes apart so they clean up easily and there's no chance of pieces getting fruit or infusion particles stuck and causing a mold issue.

The infusion part of the bottle is quite large. It has plenty of holes to allow the fruits to infuse with the water, but this does allow some particles to come through into the water. The opening to drink out of is large enough that any particle that comes through the infusion canister would be able to be drank.

The bottle is a great size too. I have been using mine for tea. I can place a couple of tea bags into the infuser chamber and let them set to get the tea flavor into my water. They also work well for cucumber water and provide a good amount of flavor. I'd get these again in other colors. I've been really happy with them so far. I haven't had any issues with leaks or anything so far. I'll definitely update if they break down, but I think these will last a long time. They're the perfect size for cup holders and work well on the trail, too.

The twist off top is easy to grab, and it has an easy hold pull tab to get the infuser out. The design keeps the infuser out of the bottle so it doesn't sink and have to be fished out. Also worth noting, the silicon tab in the top of the bottle does come out and the bottle can still be drank out of without opening it, although I don't prefer to use it that way.

title: Awesome set of tools. Versatile and well thought out. Rotary pizza/pastry cutter is excellent.
text:
This is an excellent set of stainless steel tools. It's honestly wonderful, and was a great addition to my kitchen. There were several pieces - cutter, spatula, measuring cups, masher - that were missing in my kitchen and several other pieces that exceeded my expectations. It's a lovely set and would make a great housewarming gift. I'm impressed with it. If you use cast iron like I do, it's an awesome set to add pieces to outdoors and grilling, as well.

All of the tools have a hook end that makes them easy to hang inside or outdoors. The only negative to my set was that one of the most essential tools, the whisk, was broken. It was warped and one of the wires had popped out and wouldn't go back into place. It is unfortunate because it's one of my kitchen staples, but I have other whisks. Otherwise, it'd be a five star set through and through.

The peeler is decently sharp. I don't have any issues going either direction.

The masher works well. It can leave things chunky, but I just use it a little longer and use the spatula to move the veggies around and mash a little more.

The sifter is nice, especially for powder sugar and pastry items.

The garlic masher is okay. It works well, but a lot of the garlic gets stuck and has to be scraped off.

The measuring cups are true to size. They look nice and work well. I wish there were intermediary sizes like 2/3 and 3/4, but solid overall.

There's a knife included that I think is a cheese knife. It's a little flimsy on hard cheese, so I'm super careful. It could be better.

The icecream scoop/melon baller is solid. No bending.

The pizza cutter/pastry cutter is my new favorite. It blows my Farberware one out of the water.

The can opener is alright. It's a common can opener and works well.

The tongs are good. They don't cut me when I wash them. They're flush underneath, so no edges.

Something I've noticed is a ton of the tools in this set are long - which helps me when deep frying.

The turners in this set are good. They work nicely with cast iron and I don't have any issues. They're solid stainless and the handles keep from distributing too much heat to my hands so I'm not getting burned from hot utensils.

The zester is decent. It works well, although a lot of zest gets stuck to it. No issue, really.

The pasta spoon is a new favorite. The teeth bend up nicely and grab a lot of spaghetti, angel hair, and fettuccini when in use.

The corkscrew is fairly basic. I keep it outdoors with the grill and use it outside. It's good, but basic.

The rest of the set is quite nice. Turners, spatulas, spoons, and strainers. They all have good length to them, and are solid. They work well when frying and grilling because I can stand back a little more. I'd for sure get this set again, but I wish they had included a nicer whisk and a second or third whisk in the set because one is never really enough. I also which is had silicon on the whisk. I was bummed that that essential tool was damaged. Overall, it could be a truly five star set but that one piece is really a staple.

title: Solid whisks. Silicon seems solid. Handles are a bit light, but they stay together well.
text:
I liked the whisk set. They are a little light in the handle, which sometimes makes it feel like I'm not holding anything, but other than they they're great. The silicon coating has stayed on well through several washings, and the way the whisk components come together at the tip is not wiggly. There aren't any gaps in the end, which is great.

I'd get these again. The multi sizes work well for breads, eggs, and mixing. The variety also gives me choices with wet and dry ingredients. I've not noticed any slipping on the silicon parts or any separation at the end, and all wires overlap without major wiggle and gaps. Solidly built set. Bonus - they have a hook/loop at the end so I can hang them or put a clip through them to keep them together on the pan hangers.

They handle cleaning in the upper rack of our dishwasher without issue, and have made it through numerous cleaning cycles with no issues whatsoever.

Highly recommended!

title: Great minimalist heater for small spaces
text:
This little heater is SUPER simple to operate - just plug it in and flip the switch to on. There is no thermostat, no fan control, and nothing else to fiddle with.

The design is very sleek and simple and actually passes muster with my incredibly picky wife. It even blends in with her bathroom, where nothing is allowed to exist that doesn't match the decor. ;-) . (See photo).

It is tiny - barely bigger than a coffee mug - but it puts out enough heat that you can't have it under your desk for long before you'll be too warm.

Its perfect for a small to mid-sized bathroom, a small home office, or a cube-dweller that needs some warmth but doesn't want to bring in a full sized heater that keeps tripping circuit breakers (this is only 500 watts, which is less than a lot of desktop computers draw while running).

A few things to note:

1. The fan runs continuously - there is no thermostat. If you are too close to the unit, it will probably get too warm.

2. There is a "tip-over switch" on the bottom of the unit which shuts it off it is not sitting on a flat surface

3. Because it is a fan-forced heater and not a radiant heater, there is some fan noise. Its not bad, but if you are very sensitive to continuous background "white noise" it could be an issue. I'm taking off 1/2 a point for the fan noise (it could be quieter)

4. A bunch of warnings are PRINTED on both sides of the heater in black ink. Not stickers, but PRINTED. This really is unsightly (and annoying) if you are trying for a super "clean" look. I'm taking off another 1/2 point for these stupid warnings not being removable.

Overall, I think this is the perfect little heater for a bathroom or office - at 500 watts, it uses 1/3 to 1/4 of the power of a normal portable heater. It is small, unobtrusive, and has a very clean and simple design that fits in with just about any decor.

title: A Large, Comfortable Executive Office/Computer Chair
text:
Overall, this chair from AmazonBasics will do the job -- it's fairly sturdy, comfortable with head and neck support, and assembles fairly easy. There were only four (4) steps to get the whole thing together.

The instructions were good - not great. The technical drawings looked a little rushed, but they were done well enough to let you know what goes where.

While the chair came together just fine and provides ample support, it didn't arrive in the best shape. The faux leather/vinyl has two one-inch rips on the sides that will only get worse as time goes on. And the plastic handle on the lever that raises and lowers the chair had snapped off. It's still functional -- it's just that there's got to be better quality control when packing these materials.

AmazonBasics has a 90 days warranty on the quality of their parts. The warranty reads: " If the Product proves defective during the warranty period, and you follow the instructions that we will provide to you for returning the Product, we will, at our option, take one of the following actions: (i) replace the Product with either a new or a refurbished Product that is the same as or similar to the Product you purchased; (ii) repair the Product using either new or refurbished parts; or (iii) refund to you the purchase price of the Product." I'll give the number that came on the warranty a call and let you know how it goes.

Had the chair material not been ripped and the plastic part had not been broken, this would have been a 4 to 4 1/2 star product.

****UPDATED****
See my last paragraph above. The company has been in touch with me and was concerned that the product had been damaged in shipping and offered to replace it at no charge. They said if anyone experiences a similar issue, they would do the same. The bottom line is that they want to you be happy with your purchase.

title: Where is the quality control?!?  This should come w/ band-aids & a reimbursement for your time.
text:
I purchased this bakers rack because while my kitchen is quite large, but I do not have much open countertop space. I was contemplating ordering other steel and wood-type racks, in lieu of this more industrial wire-type ones, but the price was too good to pass up. I have a similar 5-shelf rack that is of similar construction, and for my needs right now, I decided it would work.

The installation is pretty straightforward, and the instructions are easy to follow. All the pieces were there, and nothing was broken or damaged. Fortunately, despite a mediocre sanding and finish job on the wooden shelf, it was at least planed properly and I don't have a wobbly surface to deal with. I won't plan on using it as a cutting board, and it at least provides a more stable base for my toaster oven and toaster.

The problem, however, is that I cut myself several times, as did my daughter that was helping me assemble the rack! The edges of the wire-stainless steel were just chopped off and then tack welded in place, leave weld slag, and extremely sharp and dangerous edges throughout the entire shelving system. If I didn't need it so bad, I would have just boxed it back up and sent it back to Amazon. I am very disappointed that I had to spend over an hour with a Dremel in hand, grinding down welds and hazardous edges. Now, instead of a shiny stainless steel look, the rack is marred by my sanding efforts. I could not allow this to remain in my house, though, for my own safety, but especially for that of my young children.

For this reason, I would mark this down to zero (0) stars, but considering that the rack assembled easily, it doesn't wobble, there were no broken pieces, and it meets the minimum requirements I had for storage needs, I gave it two (2) stars overall. I may change this, though, so I will have to watch how it performs in the long run.

The baker rack market appears to be very competitive, and cheapest can be most expensive some times. This rack was marked down around $20+ when I first saw it, so it was a good financial deal at the point of sale, but my daughter and I could have been cut worse, or even my youngest child cut have been cut, and the medical costs could end up being much higher than what I paid for the rack, and for the relative convenience it provides with respect to storage and kitchen organization. Presently, I would not recommend this bakers rack until the manufacturer changes their procedures and puts more emphasis and action on safety and quality control of their product. In the rush to fabricate and sell products, companies need to take the time to inspect their products. There are other offerings available that cost more than this product, and should be considered before making the purchase. My $0.02.

title: One Star is Generous
text:
I don't like to give bad ratings. Really, I dont, and I got this as a Vine member. But, this thing has so many design flaws that giving it a one star is generous.

Let's start with the most important thing, which is it supposed to be a two rack clothes system. As you can see from the pictures, the racks are spaced so short and so close together that the clothes interfere with one another. I'm only 5' 4", so if my pants folded in half drag the bottom, it means anyone taller than me is gonna have pants wadded up. And even my small size shirts are wadded up on the ground level. When you hang clothes on the top. they run into and interfere with the clothes on the lower level. And, you can't set thus flush against the wall - you have to pull it out at least 4" for even a small woman's jacket not to hit the wall.

But let's talk about putting the thing together because you have to do that out of the box. First, something that probably should have taken 15 minutes to put together took me 40 minutes because the instructions are so unclear. Assembled about a 3rd of it and then take it all apart and start over because I had the wrong pieces in the wrong place. Maybe that's my bad, but I think it's the directions + unmarked assorted pieces.

Next, let's talk about the totally crummy hardware that comes with it. These screws are so cheaply made that even though I was handscrewing them in with a simple ratchet screwdriver and being very careful, the heads got stripped on some of them. It wasn't like I was using a high speed drill and was careless. You can see the shards of metal on my sheets from just screwing 1 screw in. Maybe try some good American steel next time?

Also, and more inportantly, the screws you need to hold the whole top rail on to the bottom have a complete design flaw. They show in the instructions that you hold a cute little (unsupplied) hand wrench to tighten them. The thing is you can't because they're countersunk, so you'd need to put the wrench on or below level. Which would be fine if you could use a socket but no, you need a (metric) socket big enough to fit over the cap, but the countersink hole is so small that you can't fit the right size socket down in there. See pic. So, you can hand tighten them, but the top row will probably eventually fall down with your clothes, or you can get some pliers (as I did) and grab the shiny round cap, which is hard to grip without scratching and tearing it all up. Super poor design.

And last, let's talk about quality. The only thing this product has going for it is that it's made out of bamboo, which theoretically is sustainable. I like that. But this is glued together pieces of bamboo and, as you can see from one of the pictures, the glued together pieces are already showing cracks and splitting apart before I've even assembled the thing. Wait til I put the weight of the clothes on it...

Amazon, you usually put your name on pretty good products. This is not one of them.

title: I own an Aeron chair and at a quarter the price this chair is in the same league.
text:
My Aeron chair is still going strong after more than 20 years of use. Its only problem is a slight wobble. But now that both my spouse and I are working from home, I needed to purchase a second office chair. We are middle aged and supportive office chairs are not an option -- they are essential.

With today's economic uncertainties we could not justify the thousand dollar outlay for a second Aeron chair, but we wanted something with similar technology. There are many Aeron clones to choose from on Amazon so I set my budget at $250 and did some detailed research. This chair won out because of its full adjustability, its mesh seat, and its headrest.

One must-have feature that was Aeron's original innovation is a slightly elastic mesh seat. Like a hammock, the seat suspends your butt in mid-air, almost as if you are floating. This means no hot spots of pressure points like you experience after a couple of hours in a conventional chair. Another benefit of the mesh used for the seat and back is that it is breathable, a major comfort boost in summer.

A mesh seat's surface conforms to your unique anatomy. The forward section of this seat is padded with a dense material, providing essential support to your thighs, another must-have feature for a computer chair but rarely included for cost reasons.

The seat's tall back is adjustable, includes variable lumbar support, and is lockable at the angle you desire. The headrest is multi-adjustable and allows your neck to take breaks by resting your head against it. The armrests are made of an overly hard plastic material and will not lock in their forward position, a minor nuisance. I will probably buy a couple of soft foam wrist pads and glue them to the armrests.

Assembly would have been easier with more detailed directions. When directed, move the seat bottom forward to facilitate joining the two main sections. Having a helper eases the process. The main components are heavy and awkward for one person to juggle when joining the main sections. But I was able to do it.

Once together, the chair is stylish and rock solid. It could pass for a thousand-dollar chair. There are no wiggles or wobbles, at least at this early stage of our relationship. And it is all-day comfortable. While waiting for this to arrive I used one of our dining chairs, and after only a couple of hours on my PC I experienced a sore back (I've had lumbar surgery and my back is a weak point) along with a sore butt.

This new chair, in terms of its construction, comfort, adjustability, and perceived quality, is definitely in the same league as my Aeron. Like the Aeron, it provides my late-middle-aged body with the support and comfort I need to be productive. At the end of my work day (I take breaks to stretch and walk my dog) I am not exhausted.

If I encounter durability problems I will update this review, but I doubt I will. The $250 price tag makes this chair a bargain -- it exudes quality just as effectively as my Aeron chair. And it is every bit as comfortable to use.

title: Finally - A Chair that I'm Not Nervous About Breaking

This chair is great if you a really chubby short guy like me. If you're even looking at this chair I'm sure you're wondering the same thing, how long until the lift gives out? Cons:

-The bottom of the chair can be a little noisy when you sit down as you get sort of a metal "ting" sound. Not a huge deal, just a little annoying.

Overall, if you're a heavy guy who wants an office chair that you won't be nervous about breaking and is at a reasonable price point, this chair is for you.

title: comfortable, tall but already coming loose.
text: I ordered this chair after the first two I ordered failed to ship, so this was my 3rd pick of chairs. At first, it seemed perfect. I ordered upgraded wheels to put on it, which did raise the height of the chair about half an inch. When I assembled the chair (fairly normal installation process with these types of chairs) I used that thread glue on them to make sure they stayed put. With that being said, I've owned the chair about one month now and the arms are already starting to loosen. When I sit in this chair, my feet dangle off the ground and I am 5'3 and sit with the chair on its lowest setting. I have extra room in the seat of the chair so I do not touch the arms while sitting in the chair. The cushions are comfortable enough and I have no complaints about that.  The base of the chair is metal, but rough and man does it hurt if you hit your foot with the chair when trying to roll around. The chair has already cut the back of my ankle. If you are a tall person, the height will most likely not be an issue for you. Though if you are heavier than 300 lbs, I can't see this chair holding up for a long time, even though it's rated up to 500 lbs. They really need to fix the base of this chair! Round off the edges better or something!

title: Misleading Information Is Far More Harmful Than This Amazing Little Heater
text:
This little heater actually had me sweating, which isn't hard to do, but I didn't expect that. Also, the back stays cool to the touch, due to a fan, and the sides (top, bottom, left and right) and the back all remains cool to the touch. We all know not to touch the front of the heater, because that's like touching a burning fire, and complaining about how dangerous fire can be, but excusing our own lack of common sense is far more dangerous for us and others.

Also, this little heater, in and of itself, does NOT cause cancer, regardless of what the tag says. The warning doesn't explain how this heater can cause cancer, but this little ceramic heater would have to be used in an old house or building that has asbestos or has lead paint. By heating these elements, they can possibly get in the air for us to breathe, and this could possibly cause us to develop cancer, but I don't live in a house with asbestos or lead paint, so this little heater can't heat these dangerous elements that could cause me cancer.

title: Works well, but handle allows water to accumulate inside it
text:
I have used a microplane grater for years, and love it. I wanted to pick up a wider one for hard cheeses, as the one I have is a narrow profile more for citrus zesting. I decided to give this one from AmazonCommercial a try.

The grate feel nearly as sharp as the one I have from MicroPlane. It works great and without issue. The frame also feels sturdy while I am using it.

The main issue I have with this product is the handle seems to be hollow, and there is a somewhat large opening at one end. This allows water to accumulate inside the handle and would be a great breeding ground for mold and bacteria, because it is impossible to get in there and clean it out. It is the same handle design as on a few other AmazonCommercial kitchen utensils I have, and I'm kind of disappointed by this. A simple injection molded rigid plastic handle would be just as durable and would not have this issue!

title: My first adjustable bed base, and so far, it's fantastic!
text:
A few months ago when the cheap bed frame finally broke, I had to shop around for a replacement frame. The local mattress & furniture stores wanted to sell me sets of frames plus mattresses that would run me several thousand dollars for decent quality. But my old foam mattress was stilll fine!
My outrage at the hard-sell tactics of brick-and-mortar mattress stores led me back here finally, where this wonderful, economical alternative was suggested.
It arrived on time and in excellent condition.
Set-up was as quick as unboxing, screwing in four legs, and flipping it over. Plug in. Then put batteries in the remote and aim. Easy as that!
Darn thing was heavy, so I had a sturdy helper for sliding it into the bedroom and the flip.
Very happy now with my bed, and the ten inch foam mattress is a perfect pairing. It just so happens that I've been sick with a cold, and being able to adjust my bed's position is a great help to sleeping with a stuffy nose.
One caveat to the reviewer who said they could feel the hard bed base even when they put in a two inch mattress topper...yeah, this isn't meant to replace a mattress. This is just the bed base, capiche? Get a real mattress, not a topper. There ya go, little camper!

I like that there are different sizes for use with different sized pans and different volumes of liquid when making sauces or gravies. They can also be used for whipping cream or merengues. However, they are quite flexible which means it requires more work for things like merengues. A stiffer whisk is better for that. I prefer these for mixing light liquids for sauces or gravies rather than beating things that need lots of air.

They are not heavy duty. They are lightweight so they may not stand up to heavy use. They clean up easily. The price seems right.

Even though there are two bolts that attach the headboard to the frame it wasn't enough to keep the headboard at a 90-degree angle. So, to stop the headboard from tilting forward I just put a zip tie around the bottom of the post and frame to give it added support. You can see the white zip tie in the picture. title: This isn't a chair as much as it is a torture device
text:
As I write this review this chair is "currently unavailable." I'm going to go ahead and write it anyhow as a warning to others should this medieval contraption become available again.

This is, and I can't stress this enough, the most uncomfortable chair I have ever owned. It's like they designed it to be terrible. The chair leans jussst a bit forward and jusssst a bit to the left, so you constantly feel as though you are sliding out of it. I've checked all the bolts and tightened it up, I've adjusted the tilt tension. No deal, pure pain and suffering. The seat cushion must be just for show as it feels as though you are sitting directly on a slab of wood.

It is so uncomfortable that it's hard to work in it as you just keep thinking, "Wow, this is really uncomfortable." After an hour my back, neck, and shoulders are sore and (to get a bit personal) the sliding is pinching my cods pretty good. Ouch.

Looking back at my Amazon orders the last chair I purchased was in 2013. An 8 year life for a chair for a dude my size is pretty good, I would get another one of those in a heartbeat but they are no longer available.

I hate this chair. Do not buy this chair. I mean, unless you're all freaky-deaky and like pain and suffering. In that case, you do you.

title: Loved it, then it failed me — It'll fail you too [PLEASE READ]
text:
This sealer was everything I could ask for for a solid two years, when it stopped working out of nowhere. I then saw the review/video by Michael Frick that documents the weak intra-hinge ribbon cable... which seemed to line up with what might be happening with mine, so I opened it up.

It's true. Every single one of these will break long before any critical components go bad due to a weak cable that passes through one of the hinges. Even the lightest, most careful use will prematurely kill this device.

Blatant planned obsolescence, if not pure negligence.

I really liked this sealer. Did not want to upgrade and already recommended it a bunch — big regret.

Consider some other brand until/if Amazon ever addresses this.

title: Beautiful piece but do your homework
text:
This is a very specific Television stand that will either sit low on the floor or must be places on another piece of furniture, such as a breakfront or wide cabinet making one or the other superfluous. It’s imperative that you use a measuring tape and, if you can’t visualize spacial relations, perhaps cut a template before you order this. It’s a good quality piece but is remarkably specific and in most cases won’t suit the typical needs.

It arrives in a vast box about the weight of a motorcycle and is very well packed for safe transport. (Be prepared to tip your postal carrier after s/he’s lugged this onto your porch.) The design is simple and the style looks-as is the fashion- as though it would be at home on the set of “Company.” The frame is of sturdy, black steel. It holds three gliding drawers large enough to hold a bunch of DVDs or gaming equipment. The drawers, also black, are of pressed wood with a laminate. The top is a single piece of thick glass on which you’ll rest your monitor. There is space above and below the drawers for satellite equipment such as blue ray or PS3 or X-Box. Because it’s glass, connecting wires must be carefully snaked so there is no messy quagmire of cords, wires and feeds.

Again, this is a very specific design and in the right circumstance a beautiful stand. It is likely, however, that a great deal of thought, measuring, and planning is required before deciding this is the piece for you.

title: 1966, Corinthia plush, well made and comfortable
text:
This chair is designed to look like a chair from the 1960’s. Similar designs are visible on the sets of The Brady Bunch, Bewitched and in magazine photos of the homes of NASA heroes. This very chair is seen in photos of the home of Marge Slayton and Annie Glenn. Today’s styles reflect a melange of everything from the 50’s through the 80’s. Since you’ve come this far, let’s assume the style appeals to you.

The cost is reflective of the quality. The construction is solid-very solid- and the frame holds my 295lb frame without a creak or complaint. The leather is a buttery corinthian leather, soft and comfortable with a sense that it breaths.

The chair is designed for comfort. The angle of the seat lifts the knees slightly which relieves pressure on the cocyx and lumbar. The arms are wide and long so that the arms are lifted just enough to remove tension from the neck and shoulders.

This chair takes up the same space as a full-sized wing back. It’s not a delicate piece for an anteroom oe a subtle corner. The box in which it’s delivered is large and heavy, but the only assembly required is to attach the legs.

This chair is solid, comfortable and likely to last a very long time.

title: "Firm" but I sink in more than mattress we're replacing and doesn't feel firm
text:
I sink in a TON more. This is NOT FIRM. Our old Zinus memory foam mattress I can sit on the edge of the bed and it barely moves, this Amazon Queen Size "FIRM" mattress I sink in a good 5-6 inches. This MAY be due to the air channels in one of the foam layers? Mattresses are not meant for sitting, but that's a huge indication this is less firm and less dense than Medium and Medium-Firm memory foam mattresses I've had in the past. It's not as noticeable laying down, when weight is distributed across the mattress I seem to sink in pretty evenly, so even though it's not at all "Firm" as they claim, I have had less back pain the few days we've used it so far.
The problem is, now my wife is uncomfortable because she feels she is sinking in more. We're both average weight and in fair shape, but I've had back and neck pain most of my life and neck surgery a couple years ago due to injuries. This mattress seems to have a more EVEN sink for me which keeps me in better alignment compared to our worn out mattress, but since it sinks so much more my wife feels like she's sliding down and now she's having back pain.
We didn't use it at all first couple of days, to let the foam rise to it's original shape/density. We are going to try it out a few more nights before deciding, but at this point I'm leaning towards returning it. I'd keep it if I slept by myself, despite sinking in more, because there is an even distribution when it's just me. It also seems a SLIGHT bit cooler than our older mattress. But since this thing sinks half way through it's 12 inch height, my wife feels like she's on a slide when my 165-170lbs sinks in more than her much lighter frame.

title: FYI: NOT non-stick and wasn't meant to be non-stick
text: I've seen several reviews complaining that everything cooked sticks to this pot. That's  because enabled cast iron is NOT NON-STICK. Just like when you cook in stainless steel cookware, you must add either liquid or oil when using enameled cast iron. So why use enameled cast iron? You use it for it's superior and even heat conduction as well as the easy cleanup caused by the enamel. But be careful not to chip the enamel because uncoated cast iron easily rusts and just like non-enamled cast iron, will need to be seasoned on the exposed iron to keep rust at bay. I clean mine with dish soap and water. Once I remove the food from the pot, I immediately pour in some boiling water and a few drops of dish soap while the pot is still hot. After I eat, the pot is cooled down so I wash it by hand with dish soap and warm water. Please avoid washing a hot enameled pot because the cooler dish water will cause the enamel to "craze" (develop fine lines and cracks). With proper care, this pot will last and look brand new forever...

text: I've bought many wire shelving units over the years and, up until now, they've all been those industrial grade wire shelving units that're ANSI-certified for food service use (Bought at a Big Box warehouse store whose name starts with a 'C'). Those shelving units are heavy and solid. You can climb on them without fear of bending the shelves. Imagine, then, my surprise at receiving this shelving unit. title: Game changer for small closets
text:
I bought these on a whim. I set out to buy larger hangers for my kids but upon realizing how cheap these were, I decided I'd get new hangers and they could have my plastic ones.

How have I lived so long without these? I switched all of my tops and most of my dresses over to hanging on these and now I no longer have to deal with all of the flimsy knits falling off. I also never realized what a pain the standard cross-bar having hangers really are when your closet is overstuffed. These can't get tangled up in each other the way those can.

Mine did not shed black powder everywhere. I tried to make it come off because of the negative reviews. After using all 50 hangers, I had a tiny bit of black on one finger that I probably wouldn't have noticed if I hadn't been expressly looking for it. The heads on these can be turned in either direction. There's a fair amount of tension in the hook so you do have to push it just a bit to make it turn.

A couple of tips because of some of the complaints I saw in other reviews: These are supposed to make it harder to take your clothes off the hanger. That's the point of the coating. If you're stretching your necks out when using these, take the hangers out from the bottom of the garment.

text: This table was easy to assemble, but it does take a bit of time with the most time consuming being attaching the back panel. It’s an attractive table that’s suitable for small spaces and works well as a night stand or end table. I’m using it as an end table next to my recliner in the bedroom. It’s just what I needed to sit my coffee or other beverage on while reading or watching tv. The drawer is a nice addition, and it’s large enough to hold my iPad, Kindles and my remotes. I put a decorative greenery basket on the bottom shelf, and I have a smaller one on the table top. I like the table a lot, but it’s a bit pricey when compared with similar tables available here.

title: Great for paella and sautéed vegetables
text:
I love Le Creuset products and own several of their pots and pans. You can use this pot for anything, but I especially like to use this for making fried rice, paella, sautéed vegetables and Mexican food.

Just be careful not to use anything sharp or abrasive, as you'll scratch the coating. I use wood or silicone utensils when cooking with my Le Creuset stuff.

Clean up:
Clean up is so easy too, much easier than my stainless steel. Just put some water on the bottom of the pan for 15-20 minutes and it comes off with a sponge. Make sure you don't submerge the entire pot in water overnight though, as this could potentially cause the exposed cast iron rims to corrode.

text:
As a side note, I actually purchased these, and I have reordered in order to replace all of my wire hangers. Out of 100, only one arrived already broken, which isn't a bad ratio but doesn't a promising future make.
I began searching for these because some organizational expert on Pinterest wrote that slim velvet hangers were absolutely essential to organizing one's closet. So I believed it. Having replaced most of my shirt hangers with these, I have to say that I appreciate the uniform appearance. Additionally, they do save space over plastic hangers, and they hold onto fabrics that would usually slip off. Additionally, the arms of the chair where the leather creases a bit from your arm resting on it as well as the front of the seat area were peeling after about 6 months. It's also a very loud chair. Everything squeaks very loudly when you move around. I weigh about 215lbs and use this as my work-from-home office chair. Would not recommend, would not buy again.

The chair weighs a lot and the base is all metal. It's got sharp edges that have completely skinned my heel/ankles multiple times.

title: Manual Controls Model for a Window: The fans run in both directions with separate controls.
text:
My windows will not open wide enough to hold a 20" box fan so I was looking for something that would be short enough to fit in my window. I bought this with manual controls with no remote. I am not a fan of digital and stuff like that just never lasts. The difference is this one you can't see the temperature on the dial of the fan but I will deal with that. Truthfully I wish it didn't have that feature at all.

When I opened the package I could see the bag it was in was tied in a knot and the cord wasn't factory wrapped so I was afraid it was a return but decided to give it a try. I plugged it in and to my surprise it didn't make any strange humming noises others have complained about. I turned it upside down and sideways to test it and it kept running normally on all settings. I bought the service plan with my fan just in case.

What I like about this fan is it seems to really blow decent and is quiet. You can also blow one fan in and the other out at the same time, so both fans have separate controls. You do not need to take it out of the window to change the fan direction. I was hoping for these features. I have played with the controls and both fans work like they should. I have both fans pulling the air in and it has cooled down the house pretty well and it's about 70 degrees outside. It's not an air conditioner so don't expect it to work like one.

I tried the slide sliders on the fan. They only slide out maybe 5" each side which isn't wide enough for my window. They did stay open because there are small little bumps on it to help hold it open which others said it didn't have. I don't need them open because I have screens in my windows and then my cats can look out the window on one side. They are not quite the full height of the fan so bugs will get in without a window screen. Also the fan would draw bugs in through it as it runs. I placed it in a window behind my sofa.

It comes with feet but because I want it for a vertical opening window I didn't put them on. I will save them for if I need them in the future. The window seems to hold it in place pretty well and I can tug on it without it coming out. I do not have double hung windows. It has 2 screws on the bottom back so it mostly snaps together. To take it apart to clean it will not be an easy task. I do like it so much I'm going to buy more and hope they run as well as this one does.

I recommend this fan but make sure you test it out as soon as it arrives to make sure both fans work. Turn it in all directions while it's running and test all the speeds and the direction switches. Maybe buy a service plan and keep it where you know where it is.

title: Good Design, easy assembly and multiuse raised top coffee table
text:
I bought this natural wood table for its closed storage area, and ability to raise the top use it for a desk for a lap top, and just bring food, or coffee etc. closer when seated on the couch. The assembly was quick (about 20 minutes) and easy, with well drilled holes. The holes were straight, and it fit fairly well, but the sections do not smoothly line up to each other - about a 1/16 inch offset in several areas. After assembly, the table was sturdy and did not wobble. The natural color is good. It is not all natural wood planking as advertised. It appears to be a good veneer. The drawer bottom (section below the lid) is paper, and will not be able to take much weight. I planned to store books inside, and besides the problem with a paper liner, the area inside is not very big. so will have to use the bottom shelf instead. I have some woven water hyacynth baskets that fit underneath as well, and the fact that it has only two sections instead of the three in similar tables gives more flexibility for larger items to be stored on the bottom shelf. The table does have a weight limit of 45 lbs so do not lean or sit on it. The wood is not completely smooth, and the coating is rough, and slightly thin or white in some areas. The hinge mechanism has a beefy spring, and a stop that is to allow it to support extra weight. It can be raised less than the full height if light items such as a meal, a drink, or magazine were placed on it, but should be raised to where it locks in place for heavier items, or to keep it in a raised position.. There is a released knob when it is ready to be lowered. The feet on the legs consist of glued fabric, and fell off as I was assembling the table. It would be worth investing in hard plastic ones that normally are nailed to the bottom of the legs, to allow the table to slide on a floor or carpet. Some furniture have plastic covers for the holes left in the assembly. This did not, although most of the holes were out of sight. The hinge mechanism had large very rusted bolts and this is not acceptable for a new item, nor choice of material. I will get a replacement and see if the problem is consistent. The wood also had some discolored areas that looked like it had been exposed to moisture. I wiped of grey and green in a couple of spots. The soft cardboard packaging was ripped in some areas, and the red ribbon taped to the back of the assembly hardware was sticking out through a hole. It is curious what purpose the ribbon has, because it did not help get the hardware out of the packaging.
I received the replacement and looked at the hardware. They are iron and either painted, plated or galvanized except for the hinge bolts, which have no coating and could rust again.

title: Perfect for a Small Bathroom on Chilly/Freezing Days
text:
As the season changes to chilly mornings and winter approaches, I bought this to use in my small bathroom so I could run it for 20-30 minutes before hopping in the shower. I purchased a house two years ago that was built in 1966 and instead of running the whole house heater just to warm up the bathroom, this little ceramic heater does the job perfectly. Further, my 1966 bathroom does not have much counter space and although I could place this on the floor, I prefer to have it on my vanity for better heat dispersal. Because of the tip-over safety feature, I am perfectly comfortable to let the heater run with the door closed while I'm grabbing my morning coffee before showering. As a native Southern Californian, I am still not used to the absolute cold mornings despite living in Boston for 3 years and now in Ohio for 15 years. I leave the heater running while in the shower so when I pull back the shower curtain, the room is still a comfortable temperature. Then after I've dried off and slipped on my winter robe, I can then face the bracing blast of cold air when I open the bathroom door.

Great little heater. I'm considering getting another one to keep under my desk. Again, not that I expect this little heater to heat up a big room but to give me a direct source of heat to take the chill out of the air. Highly recommend but be realistic as to how you are going to use it. Don't think that it will do anything in a space any larger than a modern half-bath or under the desk by your feet because it will not work in those applications. In those situations, you will need a larger, higher output heater than this model. The price point is very attractive too.

One note: As with most electronics of this ilk, there is a rather large flag-like warning on the cord. I just wrapped it around the cord and either affix a twist tie or a rubber band to contain the warning (which is almost the same size as this heater!) without cutting it off and potentially inadvertently slice the cord.

Hope this review is helpful. Let me know if you have any questions.

All parts are labeled. Posts C and D were labeled wrong, they were swapped. Fortunately, I noticed this early on.
Over all assembly took about 2 hours, partially because of some disassembly needed because of mislabeled parts.
I recommend keeping all bolts loose until you have all of the framing assembled, then tighten them. I had some issues with holes not lining up properly due to some slight twisting.

The slats for the bottom bunk were loose on one half and extremely tight on the other half. I had to take the end cap off of one of the slats to get it to fit. I'm not sure if the side rail was bent or if the end frame was the wrong length.

This bunk bed seems to be a bit shorter than others I've assembled in the past. The room between the lower and upper bunks seems insufficient. There's not much head room on the lower bunk. You really need to be mindful of the thickness of the mattresses that you use. A 6" mattress for the bottom and top is the MAX thickness. The top bunk's rails are about 12" high, which is about the same thickness of the mattress that we previously had and had planned on using up there, but can't for safety reasons.

There's a misprint in the specs in the instruction manual saying the bottom bunk is a queen size, although the front cover does correctly state that it is full size. It actually is full size on the lower bunk.

The bunk bed itself seems pretty solid. I would probably buy again.

title: Not bad, watch price
text:
I do like the sofa. It’s good for a smaller space and is 5-10 inches shorter than most full size sofas. Yet, two people can still lounge on it and not be touching.

The sofa also has some elegant lines. I like the gold/bronze feet, and the curved sides. It has a modern, feminine feel that’s still classic. This is the type of sofa that will feel fancy with a crystal lamp and cozy with a velvet pillow and libraryish with a stack of mystery novels nearby.

The seat is rather firm, but perhaps not as firm as other reviews have made it out to be. I do not like marshmallow furniture that swallows one in puffy cushions, so it seems fine to me. Probably, it’s not the type of sofa one would want to sleep on overnight. Also, the seat is not super deep like marshmallow sofas tend to be. While that suits me just fine, this sofa is most likely not suited well to extra tall individuals.

I’m not convinced it would hold up well to large pets or children of any size.

The seat is a “bench” style, which means there are no removable seat cushions, which is a feature I was looking for. The back cushions zip on and stay in place nicely.

Is it leather? Yeah, I don’t know. Maybe. But it’s not the high quality, buttery leather you may want, but I didn’t expect that considering I didn’t pay $3,000-5,000 for that kind of sofa.

The price on this sofa fluctuates a lot. The lowest I saw over a couple of months was around $1200 and the highest was $1800. I wouldn’t advise paying more than $1200. A few hundred less would probably be more appropriate.

My sofa arrived slightly damaged on the arm. Amazon said the sofa “wasn't available anymore” and wouldn’t replace it. It’s clearly available. However, they offered me a discount. I negotiated for a deeper discount and felt mostly satisfied. I specifically ordered a sofa that is sold and shipped by Amazon because I wanted any problems to be addressed immediately. I am glad I took that precaution when ordering something so big online. Amazon took care of it—not perfectly, but close enough.

Overall, I’m glad I bought it.

title: Not bad but could be improved
text:
When I moved into my basement apartment, I knew the temperature was controlled by the landlord who owns & lives in the main house. I realized pretty quickly that it sometimes gets rather cold in the basement so I decided to get a small heater for the cold days. This unit is adequate.

This was the 5th or 6th model I tried. My favorite one kept dying after a 1-4 weeks but it had the best features including the best safety feature. However, this one works & I've used it on/off for months. My apartment is about 430sq ft, about 380 sq ft in the main room. Just one unit can raise the temperature 2-3 degrees. Not as good the other units I tried so I usually keep around my desk when I'm working (I work from home).

Safety:
This could be improved a lot. To turn the unit on/off, there is a physical switch on the back. If the unit tips over, it automatically turns off. The problem occurs when the unit is knocked off a desk or table. If the unit lands upright, it automatically turns back on. If it lands facing furniture it will be blowing hot air directly onto potentially flameable objects unless / until you notice it got knocked over. I have cats, I don't always notice right away. Because of this, I I do not leave this on at night or when I leave the apartment.

There is no temperature control. It's either on or off. There is no fan function (ie, blowing without the heating element on). It doesn't oscillate. It is relatively quiet but because it doesn't just stay turned off if it falls & lands upright, that's less of an issue since I won't leave it on at night.

title: Living the bachelor life

As a bachelor, you tend to pick up only what you need at any given moment. That includes flatware. You can go to a big box store and pick up a knife here and a fork there, and you can buy in small quantities for a buck or two. After a while, when you realize that you need to grow up and you could possibly entertain a guest or two, you look for a decent and economical solution.

This Amazon Basics 20-piece flatware set is perfect for someone who needs something for themselves and can still host a small dinner party for family and friends. I bought it along with the serving set and it's just perfect for my needs. The weight of each individual piece is hefty and feels good in my hands and, of course, you can eat food with it! What more can you ask for?

Amazon Basics has become a trusted brand for me. Anytime I'm looking for something to use around the home, I always check to see whether Amazon Basics makes one. If they do, I always give the item serious consideration because the Amazon Basics brand has helped me be a better housekeeper. 🙂

title: Love This Pot
text:
I love this pot! It is a fully laminated stainless inner and outer layers with sandwiched aluminum for outstanding heat transfer. It includes a lighter weight fitting lid.

I was trained by a four-star Cordon Bleu chef back in my college days and gourmet cooking has been a hobby of mine for many years.

I have two sets of old USA made All-Clad cookware one in stainless and one in copper; I know quality tools.

Unfortunately, both my sets of all clad end at eight quarts. There have often been times when I needed more capacity, but just couldn't part with $400+ for an All-Clad 12 quart stock pot.

Since I was doing a stock I finally decided to get a all glad 12 quart pot from Amazon when my search pulled up this 12 quart stock pot. Since there was such a huge price difference I found it hard to believe this pot could even remotely compare to the All-Clad, but since it was Amazon I figured I could look it over then send it back with no cost to me other than my time.

When the pot arrived I was very pleased with the thickness, riveted handles and finish. The interior of this spot was not as highly polished as All clad, but if that became an issue for me a little compound on a buffing wheel would take care of that.

The real question is how well would this pot cook? I started out with a chicken stock that was cooked about 8 hours. Anyone that knows about a stock knows it needs to simmer for many hours to release as much flavor as possible, but it cannot burn. This pot performed as well as my 8 quart All-Clad pots.

The next test was one that separates a quality pot from the junk and that is to make a Cajun black roux. For those that cook, you know there is a fine line between a dark roux and a burnt roux. I was amazed as this big pot turned out a beautiful perfectly-cooked dark roux, possibly better than any of my All-Clad pots had ever done. With a root completed I went on to make a large spot of gumbo, which this pot had more than ample room for.

After using this pot on several tasks, I can't imagine why anyone would pay the asking price for an All-Clad pot made in China! When this one can be had for one sixth of the All Clad price.

title: Thermostat use update
text:
I like this heater, a little noisy but it is better than freezing.
The tricky part of this heater is setting the thermostat.
What I did to set it was to set the thermostat to the upper temperature I desired (73°). I have found that in my heating requirements that I need the 750w setting when the outside temp is 40° when the sun is down. Any warmer than that, I use a different 400w heater I own. So, when the temp drops below 40 outside, I plug this unit in, it will run to 73°, shut off and it will come on again at 63°. I run it sitting on a 18 inch high stand so the cold from the floor doesn’t effect the heater’s activation temperature setting. Eventually when it gets cold enough outside, the heater will run constantly. That is when I remove it from the stand and set it on the floor to completely heat the room (usually in the middle of the night). This unit keeps me comfortable down to 12° outside temp SET ON LOW. My bedroom is a insulated 12x6 cargo trailer with a full-size bed, toilet (my stand) and full size dishwasher.
I really question the safety of running it on high power. After being half way into winter running it on low, there is some slight discoloration of the protective wire screen. I have it on a 20 amp circuit and the outlet doesn’t get warm at all on low (750w).
I would prefer a electric oil heater, but due to my space requirements, it would be too close to combustible items. I chose this because I can aim the heat away from anything flammable.
Good luck!
Update 3/23:
After a couple of seasons with this heater, my ultimate easy heating solution is solved.
If you have to mess with the thermostat, especially if the heater is set on low, you need a smaller wattage heater.
I have a 250w, a 600w and this one. Problem solved.
I would be wary of running this unit on the high setting for long periods, ie. all night while you are sleeping. Read the other reviews about potential floor damage. Generally, I only operate this unit on high is when I get up in the morning.

title: LOVE these
text:
I bought my first pack of these this spring when I was switching my closet out from winter to summer clothing and found myself short on hangers. I wasn't looking for a miracle product; I just needed hangers and thought I'd try these out to see if they worked better than the mix of plastic/wire/wood ones I already had.

No lie - I was blown away using these hangers the first time. I share a tiny closet with my husband and before I bought these, was wondering how I was going to fit the waiting-to-be-hung pile of clothes I bought them for into my closet. I hung those, and switched out my worst (plastic) hangers and came out with more room in my closet than when I'd started. I cannot believe how much space they save. I bought more hangers for the rest of my clothes, and some for my husband's (110 total), so now they're all we're using in our closet. I even bought a new summer wardrobe for myself, and everything fits (!)

Having fully converted to this style of hanger only, it makes it so much easier to see what's in my closet - which is not only small, but hard to see into (just one door for access) and poorly lit. With all of my clothes hanging at the same level, there's nothing sticking up too high or hidden down between other garments. It's easier for my eye to scan across to pick something out, and I appreciate the aesthetic of the uniformity.

Perhaps the best thing about these, however, is that my clothes - all of them: wide-neck tops, flimsy camisoles, sweaters, you name it - don't slip off. No more picking clothes off the closet floor! And the sloping shape really does works to stop indentations from forming in my sweaters' shoulders - even heavy cotton ones. I tested them out for a month or so to see how they fared, and my sweaters were all in perfect condition, so I've cut out all those annoying rubber hanging slips that come attached in the shoulders of some garments (which always seem to slip out the top of my shirts when I'm wearing them.)

If there's a downside, and this isn't really a big deal, it's that it can sometimes be tricky to get a garment onto the hanger, since the velvet catches onto fabric and stops it from sliding smoothly. So you do have to take a bit of extra time to make sure you get your item on the hanger just right. Beyond that, I'm really thrilled with these. I feel like I have a new closet.

I haven't had any issues with breakage except for one, and it didn't break hanging on the rod. (I'm not sure what happened exactly, but my husband was messing around with it.) That said, I don't think they'd hold up well under heavy winter coats. I'm converting my coat closet to wood hangers instead, which are more durable but take up tons of space.

title: Class B Fit on the Bolts - Nearly Impossible to Get Arms On
text: No matter how you count em', there weren't the right number of bolts in the package to make this work. Fortunately I saved the hardware from the chair I took apart. The arm required much force and pressure to line the mount points up on the chair for the left armrest. They weren't even close even with the bolts as loose as possible. Instructions murky on how the upper portion of the chair (back rest) should go under or over the bottom plate mounting to the hydraulic and wheel carriage. And why should there be a few bolts left over if they supplied the correct number of the each sized bolt as indicated on the instructions (at least there was a rudimentary set of diagrams). The bottom plate should have the shortest bolts because that has no torque on it. Those are set by down pressure in the seat.  The tools (metric hex keys) were unusable on the bottom plate front fasteners. It kept hitting the adjustment knob just behind it. The back rest should be attached with the beefiest bolts, but that wasn't the case. We'll see how long that lasts with a few easy reclines. This faux-leather finish seems more durable than my previous chair, but this synthetic stuff just cracks and peels within two years. Let's see if I do better here? Spend your money on a more lux chair if you want it for the long run.

it has no intensity knob, it's either on or off.
The "safety switch" is a simple button on the bottom, if the button is pressed it can go on, if released, off. i can imagine that breaking, making it trash either as a fire hazard or trash as a small box of nothing.
It's very small, not quite enough to heat my small bathroom in a reasonable time, it's less for heating space, better for putting your toes in front of to warm them. that's a fine purpose, but not what i (and other reviewers, clearly) needed.
It's small and LIGHT and the cord is very stiff? which means the kinked cord can shift the heater around..or you can just bump it, and as one reviewer said, that metal grid on the front gets very hot...

I think that's all of what i wanted to say. it's OK as a toe-warmer, but i wouldn't buy it again.

title: I had my doubts these would replace parchment paper
text:
(Yes, another update: This is to mention the limits of these mats. I was supposed to broil a dish at 500 degrees to brown the top and did not even notice a cookie sheet remained on a lower shelf with one of these mats on it. Do not broil at 500 degrees with these mats in the oven. Although once I noticed smoke rising from the mat I promptly removed it from the oven and no harm seems to have come to it. Still flexible, but its color is somewhat darker. Other than that we washed it and have used it again since. But just a word to the wise, definitely not a broiling mat.)

(Okay, another update: I like trying different things with these, since I also like not having to scrape and clean pans. We went out to a steak house and I ordered the large onion rings. They suggested a 1/4 serving size since they give you so many. I wasn't about to pass up a full order for $4 more. But my wife said they taste terrible when reheated. I got them anyway.

So today I went to reheat the onion rings. But I had a plan. First I popped them in the microwave to get them warm. Then I fired up our Toshiba toaster oven to 420 degrees. The smallest of these mats fit the toaster oven tray, so I put the onion rings in on top of the mat and left them in for five minutes. They got a nice crisp outside and weren't soft and rubbery the way my wife said they would be, and they tasted better than when we were served in the restaurant.

Mat was a quick cleanup with a soapy sponge and hot water and absolutely no mess inside of the toaster oven. I really like these mats.)

(Another update: Some peanut butter cookies fresh out of the oven - look a tiny bit overcooked, but I like a little crunch. The mats have been used a good two dozen times thus far and not a thing has stuck, even slightly. Although these cookies are best left to fully cool before moving. They have lots of moisture in them, and while they don't stick in the normal sense, that moisture can cause some adhesion that disappears when they cool.)

(Update: Just had buttermilk biscuits last night and I can't get over how things simply do not stick to these. I told my wife I think this is the end of spatulas for people like me. It is kind of fun just taking everything off with my fingers. Between her silicone pie mat and these I think she has a lot of her Christmas presents already wrapped up.)

My wife swears by her parchment paper, and you would think I had committed blasphemy when I told her I had purchased three sets of these. I was pretty nervous wondering what would happen. Thus far we have used them for cookies, scones, and sweet potato fries in the oven. Not even the slightest hint of something sticking. I can lift things off with my bare hands - immediately if I want to get burned.

They work perfectly, and her parchment paper has not left the pantry shelf since these arrived. And they are really easy to wash off. Light soap and hot water and they don't hold any water, so if you feel like imitating a dog you can shake the water off.

Have to admit I didn't think they would make it in a 425 degree oven, but they still look new. And now she wants to give them for Christmas gifts. Guess I got lucky this time.

title: useful but utilitarian storage
text:
A sturdy, if utilitarian, way to expand kitchen storage. It's a little cumbersome to assemble (mostly for poor directions), but not difficult.

Positives:
* Very adjustable: height of shelves, height of legs, placement of hooks, you can leave off the wood shelf or top shelf
* Good capacity in a size that will match "unused wall" in many homes.
* Bottom shelf can be installed high enough to allow storage under it.
* Top shelf designed to have a rim, so things placed up top won't get knocked off.
* Easy to disassemble. no tools to assemble.

Negatives:
* Really bad, miniatures-sized directions
* Several parts can be reversed accidentally and aren't clearly labeled
* This sort of metallic design makes a ringing noise when the shelves are tapped, unless weighted down
* Wood shelf isn't a tight fit, so wiggles around a little

Despite some grumbling from me during assembly and placement, I've really liking this rack. It doesn't look like much, but that's a positive (it's for utility, not showiness). The stain on the wood shelf is generic enough a color that it doesn't clash with my maple cabinets and furniture. It holds everything I had on a smaller rack that took up almost as much space, with room to add more.
I use my rack for less-used kitchen items that I don't want to put in storage, random decorations, as well as a few houseplants. As pictured, I have the bottom shelf higher than the Amazon promo shot to allow storage under the shelf as well as for mopping access.

title: 4 star product
text:
This is a solid piece of furniture with one glaring flaw.

First the pros -
It took me less than an hour to put it altogether. It was not too difficult. The base of each leg has that nifty rotating mechanism which can help stabilize the rack if the floor is uneven. The shelves are sturdy and strong. Apparently they can hold upto 400 lbs of stuff - I wouldn’t risk that. But I’ve loaded it up with a bunch of unused appliances and it looks pretty solid. The clips which help seat the shelves onto the stainless steel columns seemed to be defective since they didn’t close all the way - but that is the design. I realized they didn't need to close fully as long as they ‘clicked’ around the necessary “level-aperture”. The shelves sit on the clips like champs. They gave me tons of extra clips and other doo-dads (but with no instructions on how and where the other doodads should be fixed).

Now the Cons -
The instruction booklet is tiny - so tiny I had difficulty reading it and just went by the pictures. The biggest problem is the wooden shelf - it is warped and only 3 corners touch the frame of the shelp. The fourth corner is up in the air. That really turned me off this product more than anything else. I used those thin Styrofoam sheets which come in amazon boxes to sort of pad under the wood so it doesn’t wobble much when you place items on it.

Amazon has a good product which could be a huge hit, but they botched the most important part - the level wood base. Poor quality control results in a great product being very average.

Despite the wood shelf, I give it 4 stars because it is a really good product.
