title: The Over-the-Door Double Hooks from AmazonBasics Keeps Clothes and Towels off the Bathroom Floor!
text:
I like the Over-the-Door Double Hooks from AmazonBasics. I easily hung it over the door in my bathroom. I call it “my” bathroom because it is located on the third floor of my condo. My personal bedroom, my private office, and one guest bedroom are located on this floor. I share this bathroom with relatives, guests, and my girlfriend, Tammy. Normally, I just lay dirty towels and whatever clothes I’m changing into on the bathroom floor. Now I can conveniently hang them up. I’ve used the Over-the-Door Double Hooks on my door for over a month. The door shuts fine. It is a little tight within its frame but that is acceptable. It doesn’t take a great deal of strength to shut the door. The children in my household (my grandnephew, Tony, and my grandniece, Dani) can shut it without difficulty.

The Over-the-Door Double Hooks hasn’t damaged my door. The tips of the hooks are covered with rubber. Also, and most importantly, the over-the-door saddle has a padded backing. This device has never fallen off the door. It does not swing dangerously from side to side. It is very sturdy and stable. My parents have a similar device hanging in their bathroom. However, it has only one hook and they use it for displaying a beautiful wreath. Because of pets and children and allergies, I don’t have time to clean a wreath. (Everything in my tall, skinny condo has to have a specific function.) I am glad there are two hooks instead of one. I can see where this would be very useful in other rooms such as the children’s bedrooms and the laundry room.

Personally, I felt that I could get the most usage out of the Over-the-Door Double Hooks from AmazonBasics in my own bathroom; fortunately, I was correct. It does keep my bathroom looking tidier. (Now, if I could only get someone to come in and scrub the sink, toilet, and bathtub once in a while.) The Over-the-Door Double Hooks would make a nice present for a student living in a dorm where space is limited. Anyone living in a cramp one-bedroom apartment, like I once did, would also appreciate this device. Furthermore, I would like to add that it arrived safely and protectively packaged in Amazon’s Frustration Free packaging. Overall, I highly recommend the Over-the-Door Double Hooks from AmazonBasics.

title: Perfect Addition for Coffee Lovers
text:
[[VIDEOID:66343c72bb056fc731e5e6eea1d80997]] I have the handheld froth but this is much better and create less mess. I can easily froth cold milk (like I did in the video) then warm it up for a few seconds and pour it into my cup to make my coffee (which is what I did in the picture). The froth increases as the milk warms and the cleanup was super easy. I’ve used it more than I’ve used my handheld frother though I’ve owned the handheld one for about 3 years or more now. I find my coffee taste better frothing the milk and I love the idea that I can make it warm while retaining the froth. I accidentally left the milk to warm for several minutes while I attended to my toddler and I thought the cleanup of the dried milk on the bottom of the container would be a pain to clean. To my surprise, cleanup was easy and I didn’t even need to soak it.

Unlike the handheld frother, there will never be flying milk because you held it incorrectly and you don’t have to hold anything. You simple pour the milk in, place the cover on and press the button. Within a few seconds your milk is froth and it even warms your milk either before or after the frothing process. How much easier can it get. I absolutely love this thing and highly recommend it for its simplicity! A great product to add to your kitchen for my coffee lovers.

This is a support under the drawer and the pilot holes were completely off on one side, fine on the other. This edge should not be sticking out. It needs to flush just like the other side. As a result, the drawer does not push completely in. I cannot drill new holes because they're too close to the other holes and because of the cheapness of the pressboard the holes I would drill would merge with the bad ones. Also, the customer should not be expected to correct the errors of the manufacturer. The stand itself is okay but be wary of poor alignment.

title: Great chair, but short people are going to need a foot rest
text:
We’ve been going a bit nuts buying new office chairs lately, since with multiple folks in IT and working from home suddenly due to the pandemic, we discovered that our home office chairs, while good for an hour or two or three a few times a week, were totally not adequate for 8-12 hours five days a week. While my husband had back problems and pain, my daughter started having more headaches and migraines. When we looked at her old home office chair, we saw the problem immediately. It was sincerely old and all the padding was kaput.

So, we needed a chair with a lot of padding, good back support, and a lot of padding. I mention padding because, well, she’s overweight but she also has sensory problems due to Asperger’s/SID/ASD/autism and she has to have a chair that feels just the way she wants it to. There is no tolerance for any sensory input/discomfort. So we way overbought for her weight to make sure that the padding was just right or even excessive.

Also. The child is vertically challenged. As in short. With short legs even for a short person. (I blame her Dad’s genes. She’s got Grandma written all over her.) She’s 5’ 3 ½” and has to wear petite pants. (When she was younger, I bought her capris to work as full-length pants, although that has improved somewhat. Just to put the whole height thing in perspective.)

Overall, this is the perfect chair that we were looking for so she would have all the room and depth that she wanted, all the padding, all the comfort, but it was too tall. So we compensated for that by putting a footrest under her desk. Problem solved, but not the most elegant way.

I wish they offered a version of this for petite people. But overall, she is very pleased with her chair now that we’ve gotten a footrest of the correct height to make up for it being too tall. So I can’t knock a chair for said child unit being short and having even shorter legs. I’m 5’ 4 ½” – so one inch taller than she is, but my legs are a couple of inches longer. The chair fits me just fine, although I might want lumbar support if I sat in it a long time, since the seat is deeper than I prefer. But at my height, my feet touch the ground completely when the chair is at the lowest height. It also fits my husband with a higher seat adjustment, as he’s just shy of six feet tall.

The lumbar support, the padding, everything else is really nice. Way better than I would expect for the price range of this chair. Overall, a nice chair that is making working at home during the pandemic a lot more comfortable and less migraine-inducing. You can’t beat that!

As the parent of kiddos with autism, there are causes near and dear to my heart. Let Amazon donate to your favorite charity! Use Amazon Smile (smile.amazon.com) when you order and Amazon will donate to the charity of your choice when you make a qualifying purchase. Check out how Amazon Smile works at https://smile.amazon.com/gp/chpf/about/ref=smi_se_rspo_laas_aas. My shopping is donating to my favorite charity, Canines for Independence at no cost to me. Awesome!

title: Easy assembly & comfortable, but uh...
text:
So I like this chair.. I ordered it because my old chair was giving me hip pain any time I sat in it for more than half an hour.. Mind you, I've been doing a lot of computer work from home lately. So half an hour doesn't cut it for what I need.

Nonetheless, this chair is doing much better. I haven't had any pain-related issues with it, although I do wish it had more lumbar support.
It is comfortable and plush, but not the kind you sink into and wonder if you'll ever find your way back out of. It's a great level for comfort.
The surface material is nice, it's a more-slick faux leather type of material, and that makes cleaning it a breeze if you ever happen to drop something on it, which can easily happen when you're eating at your desk.
The red accents are nice, I understand it's for a gaming-style office chair... But I'm not sure why anyone would specifically desire that? I guess it's a nice change from traditional office chairs? There's nothing wrong with it, it's just strange to me.
I have noticed that the wheels definitely roll quieter than my previous chair, so that's nice for late-night work when my family is sleeping.

I do have 3 primary issues with this chair. 2 of which are actual issues in my opinion, not just personal preference.
1), [Personal Preference] The "sleeve" that covers the main gas-cylinder just rests on it as a telescoping 3-part plastic piece. It rattles around and is very unfinished-feeling to me. I've had other office chairs with this exact piece before and never have liked it. But again, personal preference. This doesn't actually affect my rating.
2), The main gas-cylinder only sets into the wheel-base and the chair seat. There is absolutely NOTHING holding it in place, other than your butt assisting gravity to keep it set in it's little spot. Yes, it sets down into it, but nothing bolts it in place. If you pick this chair up (fully assembled) by the arm-rests, the whole thing could fall into 3 pieces (wheel base, gas cylinder, and seat). I did confirm that the directions do not show any way to firmly-secure this. It just shows them being seated into each other (no pun intended). There were also no spare parts that could have been used for this. I used all of the parts according to the directions without spares. In all fairness, it has not fallen apart of me, but I haven't tried to tempt it.
3), There is NO reclining ability in this office chair. Oftentimes, you can pull the handle out to unlock the ability to recline in office chairs. This is not the case here. In fact, the end of that rod/handle (for lowering the chair height) just popped off completely.. Turns out it's not secured in any way either. It slipped right back on, sure. But I feel like this chair is made very cheaply, and not functionally.

Given issue number 2 & 3, along with the fact that it has extremely minimal lumbar support, I have deducted 2 stars. It is a solid 3.5 stars for me, but I'm not able to give half-stars.

Also, I do not know what this chair costs. When we are given the ability to test and review these items, sometimes they are not live on Amazon. This chair is not, so I do not know the price. If it was less than $60, I would probably give it 4 stars. But if it's $100 or more, then it definitely stays at 3 stars.

title: Unique feature helps save nat gas
text:
I could almost qualify as a small electrical space heater test engineer. I have five of these heaters of various vintages and designs. One of them is 20 years old with no safety features. Turns out that old one is the best of the lot until this one came along. The problem I have had is the small safety shut off on the bottom. It is a very good feature but poorly implemented. Most small heaters these days have a spring loaded button which is depressed when the unit is placed on the floor. If the unit is tipped over the button springs out and turns the unit off. These buttons are fairly small diameter and if the surface is not rock solid the button will not properly depress and the unit will not function. This heater has a small round plate on the bottom of the button which provides more surface area so the button will engage when the unit is placed on a tightly woven throw rug in you living room for example. We have solar panels and excess power at the house. Instead of turning on the gas fired central heating for our house we will set this guy up in our living room and watch TV nice and cozy with this heater at our feet. But our throw rug has defeated the other models. Not this one.

I have also observed that the plug and cable do not heat up as they do with other units. You do notice some warming, but unlike others it does not seem like the cable and plug are on the edge of thermal runaway.

Great unit so far at a very reasonable price....inflation fighter.

text: I love these beautiful pans but quickly realized cooking with them was a learning experience for me, it is quite different than using the so-called non-stick variety. Once I learned how to properly prepare (heat) a stainless steel pan or pot for the type of food I was cooking things got a lot easier and my cooking became fun again. The strongest point that this cookware gives you is consistent and even heat distribution, no hot and cold spots from corner to corner. If you're cooking on high heat such as pan searing,wait until your pan is properly heated before you add the oil and food item. Once you add the food item LEAVE IT BE, be patient until the heat causes it to release from the pan.  If you follow the rules the clean-up of stainless steel will be surpisingly easy as well.

UPDATE 6/28/2020: My original was written shortly after I purchased it. After having this chair for 17 months I need to do an update. On the plus side, the chair is big, no huge, fits big people very well. The construction is heavy duty and built to last. If you are a tall person even better. With the shock absorber at top height, it sits tall for a chair. The shock absorber is very heavy duty. I am a tall and big man. I set the chair to the maximum height setting when it was new and has remained there for 17 months and it still holds me up without ever once slipping down. Being a tall chair, it makes it very easy for me to get in and out of.

On the negative side. It could use more padding in the seat. The only other negative is the leather cover is low to mid quality. Pieces of it are flaking and chipping off all over. The cover is in tact, the flaking leather is just a cosmetic issue. Overall, the two negatives are not enough of an issue to remove any stars.

title: So versatile.
text:
Maybe I've been living under a rock but I had no idea these nifty electric steamers even existed. I thought the only way to steam vegetables was on the stove top or microwave and I didn't really care for either option. I know steamed food is a much healthier option, so I was pretty happy when I came across this.

Once this arrived, I hoped online looking for steamer recipes. There are so many foods that can be cooked in a steamer. I was pretty blown away. As I was looking, I started to get intimidated. The consensus I came to, was that it's really easy to mess up a meal and overcook stuff until you get the hang of it. I don't have time to chance overcooking a meal, so I put it back in the box with intent to try it on some rainy day. Eventually, I got around to trying it out. I know you can cook entire meals on this but I decided to start off with mixed vegetables. I watched it like a hawk and the vegetables came out great, like restaurant quality great. I didn't find much online for recipes but I did learn that you can substitute the water with beef or chicken broth and even beer. It's recommended to save the juice and to pour it on for added flavor. I'm still looking for recipes if anyone wants to share them in the comments.

As for this steamer, I love how vegetables come out. The multi tier trays allow you to cook multiple items at the same time. You don't have to worry about burning food and cleanup is really easy because after all, it's steam that's doing the cooking.

I would definitely recommend this and look forward to experimenting with it.

title: My experience
text: I wanted to love this table. Pros: the design and aesthetic are visually appealing. The shade of wood finish is also a nice nod to traditional shades of mod walnut wood if you appreciate that design era. Cons: I did not find the table to be sturdy enough to be practical for my intended regular use serving a guest their beverage chair-side for convenience and comfort; this is due to the light materials used. Other Rivet furniture pieces I have from Amazon that are stabilized by metal bases are much weightier and stable as they all are made of iron or steel metal. However, this particular table is very lightweight and does not have any of the weighted stability or longevity one can find in upgraded metals like iron and steel; this table has a coated aluminum or other lightweight alloy base. Additionally, the wood top of this table is a softer species stained to give it a walnut-like aesthetic. If you intend to use this table for it’s looks alone, I can recommend it. But if you want a sturdy functional table that won’t be easy to knock out of position, spill a beverage, or knick and scratch the wood, this particular piece of furniture may not best meet your needs. title: Great containers, but use caution when microwaving with lid
text:
PROS: Leak proof, stacking (w/lids off), doesn't retain odors or stains (even red sauces), easy to open/lock (and I have a bad hand tremor), durable after 3 years of light use, clear so easy to see inside, nice for small items and the 4.2 cup (1liter) is perfect for me.
POTENTIAL CON: not really a "con" but you should be aware of likely damage (copied from 2019 review by user MADE.IN.BKLYN, wish I'd remembered):
here is a tip I learned the hard way from my little microwaving lunch FAIL...Be careful when heating these in the microwave! Remove the top completely, don't just loosen. Don't recover/re-lock (using locking top) your food directly after heating. Turn the top upside down with the lock fasteners facing up or cover with a paper towel between the container and the lid. The lid will seal and create and air tight vacuum that will permanently warp the shape of the container.
If you're really determined to get your food out after it has pressure sealed from the heat, you can puncture the leak proof sealing ring on the lid (not easy but doable if you're hungry enough) which ruins the seal. This is not a fault of the container - I should have known better. Other than this, I highly recommend this set.

title: Shipped twice, once with missing parts, second dented base.
text:
Took a while to get the first order of this chair. Probably waited 3 weeks. Once it got here started to assemble only to realize it was missing wheels and base support. Created a return ticket and UPS picked it up from my house a week later. At the same time, Amazon stated they would send me a replacement, which I finally got 2 weeks later. So I am at 5 weeks from the order date.

After unboxing replacement noticed a large dent in one of the base arms. It is mainly cosmetic so will let it pass.

The biggest issue for me is that it is just not that comfortable and has no back support. I am 6 ft and 200lbs. I think the chair is intended for someone taller and much heavier. Even at the lowest setting my feet barely touch the floor. Also, it is VERY wide and the seat is deep. It could easily accommodate a very large person, but not exactly built for my build. The lower back area really doesn't have support although the product description says it does. Maybe for a taller person, it would feel more supported, but I can't judge that.

Installation was a bit awkward, but not a big issue. The manual states when assembling leave all screws loose until the final step. The way the seat back metal plate goes under the base plate is very odd, you really need to play with all the positions until the armrests are in. Two people would really help in the install, but I was able to do it myself. Pinning the chair against a wall for the armrest fit helped. Everything is quite heavy as well. That's a good thing but be prepared for that. Again 2 people would help. The cylinder that connects the chair to the base has no anchoring mechanism. Not the best design in my opinion.

The base also had a lot of aluminum scrap filaments all over it that are very very sharp. If you are bare feet be careful not to put your toes under it, or you might also consider filing them down first before assembly.

title: I'm super impressed with this $150 table!
text: I had some concerns purchasing this table given some of the negative reviews, but I wanted something made of real wood (which it is) and inexpensive (which it definitely is). After spending less than an hour assembling it, I have absolutely no complaints. The table is sturdy, attractive, and very functional. The only tiny qualm I have is that the sole plywood piece (which is the bottom of the lift top storage area) is a bit flimsy. We don't store weighty items there, mostly redundant remotes, game controllers, etc. so I don't see it being an issue, but there it is. Otherwise, this table is solid. I really like the locking function of the lift top; it makes eating or working at the table easier with no sway or instability. The table surface itself looks like a finger joint butcher block. I expect it to hold up well to everyday wear given that it is solid wood. I went with the natural color and luckily didn't find any scratches or marks. Overall, I'm extremely pleased with this table and would recommend it.

title: This Pan Made the Best Pizza I Ever Made
text:
I am a huge fan of homemade pizza, and I am a huge fan of cast iron. Before this fabulous pan came along, I had been experimenting with making deep-dish pizza in a cast iron skillet, and it was very very good.

Because this pan is wide open, you can preheat it before dropping the dough in, and this is a good thing. I preheated the pan, I dropped the shaped dough into the pan and let it toast in there for a minute or so. Then I added tomato sauce, pepperoni, caramelized sliced mushrooms, little mozzarella balls, and grated parmesan, and cooked it at the hottest temperature my lovely old Wedgewood stove has, until the cheese had melted and the pizza was a mass of bubbling temptation.

Divine. Possibly the best pizza I ever made... and I've made some pretty outstanding pizzas.

title: Commercial size, but not commercial quality
text:
This is a fairly large laundry hamper that requires assembly and should take about 10 minutes. However, I have 2 issues with this laundry hamper. First, there was a manufacturing defect so one of the holes was drilled on the wrong side of the vertical pipe that the lower circular piece connects to. I drilled my own hole but it doesn't look great and normally I would return the product for a new one but I wasn't able to for this review. So I made it work. Check to make sure all the holes are drilled correctly before assembling.

My second issue is this laundry hamper is basically made of hollow, thin aluminum tubing. It holds together fairly well for a home laundry hamper, but it will likely fall apart in a few months in a real commercial setting. The wheels are nice and large and it rolls well on hard flooring, and decent on carpet, depending on thickness.

I'd only recommend this for home use or in a corporate/commercial setting where it isn't going to get banged around a lot. If you expect to roll this across the room and hit a wall like people sometimes do with commercial products, this isn't going to last. But it's been working well for my family's laundry. It really holds a lot compared to the average household laundry hamper, and I had to clear out some space in my closet so it would fit.

One more minor issue is that while the hamper included an Allen wrench key to tighten the bolts, they did not include a wrench for the lock nuts on the lower portion, and you can't hold it by hand. The Allen key stripped on me halfway through and I had to use my own tools to finish the assembly. The whole situation just wasn't good and this is definitely not a very high quality product overall.

title: An interesting juxtaposition of wood and steel.
text:
This unusual occasional table was super easy to put together with just the included machine screws and a Philips screwdriver.

The table arrived with an unsightly scratch. It had just the standard one-spray-coat of factory finish, which is very thin.
We decided to put another three coats of finish on the table to protect it from additional nicks and chips, as well as from water rings.
We used a spray varathane satin finish, to match the original finish as closely as possible.
The additional coats did help hide the scratch.

The table is man-made wood composite, with a very thin veneer of real walnut round end grain, 1/16 of an inch thick, or less.
Of course the rim of the table is composite wood, as mentioned, but it has been given a credible “live-edge” look that is currently quite popular.
(This is a rustic-modern style, where the wood appears to have had the bark removed, with no further refining.)
The rim contrasts nicely with the more refined appearance of the top.
The table is well-built with a black painted steel frame, heavy enough to remain stable, without being unwieldy.
The style of the table is striking and is certainly a matter of taste, but if you like the look, it would fit well in either a cottage-type setting, or in a more formal one.

title: Exactly as advertised, pleasantly surprised!
text:
I ordered this for an office with a bit of skepticism, as there weren't reviews and it's a rather unknown product. It arrived expeditiously, well packaged and well delivered with no damage to the container or contents. It's heavy, but not too heavy for 2 guys to haul around. Has a nice real wood frame (not particle board) and a very nice feeling fabric/velvet.

The parts for assembly are in a package hidden in a compartment on the bottom (inside a zipper). The zipper for the compartment was pretty poor, but serviceable. The actual "Assembly" consisted of bolting on the 5 main legs with a single bolt each and 2 screws each (which screw into the interior wood framing) - a screw gun is handy for that. A central support leg under the middle of this sofa also gets screwed in. The included accent pillow/cushions (the rectangular blue ones in the pics) are of decent quality.

The legs themselves are a very nice heavy solid cast type metal in a matte gold/brass type finish. The velvet is extremely soft, seems to be durable so far and miraculously doesn't hold pet hair at all. We have a small white dog at work that sheds all over and the hard just wipes off of this sofa. The arms and back are also cushioned nicely, and the back provides a reasonable amount of support. I've already had several people sit on the arms with no ill effect.

The color is fairly accurate to the pics (perhaps slightly darker). The cushion support would be classified as medium firm, but not overly hard. It's comfortable to lay down on, but if you're over 6' tall you can't completely stretch out.

Overall a very nice sofa for the money - guests are impressed by it and it fairly easily competes with other much more expensive pieces we have. Our experience is positive and I can positively recommend this sofa.

title: Looks authentic
text:
For years I was on the lookout for one of those arched, multi-pane window frames at antique shops just so I could add a mirror behind it and create this piece. If I did happen to come across something similar, the wood was usually in such bad shape, I couldn’t justify paying the price being asked. When I saw this Stone and Beam mirror, I grabbed it quick! It has that worn, weathered whitewash look I was searching for. And it’s huge. I mean really huge. Check your space with the measurements in the listing because it does take up a good bit of room.
I was going to hang it in my extra room, but due to the weight, I decided to lean it on top of a shelving unit instead and I will secure it to the wall with some wire later. Please forgive the random decor. That room needs to be redone badly and I’m hoping this piece will inspire me to get to it. It was gray and raining outside when I took the photo, but on a sunny day, I think that mirror will draw more light in and help brighten it up.
The shipping box was in perfect condition, none of the packing inside was damaged, yet there’s a crack in the wood on the upper right side of the frame. I thought this was part of the vintage look at first, but the crack goes around the edge as well. I wonder if this didn’t happen at the factory. Thankfully it kind of goes with the rustic, vintage theme, but I do worry about it cracking further at some point.

title: Useful collection of nicely sealed food saver containers, can save money and waste.
text:
I'm single, I lament the way most things are geared towards friends and families. It's hard for instance, to buy a individual size pizza, a single phone plan or other things without running up the cost. I make a lot of sandwiches, bake my own pizza, and make casseroles at home often. I gain too much weight having to eat most of the 4-6 servings of most things in a day, so it's good to have something to store. It also makes it faster to make a nice sandwich. Here I can wash lettuce, slice tomatoes, slice a block of cheese, and store for future use. I can save other things like cooked bacon, leftover mac and cheese, plus many other cooked foods.

There is a nice array of sizes and these all seal well with the four locking tabs. No air gets in and no liquid can get out, so the food can last longer. Small containers I find are great for storing hotdog chili or open chip dips. Larger ones can deal with leftover pizza, casseroles, lasagna, or homemade bread. You can use the middle ones for premade sandwiches or like I do to store the fixings for making a nice BLT club sandwich. They also work well to store just made tuna salad for your sandwiches or salads. If you juice they work well for fruits and can make they last longer and resist mold better as they are fairly air tight. Inexpensive, with better than average quality. Recommended.

title: Expensive but nicely printed mural on layered wood.  You need a proper plan to hang these right, check for 16" on center studs.
text:
I saw a comment that these are tricky to hang, but that does not have to be the case if you think it out first. My method worked as follows: I measured down from the ceiling and made several tick marks and drew a very light pencil line between them across the top. Next, I marked the keyhole (place to hook headed nail or screw) in the back of the panel by measuring. I measured where the keyhole position was relative to the top of the panel and checked to see if they were uniform (they were within about 1/32"). You will now need a stud finder. The standard 2"X4" or 2"X 6" studs in most walls is 16" on center, and coincidently that's the spacing of these panels. Now put three screws or headed nails at equal heights centered exactly 16" apart in the center of three studs. Measure down from the keyhole bottom to the next keyhole bottom, and leave about a 1/32" extra gap and put in the next set of screws or headed nails. Do the same for the bottom level. Now make sure to hang the bottom panels first in the correct pattern (bottom corners and bottom center piece). Do the middles next, and finally the top. The reason for this order, is that if you start at the top you won't have room to fit the keyhole, because the top will be in the way.

If you have an older or non-standard home, they might be 24" on center or something odd (if you do have that you can only use one stud). Given the weight of this artistic wall mural, you will want more support than just drywall. I recommend getting some angle iron pieces and mounting them at the bottom of the six panels you couldn't put the keyhole screw or headed nail in the stud. You should be able to offset to one more of the stud positions so you will have both sides supported. This will take some stress off the middle, and you can still use some angle pieces directly in just the drywall for extra middle support. This will be a bit more complicated as you can see if you don't have 16" on center studs, so you might check before you buy this art.

The art itself is a print on wood that has a fabric look, a nice highlight that goes well with wood tones, blues, greens and neutrals, but may contrast with reds, and yellows. Nice for a bedroom or even a den, but not recommended for basements, kitchens, or baths. Not recommended in high humidity areas of the home, I don't know how stable the print in or other than the layered wood if it's on a paper base. This is fairly expensive for basic patterns, so make sure you like what you buy, their are more to choose from. Recommended for the home decorator or handyman who likes to brighten up the duller walls in his/her home.

title: Broke during shipment.
text:
The mirror itself is gorgeous, sturdy & looks amazing in the bathroom we put it in. See my explanation below as to why I only gave 3 stars. If possible I would’ve actually given this order 3.5 out of 5.
We ordered 2 of these mirrors and based on the price they are now, it should’ve been a good deal!
When they came in, we completely opened one & found the glass shattered. The other one we opened the top, pulled it up a little & thought it looked fine.
On the first one, Amazon was great. They replaced it immediately & didn’t ask for the broken one to be returned. A few days later the new one came in in perfect condition. It wasn’t until then that we figured out that the 2nd from the original order was also cracked. This time Amazon wanted it returned which is completely within their right. But our printer was broken, this is a heavy bulky item & just didn’t seem worth the effort to try to send it back. As much as we spend at Amazon (a lot! Especially during holidays & this house build), with very few returns I kind of feel like they should’ve taken our word that it was broken especially considering the cost to them on returning it. But that’s their decision.
The missing stars are not for the mirror itself, it’s for the security of packaging for shipment. Two out of 3 being broken means you have a 33.3% chance of getting an undamaged mirror.
Again we were very pleased with the one good mirror. So if you have prime & like the mirror, by all means place that order! You can return it if something does happen. If you don’t have prime & have to pay for shipping, I’m not sure I would risk it.
If my review of this mirror has helped you make your decision please hit the thumbs up button. Thank you!

title: Holy cow this chair!
text:
OK, just to get some things out of the way I'm 6'1" and 350 lbs. I literally just got done putting this chair together, and I'm sitting in it right now writing this review. Let me say first that WOW! This chair is absolutely amazing. I previously had a Killabee gaming chair for almost 2 years and while it was comfortable at first, I was never very thrilled with it and it didn't seem to hold up very long. This AmazonBasics chair is an absolute game changer! Taking it out of the box I was immediately struck with how heavy duty and high quality the construction was. I did a lot of research on chairs before purchasing this one and I don't write many reviews but I felt compelled to say how good this chair really is. As soon as I had finished putting it together and sat down, I literally let out a big sigh. This chair is like sitting on a cloud. It hugs you in all the right places, and is the perfect size for a big/tall person. I seriously don't know how anyone can give this chair anything but 5 stars. As far as comparison to my old gaming chair, this chair hands down is the winner. It has a wider more plush seat, and a wider more plush back. It also sits at almost the exact same height as the Killabee big and tall gaming chair. GET THIS CHAIR! You won't regret it.

PROS: very comfortable, lots of cushion, high quality construction, relatively easy to put together, very ergonomic, head rest feels like a pillow you would sleep with, bonded leather feels high quality, sits at a great height, can tilt

CONS: Armrests not adjustable, no recline (only tilt), no adjustable lumbar support (although it does have great lumbar support) -- as you can see the only cons I can find are the adjustability. Everything else is 5+++ stars.

TIPS ON PUTTING IT TOGETHER: I read a lot of reviews on this chair and many others and it seems people always have difficulty putting these types of things together. It took me roughly 30 minutes and while it wasn't difficult it definitely wasn't enjoyable. I put it together myself using the box it came in as a prop to hold the chair up while I put it all together (there is a diagram of this in the instruction manual). So it can be done by yourself if you are smart about. Although the chair is heavy, when you putting it together the heaviest piece you will have to lift is the seat bottom which is only about 10-15 pounds. Also when putting it together make sure you leave ALL bolts somewhat loose (don't tighten down) until everything is put on then you can start tightening bolts. Do that and you definitely won't have any issues putting the armrests and etc. on.

What are you waiting for... BUY this chair already!!!

title: Mine came incompletely assembled
text: Ordered this little guy heater, It had 2 screws rattling around and the fan was moving around inside. Sent it back, got replacement, exact same issue. No quality control anymore? . I decided to not return it, just fix it. If you are in the same boat as me, UNPLUG FIRST! remove 4 screws on the back. take apart. Remove the next 4 screws holding the insides to the back piece. Flip over with radiator facing up. pry up carefully. install the 2 loose screws in the back of the fan motor assembly. reassemble and plug in and go. After the repair it is working great! I will not buy this product again. If you plug in with loose screws and fan motor this could be a serious fire hazard.

Pros: Great price, light weight, keyholes for hanging are level and evenly spaced, easy to hang. Fast shipping with prime and packaged very well.

Cons: It has a composite frame which wouldn’t have been a big deal if made correctly. The angle of the cuts are off, not allowing them to line up properly, which caused gaps in 3 of the 4 corners.

I can’t decide if I should return it or try to use a filler and black paint to fix it. The gaps are just so large that I’m nervous I’ll mess it up more.

text: First: the kitchen rack works and looks as advertised. It fits very well in our small kitchen. It's sturdy enough for a microwave, kitchenaid mixer, and other misc kitchen items. The only drawback was assembly. I opened the box to a complete mess. Tiny bits of styrofoam everywhere. Plastic pieces loose-leaf out of their packaging rolling around in the box. One of the metal "rings" attached to a rack that slides over the poles was slightly warped / not circular. Rubber mallet did the trick, but I was worried for a minute because it didn't glide smoothly over the pole like the other rings. Product was cheap and works *very* well in our kitchen, but the total manufacturing and packaging process must have taken less than 4 minutes. Just a small amount more quality control and it would have been 5 stars.

title: First one was a dud, replacement was as well.
text:
Ordered this to keep a well house above freezing. First one arrived on time but something was rattling around inside the case and the fan did not move. Got on chat with a live person and was happy to learn that they would replace it with no problem. Just got the second one today, but unfortunately this one had the same problems. Returning and looking for a different one.
Edit - After going through the process of setting up a return for the second one I got curious and took the heater apart to see if I could find the problem. I found that of the 2 screws holding the fan one was missing (the one rattling around loose) and the other was backed out about 3 turns from being tight. I tightened the loose one and returned the missing one to its place and the fan then moved freely. After putting things back together I was happy to note that everything worked as it should have. I will not be returning this after all, but if you are not comfortable with or do not want to take the time to make this sort of repair I would not recommend purchasing.

title: MAJOR delivery problems
text:
Ugh, i hate to be the first super negative review but let me clarify that this is not about the actual couch, but about the TERRIBLE DELIVERY. My couch was supposed to be delivered TODAY. I live in a NYC walk-up. So I had to coordinate with my neighbors to help me remove my old couch as well as clear the hallways so that there is plenty of room for the delivery guys. According to tracking, my item reached the great state of IL on Tuesday (today is saturday) which is PLENTY OF TIME for it to arrive to me by today. The XPO delivery company did a search and located the item as STILL SITTING IN ILLINOIS!! WTF?? I just moved the entire front half of my apt to make room for the couch to come in (tiny nyc apts require a lot of strategy) and my neighbors are all now holding up their own plans for the day bc of this. Complete flakiness. XPO is saying it's Amazon's fault and Amazon is saying it's XPO's fault. Meanwhile this flakiness has impacted more than one person and interfering with my work schedule. Epic fail, Amazon/XPO. Very disappointed and burdened.

UPDATE: Amazon re-shipped a new couch to me and this one arrived smoothly and in mint condition. The brass legs are real heavy/sturdy brass legs and took a lot of hand strength to screw them into the bottom, but I appreciated how sturdy they felt. The seat is more on the firmer side while the back cushions are more robust. BUT, still all very comfortable and quite beautiful. It appears larger in person than in the pictures somehow. I'm very happy with the purchase and hoping this lasts a long time! I also noticed the price just went down! Missed out on that one, but it's ok - the couch would still be double the amount on West Elm or something. Worth the trouble and cash :-)

title: If you want your office chairs to stop breaking/warping, buy this one.
text:
I am not particularly big or tall (5'11" 220lbs) but I have a bad habit of "jumping" into my chairs (or so I'm told), and they start to lean or break relatively quickly.

I gave it a while with this chair, and it (so far) shows absolutely no signs of wear, and has not lost a smidgen of it's integrity. It also has exceptional padding on the back and headrest. Overall, sitting in it feels quite good.

If I had to give a few criticisms for daily use, I'd have to cite that the base arms (that attach to the wheels) are a little rough around the edges. A couple times I had hit the base of the chair with the back of my feet and it FELT like it had cut me, but not so. It's rough, but apparently not sharp enough to break skin (for me), so could be worse? A little deburring never hurt though, and I'd recommend the manufacturers to improve this.
Also, the arms of the char feel Terrible if you have sharp elbows (I do). There is VERY little padding on the arms of the char, and that was surprising given the target demographic of the product. Like, I can get used to the arms being quite far apart, but I have to stack small pillows on them to make them usable for long periods of time. I currently have a solution coming to me in the mail (but due to current pandemic issues won't be here for another month).

Also, if you get this char, then you'll want to lightly install the bolts, and then re-tighten them occasionally over a couple of days.

Overall, it's exceptionally well made for the price, and if they'd just give the arms a little more padding, and the base a little refining, then I'd give it 5/5. Right now, it definitely could be worth it (depending on your situation).

title: great chairs!!
text: I shopped around at other sites before buying 2 sets of these chairs. They are a great price and for the quality, I think they're better than brand names I may get marked down somewhere else. Design elements are the same as high end furniture brands at a fraction of the price. These are way better than something you'd get for the same cost at Big Lots or another cheap store! The cushion is thick and quite supportive and comfortable, I love them. I got them to replace the old bulky chairs I had in the last photo. They will look nice at my holiday table this year! I like them so much I may get 2 more pairs for more seating. They are light and the box itself was not heavy with both chairs inside. As can be seen in one of my photos, the chairs are inside the seat! Amazon thought of everything and they were so easy to put together, your 10 year old could assemble them. The chairs are safely transported and the only tool you would need is a scissor, as the allen wrench is included along with all hardware! I had set aside my morning to assemble them, and boy it was so simple. Take out the legs, screw them in and boom! It is foolproof, all the legs fit in the same way and all the pieces are the same. Just follow the picture and it's all you need. Compared to other self-assembly kits, all the hardware was cut exactly the same, all smooth and fit the holes perfect. There was nothing missing from any of the kits. Note: the washer is flat and unfinished on one end, and the smooth side I put outward toward the hole, so it would be less scratching on the wood. Perhaps it wouldn't make much of a difference, but I'd advise it. I had no problem with holes not lining up or any legs being one length versus another! I did notice on one of the "C" legs, a nail was slightly sticking out so the leg didn't lay quite flush in the slot. It didn't make much of a difference as you can still screw in the legs to the holes  it would just be a little tighter to work in. I think the chairs and beautiful and I'm very pleased. Maybe they look sort of "short", but the height is right when you sit down for most seated persons, ergonomic and measurements appropriate. I kept one of the boxes for storage of some things, and I would suggest even if you aren't worried about having to return, keep the boxes as if you ever move, it'd be a cinch to put everything back up and transport in the boxes. Fantastic craftsmanship from Amazon, would definitely buy from this collection again.

Assembly is not too difficult. You use an allen wrench (supplied) to bolt the seat cushion into the legs. You can do it with the allen wrench but it's a bit tedious, I wish they had used bolts with hex or screw heads which would have been easier to turn. I used a (manual) driver with the right size allen key which made the job easier and quicker (I bought 6 chairs). You can use an electric driver but then you have to be careful of overtightening the bolts and splitting the wood. Right now newly assembled they seem sturdy enough. I will have to wait and see if the bolts need retightening after some use. This is a common problem with chairs of this type but not a deal breaker.

It's a little difficult to level the chairs for final assembly. They tell you to place the chair legs on a level surface like a floor and finish tightening the bolts. This means you have to get on the floor and crawl under the chair to access the bolts. I found it easier to place the chair (which is new and clean) on a flat table, push the seat cushion down so the legs are level and then, sitting in a chair, tighten the bolts from underneath. Much easier doing this sitting than crawling under the chair.

title: So close… Elementary mistake during manufacturing results in catastrophic mistake
text:
Now, I never write reviews, but I’m throwing 30 minutes at this review, because the solution for the manufacturer is so painfully obvious and inexpensive.

Story:
I plug it in, turn it on, and I smell that hot electrical smell, and the fan spins.. everything seems fine… but then, the fan starts making this ticking sound like it’s hitting the plastic body. Uh oh! Then, the fan just STOPS! But, the 1500watts of electricity is still flowing to the heater elements, getting that metal dangerously OVERHEATED without the fan to blow cold room air through it. I turn it off, shake it, and hear screws rattling, and the fan blades are bouncing around, like the screws for it came out!! No way, I think…. So much for the “safety”.

I return it, and get a 2nd one (the good reviews must mean I just received a one-off bad one, im just unlucky)….
Receive the replacement… Plug it in. SAME THING. Rattling screws… I’m flabbergasted… Wifey tells me to calm down…. I read some of the 1-star reviews and another gentleman said the 2 screws that hold on the fan fall out, but he fixed it and it’s good now. My wife is telling me we need to return this POS, but I forge ahead and open it up.

After getting all the screws out (4 on back - 4 for heater block - 4 plastic snapfits), I see the problematic 2 screws, that are supposed to hold the fan onto the body, just laying there in the plastic body…

My evaluation: This happened because fans/motors vibrate, so have the potential of backing out screws. This is why locking mechanisms are needed like locknuts, or Loctite—anything—for cars, motors, anything that vibrates.

So, I grab some Loctite, apply it to the the thread of the 2 screws, re-fasten the fan to the body, and put it all back together (making very sure the wires are routed far from the heater element). And now it works fine.

The product looks sleek - nice modern design.
The safety switch on the bottom of the unit is spring loaded, so if it were to fall over, this safety switch turns off… but this “great safety feature” is 100% bogus since they failed to think of all the different ways this could fail.

All in all, they could’ve made a good product had they put in their drawings/work instructions for their Chinese manufacturer to apply a couple small drops of Loctite to the 2 fan screws. Shame.. probably 1-10% (thousands?) of people are dealing with this same dangerous issue—read through the 1stars and you’ll see.

I’ll give it 2 stars because it was likely a single department’s (or person?) fault—but still, others on the design team should’ve caught this. Or processes in place to catch catastrophic failures like this…

TLDR: That mishap of not spending 5 more seconds per unit during manufacturing to add Loctite to 2 screws, destroyed its potential. Devil is in the details!

title: Am I using these hangers wrong somehow? 'Cause I didn't save space.
text:
"Be the reviewer you want to see in the world"-- that's what I'm going for here.

Tl;dr--
Pros: holds slippery or wide-neck items wonderfully, nice and uniform look, velvet did not rub off when tested, seems fairly sturdy
Cons: Does NOT save space as advertised (as compared to average cheap plastic hangers-- see photo)

The novel (soon to be a major motion picture):
A lot of folks here talking about how much more space they have show before and afters that look the the closet was rearranged and/or culled in the process. Which makes sense! You're touching every item to re-hang, why not reorganize, right? But for someone like me, who just has way too many clothes and needs better storage solutions for what they want to keep, this does not truly answer my question. So, when I bought these hangers, I controlled for all variables and did a perfect experiment that would make any science teacher proud: the very astute among you will notice that the items are even hanging in precisely the same order as in the before picture. The ONLY thing that changed was the hangers.

And friends, let me tell you: I somehow felt like I had slightly less space on my closet rod, if anything! Where did I go wrong? Now, granted, I did not have wooden hangers in this closet, or coat hangers, which are very thick. Most hangers were just the cheap plastic ones of average width.

Anyway, other than that, they're hangers. None of them that I used (half a box of 100) were broken or broke while I was hanging things, but I'm fairly gentle while hanging my clothes. I didn't try to swivel the heads. I do not know how they stand the test of time because I have only had them for three hours. I deliberately rubbed the ivory velvet on a knitted black sweater to see if it would shed and it didn't-- the inside of the delivery box is velvet-dust free as well. I didn't find any "bald patches" on the hangers, but even if I had, they're hangers, who's gonna look? They hold pesky items that like to fall off very well, and they look nice.

title: Good grip, pointy tips.
text:
The velvet has really good grip. The hooks have smooth rotation and are securely installed. They have a narrow profile comparable to a pure wire hanger.

The tips on some of them can be a bit pokey. They won't draw blood, but they might fray a delicate fabric like rayon or lace if you aren't careful putting it on the hanger. This may vary by batch, and you could probably smooth them down with a dremel if it will be a problem for you.

They are also somewhat bendy/springy compared to wire hangers or most solid plastic games. For me this is a big plus that makes me likely to buy again, as it allows me to easily hang shirts that have tighter necklines without having to feed the hanger in through the body or sleeve, but if you're going to put a lot of weight on them like a heavy winter coat, you may want to get something more robust.

title: Pretty good
text: Anyone familiar with “velvet” hangers knows they’re great space savers and awesome for hanging silky or wide neck items that tend to slide right off plastic hangers.  These are no exception.  I love velvet hangers and I’m not sorry I purchased these, but TBH... they’re a bit floppy.  I bought ‘em to save $$—I only use these for shirts anyway so I figured no big deal if they were missing the lower crossbar. To be clear, I don’t think the crossbar (or lack thereof) is the whole issue.  Years ago I bought similar hangers without a crossbar (from TJ MAXX, maybe?); I still have them and they are definitely better quality than these.  In retrospect, I’d probably pay a few bucks more for a sturdier option, with or without a crossbar.  That said, I still feel like these are a good deal if you’re on a tight budget and looking for light duty velvet hangers.  I’ve not had any issues with the black flocking rubbing off.  A few were broke upon arrival but I think that’s just par for the course with velvet hangers.  They’re awesome but not exactly the workhorse of the hanger world and I’ve had heads occasionally snap off of every velvet hanger batch I’ve ever purchased—regardless of quality/price.

Past AmazonBasics purchases had set my expectation that all products would be of equal or better quality than name brand, at a better price, regardless of what I might be buying.

I knew the moment I opened the packaging that these didn’t live up to that expectation. The density of the product gives me the impression it will be far less durable than reusable plastic grocery bags. The zippers were not on the same side and the zipper was closed, meaning I had to pull the teeth apart before using it for the first time. It ultimately zipped closed without issue but it left a bad first impression.

Handles on both sides don’t make these any easier to get under the bed, nor even back out. If the contents aren’t rigid, like clothes, they quickly bunch up on my low bed frame before I can get them under the bed. The bunching makes having handles on both sides, which seemed like a perk, pointless. They have to come out from the side they went in. I wouldn’t chance trying from the opposite side for fear of leaving all the contents under the bed when the bag shreds into pieces.

These aren’t sealed or airtight by any stretch. The contents will be exposed to anything that may be under the bed.

title: Best chair for the money if you are big fella
text:
This is a really great chair. I'm a big guy (400+) and was worried about finding a chair that fit, was comfortable and durable. It has been 10 months since purchasing the chair and I have some critiques.

First, know the chair is incredibly comfortable. I mean, you lean back and I honestly could fall asleep. Another thing I'd say is even at my weight, the castors are well made and heavy-duty. They roll free and are not easily stopped. Great for a big guy, like me. Moving up the chair, the 5-point base means not only is it a lot more stable than some chairs but because I'm heavy it helps to spread the weight over a larger area which is much better on your floors. The piston is a little disappointing. After about 2-3 months I found it would slowly lower and bottom out over the course of a few minutes. For me, it wasn't a big deal. But for some, it may not be tenable. The joining plate between the piston and the seat is top-notch. Really thick steal and a good size plate that isn't going to bend or break over time. I've been super happy with that feature. The seat has the perfect amount of cushion. I was worried it would compact over time and become uncomfortably hard, but so far that hasn't happened. The arms are good quality steel. But just make sure you tighten them properly or you may end up with structural problems as they provide part of the support structure for the back of the chair. Lastly, I did find the faux leather is a little touchy to scuffing and ultimately flaking. One corner of the arm on my would rub against the desk when I leaned back and would rock, contemplating some problem. I realized a little too late that was damaging the chair. Not really the chair's fault. But I thought I should mention it.

All in all, it is an amazing quality for the price. Honestly, I've never found anything so comfortable and sturdy for cheaper. If it completely fell apart after 2 years, I would have well gotten my money out of it.

title: The most comfortable chair I have ever had in my life.
text:
I am 6 feet tall, and weight somewhere around 300 lbs. This chair is the best chair I've ever sat in. The chair is **solid**. I assumed the legs/wheels thing would be chromed plastic--nope. Metal. The padding is thick and comfy. The back is taller than my head when I'm sitting (which is very rare for me). Every time I sit down, I am surprised again at how solid and comfortable it is. No joke, the day flies by now. I’m spending over 12 hours a day in this seat and I can really tell the difference.

I would recommend that when you put this chair together be sure to assemble the pieces before you completely tighten all of the screws. Professional assembly is not necessary. The screws are only 2 different sizes and the packaging comes with a set of Allen wrenches that are easy to use. I did have the most difficulty with the handles. You have to squeeze them to make the screws fit but it’s doable with a little elbow grease.

title: Don't buy from Amazon Warehouse - Unique gas lift
text: I bought this chair from Amazon Warehouse, with the only condition stated was that the packaging was damaged. The problem was that the base where the casters go only had the hole for the standard 2inch end of a cylinder.  I am assuming that since the larger cylinder fit into the chair's metal tilt base that the odd part out was the incorrect sized wheel base.  Amazon help wasn't a help as they don't do replacement parts for the chair, which means if the gas lift ever breaks, you are going to be SOL trying to find a new gas lift.  Also, since the inner rod is larger than standard, things like Chair Saver won't work.

title: Watch your heels
text:
I finally assembled it after about a month and a week, and it's about as difficult as an office chair is (I've assembled a couple of others in the past 2 years or so). The more annoying aspect was the alignment of the mounting studs for the arms - they didn't quite line up easily. Lost a scrape of skin trying to smash it together (it didn't work). Had to wiggle it around (follow the instructions when it says to not tighten all the way!) before I was able to coax the arms into their mount points. Once mounted and all tightened down, feels really solid and when sitting, I feel supported (I'm a moderatly bigger dude, just a couple pounds over 300) and comfortable.

Well, comfortable, until I smashed my right heel into one of the wheel arms. Yes, they are metal, but that's not the main point - it's the bottom part of the outer wheel arm, right above where the wheel attaches to the wheel arm (which by the way, loved the effort and eventual click of the installation - felt like I should expect they aren't going to fall out). It's not as... smooth, or rolled under, and therefore presents a bit of a sharper edge, which isn't the greatest. And if you unintentionally drag your heel against that edge, you will know it, and it'd be a good idea to ensure you won't get cut.

With all that, will I return it? Hell no. It's more comfortable than my last chair, by a good margin. I'll just need to adjust to the wheel arms being a bit longer than my last chair. Hurt heels ain't new to me (just finishing getting over an exercise-related blister on the left heel).

Also: There are two Allen wrenches included (M6, M8), but the contents-of-box listing indicates all screws are M8 - this is obviously false, as in the first step to work with screws indicates to use the 2x 'J' screws (M8 * 25mm) and 2x 'I' screws (M8 * 35 mm) with the M6 Allen wrench. Which doesn't quite make sense, but it is obvious that the contents listing is incorrect and the steps are correct, as the J and I screws use M6 heads - see the included pictures.

I bought a warehouse deal, and I really shouldn't have. The description was labeled as "repackaged." When I received the package however, the box had "damaged" written in giant sharpie letters. Me, being the fool that I am, opened the box to investigate. "Surely," I thought, "this is the warehouse code used for damaged packaging." I opened the box, tentatively, and I began to sigh in relief: everything looked to have factory packaging. I begin to set up the wheels, and lo and behold, there is a puncture in the leather. "Okay," methinks, "a puncture for a price discount is a trade fair enough." Oh, but oh no, I hadn't gotten to the best part. I begin to unwrap the lever, and what do I find? Oh, just your normal broken level tip encased in a pill bottle that read "meth" in the same sharpie as the box. Oh, it's just a meth chair. Nice, thanks Amazon.

To Customer Service's credit, they did issue me a refund and are having the chair picked up, but really? A report is being filed they said, but they didn't even want a picture. Like I am genuinely concerned. Cool, meth chair.

title: This is a big chair.  Too big for me.
text:
This chair has a lot going for it but still wasn't a great fit for me. I'm 5'8" and about 330 lbs. So I'm more on the big side, less on the tall. The good news is that the chair is plenty wide. I tried the Serta iComfort i5000 Big and Tall chair from Office Depot (purchased from Amazon but no longer available on Amazon) and found it to be well built and attractive, but surprisingly narrow. The actual seat had these metal bars underneath that pushed in on my thighs and were incredibly uncomfortable, and the lumbar support was too aggressive and felt like it was pushing me out of the chair. I was sad to send that one back as it was a really solid chair with some odd design choices that made it unusable.

This Amazon Basics chair is the opposite. It has a nice, wide seat with plenty of room for a big rear end. The problem I'm having is it's too big. The chair is simply too deep for my (apparently) short legs, and my feet barely touch the ground at the lowest setting. Also, the arms are really, really tall. So tall they don't fit under my desktop even on the chair's lowest setting. My desktop is just over 28 inches on its bottom side. So if I sit all the way back in the chair, I have to reach pretty far to get to my keyboard. It's an ergonomic nightmare for me. I've resorted to using a small pillow to push me forward in the seat to make it usable for a few days until I can return it.

I'm also not impressed with the cushioning on the seat. It's there, but I feel it bottoming out pretty easily and for extended sitting, it's just not good for someone of my size. The leather feels reasonably nice, but they use a lot of vinyl for parts of the chair that you don't actually sit on. For example, the tops of the arm rests are covered in leather, but on the sides of the cushioning it's vinyl. It's pretty obvious since they have slightly different finishes.
Not a deal-breaker, but that's how they can get to this price point. Finally, it's also creaky when I lean back. I haven't bothered problem solving on the creaks as it's going back so I'll be taking it apart tomorrow.

If you are more on the tall AND big side, then this may be a great choice at this price point. It's not a bad chair at all and feels pretty solid and looks pretty nice. For me, however, the search continues...

title: Wife approved
text:
I bought some of these reusable sheets a LONG time ago for my wife, and she didn't like them (the sheet absorbed heat and would make cookies hard on the bottom) and she forgot about them (probably threw them away - we were still dating at the time). She asked me to get her some reusable baking sheets and I said I got her some, and she didn't remember.

I measured her pans, and this was one of the few sets that had sizes very close to the pans she buys. if you are starting from scratch, it might be worth buying pans that are only half-sheet and quarter-sheet. Those are standards, even though they are very loose standards. I see a lot of comments, that do not measure before buying. Then the comments say "it's smaller than it looks!". Keep a tape measure around for online purchasing.

The amazon basics set was $8.22 for the 3 sizes. essentially: half-size, quarter-size, and something random which happened to fit my wife's baking sheet. She liked them a lot, and had no issues with anything she put on them cooking differently than the parchment paper. She asked me to get some more at the largest size (half sheet), as cheap as possible since she only needs them a few times a year for big projects. I found some branded "COOK TIME" that were 3 half sheets for $9.99. She said these were just as good as the amazon basics and she did not have any problem with the quality of either set.

title: Wood surface porous and not finished for food grade
text:
If came damaged but was part of the warehouse stock for a savings of $4.99. The metal of one of the racks was bent and also had a little light rust/deterioration of the chrome metal finish. The wood is NOT finished nor suitable for food prep, and is made of particle pressboard refashioned into a solid top piece, which also had defects of a few instabilities/splits where the wood is microfractured. So, if you are looking for a reliable surface for doing some real food work and need an appropriate wooden food-grade service, this, in my opinion, is NOT it, hugely based upon the fact that solid top surface pieces are used as standard in food production kitchens/industrial kitchens because of needing the ability to clean the wood surface without the surface being porous and absorbing food debris and harboring growing bacteria. The wood is barely finished, if you can call it that (it’s pressboard, what do you expect?) and I would have been happy to know it was pressboard before purchase. If you work with a decent wood cutting board upon this wood surface, or with a well covering pastry cloth before you do ANYTHING where the food could contact the surface (because it WILL easily stain and absorb food particulates and debris as it is very porous) then you’re going to be okay if that level of cleanliness isn’t important to you. Otherwise, a way KIND OF around this would be to do a heavy linseed/coconut oil sealing of this pressboard wood material (possibly a wax sealing first?) in order to ensure that wet materials and food stuffs would be repelled by the wood and the wood would be sealed and easily cleaned. After growing up in restaurants throughout my formative years and most of my adult life of working in food service, this is important. Fortunately I am using this piece as a spare craft table, which is pretty freaking awesome as a surface for the many random projects I have to occupy myself with. I intended to purchase this to hold canned foods and dishes and repurposed a bookshelf and metal rack instead.

Each shelf is only able to hold about $100 lbs, which makes this like a reduced scale pseudo-industrial rack as it doesn’t have the strength or thickness of metal usually found in the industrial versions of these types of metal rack pieces. If you need to store a lot of weight on this piece, I’d recommend a more sturdy version that may be more expensive of a model but that has a higher ranking weight bearing capacity certification. It’s sturdy, but thinly sturdy as compared to industrial grade racks, which are available on Amazon but that are NOT Amazon Basics brand.

title: Unbeatable quality for the price
text:
I was ready to be disappointed with a thin gauge poorly made pot that would be good only for making a lot of stock at once. I was VERY pleasantly surprised by the uniformly thick walls and bottom that are try-ply. I tested the bottom and lower sides for hot spots by making an Italian meat sauce. Even over high heat on my not great gas range there was no scorching or burning for the meat or the sofritto. I then turned the heat down for a slow simmer and again was happy that there were no burned too hot sides, this pot heats very evenly.

If there is one area that this pot lets you down it would be that the lid is not tight fitting and feels like an after thought. That said it is only disappointing when comparing it to all clad which for a stock pot this size is over 10x the price. (Not even an exaggeration). The lid still keeps the heat in and is sturdy enough for the job.

All that to say this is by far the best stock pot I can afford and even if I had the means I couldn't bring myself to pay 10x more for one that just has a better lid. I would call this a good deal for 5x its current $40 price. Buy it now before it costs much more or is taken off the market.

title: Design Flaws: Safety not Guaranteed
text:
This product was bought to warm a small space, it did that job well however it is lacking quality control and the safety features DO NOT seem to actually work. Unit started sparking, smoking, and almost caught fire, thankfully I was able to unplug it in time. Safety features did not turn of heating element.

The Amazon Basics Electric heater has a design flaw in which the power light cable is not properly routed around the heating element. Instead it is wired near and on top of the heating element its self. After some use the power light cable will begin to heat up and melt which can result in the copper being exposed. If this were (and in my case did) come in contact with the heating element it will cause a short. You can see in the photos that the cable was too tight and the cable was nearly touching the heating element to begin with. You can also see the scorch marks which go up the entire length of the element.

As a general rule electric heaters should not be left unattended, however this one especially so. Do not leave this unattended if you do buy it, be safe, get a product that will keep you safe. In addition the heating control does not disengage the heating element either, as best as I can tell it is always running just with no air movement (as the fan is off) which makes this even more dangerous..

title: Attractive Large Metal Object Shaped Like a Chinese Lantern; Flammability of Sisal at Top a Worry
text:
I was drawn to this item because I like old metal objects that look like they came from abandoned factories. The item looks pretty much like the picture. It is large and would hold a big pillar candle. The odd thing is, though, that, as pictured, the top rim and the handle are wrapped in sisal type cord. I am certain that this material is flammable, and I suspect that the wrapping on the rim, at least, could easily catch fire from any candle placed inside. I have therefore decided that I will use it as a planter for morning glories, hoping that they will entwine themselves through and around the many openings during the summer. If you intend to use it for candles, I would suggest removing the fiber at the top before doing so. Seems like a safety hazard to me if the sisal remains in place.

Another reviewer said that this item is a conversation starter. I am more worried that it will be a fire starter. Proceed with caution.

title: Not emf friendly, easy to clean
text:
Comes in a plastic housing so you basically have a 120hz emf emitting device. Most heaters are like this. I like to minimize my emf exposure so I just bought the Aroma Room ceramic heater B08FM9SLPB to replace my Amazon Basics ceramic heater which still works great. If you want to go emf friendly all the way, consider getting an electromagnetic shielding sleeve for the power cable. :)

Recently my Amazon Basics heater started smelling burnt and upon closer inspection, there was some hair stuck in the back by the fan. So I opened it and noticed there was hair on the fan shaft. It was very easy to take apart actually. All you need is a phillips cross-head screwdriver and take 8 screws out. The fan slides off the motor shaft / rod but since the fan fits the rod perfectly, it does take some effort to slide it out. Make sure to pull from the fan cylinder not the fan blades so you don’t break them.

Once I pulled the fan out, I noticed all the hair on the shaft. =D The hair slid right out too. I vacuumed the heating element and the rest of the innards and it works like new again.

I’ve had my Amazon Basics heater for over a year now and it’s worked great. I recently felt like purchasing an emf friendlier one which is why I bought the Aroma Room ceramic heater B08FM9SLPB. :)

title: Perfect window fan WITHOUT all the bells and whistles (and lights)
text: We have a 1925 one-and-a-half story cottage-style house with no air conditioning.  Our Iowa nights can get really sticky, especially with the bedrooms right up against the roof line.  I originally bought a pair of Bionaire Window Fan with Twin 8.5-Inch Reversible Airflow Blades and Remote Control - one for the front bedroom, one for the back bedroom.  If you do a search for "best window fan" this one seems to be everyone's favorite pick.  However, the buttons make a loud beep, you have to cycle through the buttons to change the speed of the fan and the direction of the fans.  It's nice to see the temperature display but it's a bright red LCD.  I only run the fans at night but I've already had to replace one of fan's fuses.  Honestly, I wish I had found the Amazon Basics fan first.  Fan speed is a standard off-high-med-low dial, fan reverses with a switch, and there's a built-in thermostat, but of the unmarked dial variety - all of which are SILENT!  If I want to change the speed or direction of the fan in the middle of the night, I'm not going to wake up my husband with a bunch of beep-beep-beeps and I don't have a bright red light shining in my face.  Otherwise, both fans have the same fan volume but the Amazon Basics comes with little swing out legs so I can take it out of the window and use it as a box fan PLUS it's lighter and less expensive.  I also like the way the cord comes out of the fan - it's got a little notch to keep the cord from getting mashed against the window sill.  I'm here to buy another two fans (so each bedroom has one) and then I'll put the Bonaire fans downstairs where the beeping and the lights won't matter so much.  The more Amazon Basic products I buy, the more impressed I am with the price and quality.

Even though the box said pre-seasoned, I seasoned the pan before using it. I also used a pastry brush to spread a little olive oil on the bottom before placing the dough and put it in a 400 degree F oven at the lowest rack position. 25 minutes later the kitchen was filled with the wonderful aroma of a pizza shop.

I worked in restaurants and bakeries and this pan produced the same quality crust as a pizza stone, but was much easier to use with no need for a peel or semolina that will get all over the bottom of the oven.

I made a scratch dough using a Bobby Flay recipe from the food network, but I don’t see why this pan wouldn’t work just as well with a frozen dough.

The pizza lifted right out of the pan with no problem, I put the pizza on a large cutting board because I didn’t want to cut it in the pan. After cooling, the pan cleaned up good as new with a little soap and water.

I can’t think of anything I don’t like about this pan. Amazon did a great job and I would recommend this pan to anyone who wants to make authentic carry-out pizza at home. I imagine this would also be a great pan for calzones, I am going to try that when the weather cools down.

I'm a little bummed that I got the older blue version, but just ordered the matte navy blue for myself, and the matte white for a friend.

Bottom line: this is a must-have kitchen item for novice cooks to serious chefs.

There are 3 sizes to this set. 2 Small, 2x3x2h.. 2 medium 4 ¾ x 3 x 2 3/8h .. and 1 large 6 ¾ x 4 ¾ x 2 3/8h, with each having a lid. The containers fit inside one another for compact storage.

Video from most of the professional chefs about mashing potatoes usually includes a suggestion and demonstration of using a ricer to mash potatoes instead of a masher. This masher has smaller than normal round holes which produces a ricer type of effect so the end result is probably pretty close.

The masher is 11 3/8 inches (29 cm) in height as opposed the image stating 12 inches (30 cm) and the head (where the mashing occurs) is an oval of 3.5 x 3 inches (8.9 x 7.6 cm).

I wanted this because of the softer material (a pretty strong nylon) in the event that it should ever be used in non-stick cookware.

title: Sturdy, attractive...BUT the knives rust
text:
Things we love about the set:
For the price - these have a great heft and stiffness. They won't bend easily. All the Forks & Spoons are 18/10.
Look pretty good too, nice shape.

The bad:
The knives are not 18/10. Of all the things! I think they are 13/10 or 13/00. After just two weeks of regular usage, including dishwasher time - the knife handles are starting to rust.

Sadly we're past the return window and now have to go shopping for new knives that hopefully match with this set.

Stone & Beam really needs to correct this in their production process and description. It is deceptive and dishonest to have the set labeled as dishwasher safe and rust resistant and then include sub-par knives...something that gets used just as much as the rest of the set. If they fixed this, the set would be a perfect fit.
