title: Easy
text:
This is easy to assemble, the instructions are simple to follow. It's mostly snapping major pieces together, with four nuts and washer sets to screw on the wheels with the included wrench. It's also easy to partially disassemble for storage. The push-button locking pins that join most pieces together make quick work of it.

In practice, this is a one-rod rack with an accessory rod in back that can be used for a few things turned sideways. The rods are too close together to use both normally.

Feels sturdy enough to hold the rated weight (over 100 pounds per rod) if it's spread out on the rack.

Maybe the best, most sturdy part is the almost 4" (3-7/8") caster wheels. They're big and strong enough to go across ground that isn't completely smooth without much trouble. The brakes work, so the rack stays put when it's supposed to. (The wheels are oddly smelly, but that's not any issue once installed.)

The rack is fairly stable, with a base that's almost 20" wide at the ground, but it can tip forward when you have the front rod filled and you pull on something. Not a bad idea to secure it to something with a strap or wire (insulated to avoid scratching) to keep that from happening. Or just be careful.

title: There is a trick to assembling the rack!
text:
After I figured out hoe to properly assemble the Baker's Rack, I am fully satisfied. It is a very good, sturdy, and functional storage addition to my small kitchen. One thing that stumped me about assembly: each of the bracket collars has a stamp on the outside showing which way goes up. Importantly, INSIDE each bracket collar is a small lip, or ridge closer to the top. This lip, or ridge, corresponds to the 'rings' on the support poles. Simply take one half of a bracket collar, place it on the pole just above one of the 'rings', and slide it down; it will snap/click into place. Then simply attached the other half of the bracket, and voila! After all four brackets are in place, when you slide the shelf unit down, it will catch on the bracket, and the shelf is in place. A small tap-hammer or rubber mallet is helpful to get a tight fit. A small portion of the bottom of the bracket will show, but that's OK with me.
I have about 80lbs of cast iron cookware on the bottom shelf; about 20lbs of finer cookware on the middle shelf and all holds well; it is VERY sturdy. On the top rack, I have very large jars of loose leaf teas, and I am not worried about anything falling over/collapsing.
This shelf unit works well with the Gorilla Grip Heavy Duty Shelf Liners; no trimming necessary- for me that is.
I hope this helps! I would recommend and buy again!

title: Bent and warped as heck
text:
TL;DR: This is a detailed review. I don’t ever leave bad reviews, because I’ve never really encountered a product I was disappointed with - - until now.
Upon receiving, the box wasn’t damaged at all, and it wasn’t until we unboxed and started inspecting that we noticed two of the shelves, and the hanging bar at the top, were extremely bent and warped.
One shelf in particular (one pictured with cartons and chip box) was so warped that it looked like the shelf was previously assembled, and someone more than 250lbs (weight capacity) tried to use it as a bench. It’s severely warped.
The plastic clips that are meant to clasp around the bars, to slide the shelves onto, were too small? They all wouldn’t clasp and clip into each other. It’s as though they’re not the right size.
I don’t imagine this unit will last long. I’ve since moved the heavier objects off of the shelf that is so bent, because I don’t trust it can handle the weight.
Why didn’t I just send it back, you ask? Well, I’ve learned from this experience that you should really pay attention to how something is packaged when you’re removing it from the box. I can’t figure out, and I just can’t take the time to figure out how to get in back in the box from where it came, so that I can seal it and take it to a drop off location. So, here it stays, unfortunately. Wouldn’t spend that $60 again on this product, and I don’t recommend.

title: Yeah ummm... What?
text:
[[VIDEOID:3c12d329d9cfa25d8e9c4b7a62d48851]] Lets start with the package that I received. It looked like the delivery man kicked it the entire way here. It was beaten to smithereens and half the box was ripped.

Upon opening the box, about half of the black caps that they put on for shipping purposes were broken. The parts themselves didn't seem all that bothered, but they were definitely knocked around. and not in the right places. The zip-tie that was supposed to hold something in place was completely busted before I even opened the package. Chances are, it was rattled a lot.

I love the chrome look and the feel of it in my hands but the four legs were not the same lengths. When I screwed the bottom legs all the way up on all 4 and laid them next to each other... They were all varying heights (within a half inch of each other... but they are legs, they should have been designed and engineered evenly)... So lining them up by the incremental markings wasn't a possibility because even if you were at the "4th from the bottom" they were still up to half an inch off each-other.

So I busted out yee ol' tape measure and got to work. Measured down, put the plastic caps into position, and slid my first rack on. Low and behold, the plastic slid down with the rack and it took several frustrating attempts to get it on the right way.

Fast forward, the rack is assembled and I go to place the wooden block on the top.

That block is warped from here to NASA's Mars Exploration Program.
It wobbles more than a see-saw. Not to mention that it doesn't line up right with the poles (possibly because it's warped). I'd be scared to place something on that wooden block with the fear that it would wobble off and break.

I'm going to be returning this product. Very... VERY... disappointed.

The pictures I'm posting with this show 1. What the bottom of the box looked like. I did not remove any of those caps - they all found their own way there during shipping. 2. That the wooden board doesn't line up on the top. 3. The busted zip-tie that doesn't even look threaded. and 4. A video showing the wobble with almost 0 pressure.

text:
This project was hard to assemble with the instructions given. They were not clear and it has to be assembled in a specific way. Once I figured it out by going through reviews on amazon then it assembled really easily. That's why I'm putting in an explanation in my review.

1. Put the black pieces together then slide up or down until it clicks in place.
This will allow the shelves to go on easily as shown in the instructions.
2. Make sure the shelves are placed on properly with the side wall facing down. Also the 4 holes that the poles go into are a little narrower on top and slightly wide at bottom. So make sure the wider side is facing down.

Overall really nice product. Clean and sturdy finish with nice amount of space.
I just wish the instructions were a little more clear or at least would have arrows for description.

I’ve been a commercial carpenter for 19 1/2 years and I’m not scared to admit this stupid mistake while I assembled this.
When I thought I was finished, the table top was 3/8 out of level. I was like, “WTF!?” I know the floors not off that much. I assembled the legs upside down! It has adjustable screw feet to Illuminate this problem and let you get it from going both directions. Because the plastic plugs were already in the legs I thought that was the bottom.
Another note that might help someone, the collars on the shelves are tapered 1 1/8”- 1 1/4. There is a Notch on the caller that’s the downside. Also when I reassembled us the working shelf with the wood table top is going to be raised to the maximum height on the shortest hori notch on the caller that’s the downside. Also when I reassemble this the working shelf with the wood table top is going to be raised to the maximum height on the shortest Vertical legs. My bad!
So embarrassingly I fixed my F up and timed it. I didn’t stop the clock for the beer and cig I drank and smoked in the way. Also, the wood block was at a good working height when it was assembled correctly. Again, I am wicked embarrassed about the error. When I was starting it, I was on the phone with my ex and told her how easy it was, so the mistake is mostly her fault. Pix of the correction and timer.

text:
This was disappointing. While it is easy enough to put together, and the directions were very straight forward, you'd better hope you get one with excellent welding, because the one I received was entirely shoddy. Tubes were difficult to securely insert without added force, because cylindrical openings were not properly welded circularly. In addition, the setting area for the wooden plank cannot fit it properly, because the metal has warped. As such, it has to be shifted forward, so as not to fall forward.

Ultimately, it'll do as I'm mainly using it for kitchen storage over active daily use, but I would not recommend this to anyone looking to use this for activities, outside of easing up their own cabinet space. Save your money, and spend on a different brand.

title: Pain to put together but looks nice
text:
I had some issues with it, otherwise I would have given it a 5 star.

Bad things first:
It was quite a pain to put together. It would be nice if there preset places to put each shelf, but there's not. You have to attach a plastic piece, then try to get the holes in the shelf to go over the plastic pieces. The plastic pieces do not want to stay put. They slide down, so they're never quite even, and I couldn't get the shelves to go completely over them, so you can still see a bit of the plastic poking out.

The shelves were so annoying to get in place, I actually forgot to put the part with the hooks on and when I realized it, I didn't feel like dealing with getting the top shelf off again to put it on.

The good things:

It is TALL. I'm really impressed with the height of it.

Seems pretty sturdy, despite the pieces not being completely even.

It holds quite a lot and there's a good amount of space on the shelves.

Overall I do really like it. Makes it easier to organize my kitchen and seems like it's got more space than other kitchen racks I considered. I just wish they'd figure out a different way to put it together.

text:
You really need to know how to use cast iron. I am a newbie with cast iron, so I thought that when it says pre-seasoned, then it's ready to use without adding any other kind of oil. I was wrong, you always need to use some sort of oil. I used it without applying cooking oil because of my ignorance, and the crust of my pizza got stuck to the pan.

Easy to clean: If you forgot to add cooking oil like I did, then it is not easy to clean the mess. Otherwise, I'm guessing that using oil makes it easy to clean, but just using hot water.

Sturdiness: This pizza pan is hefty since it's cast iron.

title: Almost perfect little space heater, but one glaring mistake.
text:
I love this little space heater. Sitting at my feet in my office, it offers the perfect amount of warmth to keep my feet and my body warm in a cold house. I like the size, the looks, and the fan's sound was just fine and it served as a nice, even white noise.

The only problem, and the reason I returned this and went with another make (Andily 500 Watt), is because the on/off switch is on the backside of the unit. When placed on the floor and kind of pushed back towards the back wall underneath my office desk, I have to bend down and pick up the unit each time I want to turn it off or on. So to turn it off, I have to pick up a hot unit with my bare hands and fiddle with it to turn it off.

That's it. That was the one thing that prevented me from keeping this great little heater.

Amazon, if you are listening, just make a version with the on/off switch on the top or on the front, like the Andily space heater has.

I wish I could have kept this one, since it looks much nicer, and the heating element and the fan are larger in size even though they are the same wattage as the Andily one. This combo of a larger heating element and a larger fan creates a wall of warm air that is wider and this seems to heat up the area underneath my desk much better. And also I figure a larger fan in this unit would have to work less harder to move an adequate amount of air than the smaller fan in the Andily unit, so it should last longer, all things being equal.

Oh well.

text:
I already have heaters installed on my walls. They are powerful but very noisy. I need a heater with a lower noise level that I can tolerate running continuously in my home office space so that the heater on the wall doesn't have to run too often.

This heater does have a lower noise level compared to the heaters on the wall, and still produces a substantial amount of heat. However, it is not as quiet as I expected after reading others' reviews. I still hear it even when I'm sitting 8 feet away from it. It also gives a plastic smell when I turn it on for the first time. I hope the smell will go away after some time.

I would still say it's a very good simple heater for it's price. But if you have a very high standard of quietness, this is not the best solution. You have to go radiator type of heater.

title: The perfect desktop heater - 2023 UPDATE
text:
2023 Update Review:
It has been the entire fall/winter/early spring seasons and I'm finally ready to put away my little desk heater. Nearly 6 months of use and it still operates as perfectly as it did when I first got it. I couldn't ask for a better designed heater for my use case. I have found that putting it on the floor at my feet, I tend to get warm all over instead of just the upper body. If you need a quiet little heater for at your desk, look no further than this. I'm so glad I gave this a try before spending more on "features" I didn't want or need. Amazon Basics knocked it out of the park with this heater, at this price.

First Review:
After doing a fair bit of research for a small ceramic heater that would fit well on my desk and put out enough heat to keep my hands warm, I landed on this Amazon Basics. I didn't want or need a 1500 watt heater and so many of those in this price range got terrible reviews. The few heaters I did find that had variable wattage all had the fatal flaw of starting up at 1500 watts which you could then dial down to 750 or 500 watts. My desk's power strip would not handle such a high current draw. This Amazon Basics heater draws exactly 500 Watts - as shown in the photo. Plugging it into a Kill A Watt device, I measured the startup and running wattage and found it to be remarkably stable and precisely on the mark. The heat delivery is just right for close proximity and it manages to actually raise the temperature in my whole office after about 30 minutes. The tip over safety switch works reliably. The body of the heater (plastic) stays room temperature. The fan sound is quiet and not a distraction at all, even during online meetings. The sound it makes is a gentle, constant white noise. There is virtually no blade thump, thump, thump that you hear with some fans. I find it quite relaxing. There was some light, warm plastic smell emanating from the heater when I first powered it up but I expected as much. After a few hours it went away. Each morning when I first turn it on there is slight hint of it but it seems to be less and less with each use. Not a problem, or unpleasant, just noting the observation for those of you who may have super sniffers.

Time will tell how this heater holds up with daily use. At this price, even if it only lasts until next spring, I'd call it a win and would definitely buy it again. I have a feeling it will last much longer as it seems to be made much better than its price would indicate.

title: Solid construction, hearty upholstery, too narrow for my frame, so not quite a 'standard' queen
text:
A beautiful addition to my furniture, this headboard is a quality piece that is exceptionally easy to assemble. It matches my décor well, is cushiony and strong, and has a durable upholstery. It was shipped and packaged in a reliable box with plenty of packing materials that kept it safe for its long journey, and the included hardware, tools, and instructions made it a cinch to assemble and attach to the frame. There are at least three vertical settings (with a fourth for the attachment to the frame that has a large variety of attachment options).

The biggest problem with this piece, and as reflected by many of the reviewers, is that it was simply too narrow for my bed frame and is not a standard queen-sized mount for a queen-sized frame. There are no ways to adjust the horizontal attachments, either. Visually it appears to fit fine, however, so I made a small modification by adding a plate to retain the other side and make up for the remaining six-inches or so. It is unfortunate that this is the case, but there is a measurement in the description and all headboards that are sold on Amazon have a variety of horizontal measurements, so I can put this error on me.

Regardless of this, it looks great, and that small detail is completely unnoticeable to anyone that wouldn’t pull it away from the wall – which is no one. I do think that the price point for this unit is a bit high, though. I would pay about fifty dollars less at the time of this writing (from $200 to $150) and I would feel the headboard would be a good value.

title: Does not live up to expectation
text:
I'm new to steaming, so I thought that this unit would be a good introductory unit. In my mind, the three compartments should help me get meals on the table with a little less effort than normal, allowing me more time for my family. Unfortunately, I was very wrong. This steamer turned out to be quite the disappointment.

What I liked:

- Once I figured out the presets, I liked what it could do. It has a setting for veggies, one for rice, one for meats, etc.

- Each of the three trays are numbered so there is no guesswork as to which tray goes on the bottom and which goes on the top.

- The water level was easy to read.

- If I forgot to check the water level, the unit shuts off in order to prevent it from burning out.

- The unit steamed fresh and frozen vegetables wonderfully. I did not test to see how fish, meats and eggs turned out.

What I disliked:

- The unit is quite cumbersome. In order to fill the unit with water, you need to pull all the trays, including the drip tray out.

- The unit is quite tall, so in order to use all three trays you need plenty of clearance on your counters. The same goes for storing the unit.

- The instruction manual was poorly written. It would be nice if the instructions would go into greater detail about the features. Cook times in the instruction manual are not accurate. Either foods were overcooked or undercooked. You have to watch closely and not rely on the times printed in the manual.

- It does an extremely poor job of steaming rice. I tried on three different occasions with no success. The final time I only used 1/4 cup of rice and doubled the steam time that was suggested, but the rice still wasn't edible.

- The trays must be hand washed only. They are not dishwasher safe.

- It was difficult to operate the steamer. If you hit the power button, it should come on. If you hit a preset (such as eggs) it should automatically start. That's not how this unit works.

To sum up, this is not a good unit. As someone just getting interested in steaming food, I found this unit much to complicated and cumbersome. If this was a unit I purchased, I would have been extremely disappointed and turned off from steaming food. As a tester, I was disappointed, but it won't deter me from finding a unit that will work for me.

title: A nice little masher
text:
This AmazonBasics Nylon masher weighs just under 4 ounces and is a shade over 11” long. The handle is soft but doesn’t have any grips or textures to fight fatigue. Meanwhile the masher end has sufficient hole size to turn soft foods into a pastes but it won’t rice them.

What I liked most about this masher was that it worked perfectly with nonstick cookware and plastic bowls. Where a metal masher might be stronger and more suitable for tackling harder or steaming foods, this one was far less likely to damage porous cooking surfaces/serving vessels.

What I liked least bout this masher was its heat resistance. While this masher can handle warm and even slightly hot foods you really have to be cautious about using it inside of still hot pots and pans. I also found that learning the handle on the side of a hot pot/pan wasn’t the best way to extend the life of this masher.

Overall, if you are measured with the types of foods you want to mash and the amount of heat you expose this masher to I think this AmazonBasics masher will prove highly functional for most home cooks. I did find using this masher for extended periods a bit fatiguing and I quickly learned to be careful about how much heat I exposed this thing to but with a bit of mindfulness I found myself getting good mileage out of this masher. Solid 4 out of 5 product from AmazonBasics.

title: The prototypical jack-of-all trades...
text:
This AmazonBasics Multi-Speed Immersion Hand Blender with Attachments is a marvel of versatility. You can go from blending warm soups and sauces in pots/pans to chopping or mixing items in the included containers. Changing tools is a breeze and there’s sufficient power on board to handle most small tasks. This is a value item so throwing thick batters, ice and other hard to cope with items at it will likely cut its lifespan short.

Pros:
- This is almost like having a sous-chef in the home as preparation is greatly streamlined with the range of tools and functions this blender can perform
- Space saver. I don’t need a separate blender and chopper sitting on the counter now. I can tuck this little guy in a corner and it performs 75% of the tasks I would need to use those two machines for plus it performs more functions neither of those could handle.
- Comfortable with easy to reach settings. A stick blender won’t get much use if it’s hard to hold or awkward to control. This one has the ergonomics down pat

Cons
- The stick/shaft is a bit shorter than I’d like. It’s fine for 5-6 quart pots/pans but larger items might present too much of a challenge for this tool
- I wish it had more power settings or maybe even more power altogether as I wouldn’t trust this item to crush ice or churn nuts into various nut butters. I still trust my standalone blender for that task.

Overall, this little guy is a cool addition to the kitchen. It adds versatility and usefulness you may never have known you were missing. It lacks the power for big jobs and its shaft is a bit too short for 8-quart and larger pots but those are minor concessions you’d expect from something in this price range. Recommended for most home chefs who want to up their cooking games without breaking their budgets.

title: Not bad for the price. Amazon needs to do better handling product.
text:
The stars don't do justice to how I feel about the product. I actually love the desk and the price drop to sub $60 range makes worth every penny. The reason for the 3 star is the bottom paragraph of my review. But let's get to the review.

It's sturdy enough. I wouldn't recommend you sit on it, though. Use it for what it's for and you'll be fine. Assembly is fairly simple but if you're not good with your hands you might have a little trouble with the screws for the racking and accessories. I'm not the biggest fan of wire racking for storage BUT for quality at low prices it's a decent bang for buck. If it was any other material it would be flimsy and probably more expensive. The speaker stands are a bit weird and leave me wondering why they seem to be upside down. I get that these can hold games/DVDs but it comes off...strange . Why are they beneath table level if that's what they're for? I can get used to that, though. The phelted covered tilted stand is neat and if I'm wearing headphones it's good because my phone is next to my screen so I can see it light up even if I can't hear it. The drawback? It should be able to pivot a tad towards the center so it's easier to see. Not a big deal but a bid of detail there would have been nice. The cup holder is inevitably going to make me spill some thing at some point. I can already feel it coming. A small can of red bull is going to go in between those wires and straight in to the carpet. I can already see it coming. A bit more coverage around it would be nice but you get what you pay for. I can always remove it and buy one online. To clamp to the table. None of those are truly worthy of the 3 star, though.

The 3 star is the fact that the quality is affected if the distribution centers can't get a handle on their damages and QC. The pictures attached are what I mean. The blemishes are easy to overlook and I'm sure I can cover them up or ignore them but there's no reason it should look like this out of the box. This was obviously dropped and/or mishandled. Other than that it's very well done and I don't regret the purchase.

title: Still Great 3 Years Later
text:
Two apartments and three years later (plus a short stay in storage) this sofa is still going strong! None of the cushions have gone flat and only the back cushions look a little lived-in but aren't sagging. The upholstery has held up excellently and hasn't developed any pilling or broken seams. The removable cushion covers make it easy to clean, too.

As for comfort, I wasn't sure whether to give it a 3 or 4 star rating. Because of the style the back cushions are kind of short and don't provide any neck and head support when you're sitting upright. However, you do get the neck support if you slouch into it and put your feet up. The seat cushions are pretty firm but I suppose that's the trade-off for how well they maintain their shape. The back cushions are a little squishier but still on the firmer side.

This sofa is lightweight which makes it easy to move but also makes it easy to accidentally bump out of place if it's on hard, smooth flooring (wood/tile/laminate). I recommend putting no-skid pads on the legs or having at least the front legs on an area rug. Its lightness doesn't seem to affect its structural integrity, though, and mine hasn't developed any squeaking, wobbling or creaking.

This is a perfectly-sized couch for apartments and, like I mentioned earlier, is easy to move and transport. Only thing I can't comment on is how well it holds up to kids and/or pets since I don't have any of my own.

title: just like the real thing
text:
I almost didn't buy these hangers, because some of the reviews mentioned that these shed and stained. I ended up taking a chance, because the price is much cheaper than the "real" version in the stores and I like how these have a notch for straps (even though the flocking keeps straps on the hanger pretty well by itself).

I'm glad I went ahead and got these. I have some of the real ones that I got on clearance a while back and these seem quite comparable. They look pretty much the same and the thickness and flocking are very similar. I wouldn't put really heavy items on these, but I wouldn't do that with the other ones either. (I prefer thick wooden hangers for things like winter coats.) The hooks do rotate, but they kinda feel like they might get weakened if rotated a lot over time. Again, my other hangers feel the same way. I think these are a great cheaper alternative for people looking for this type of hanger.

As for the shedding and stain, well I figured I would just prepare for that. I wiped down each hanger with a paper towel over a plastic bag when I unpacked them. There was no shedding and the white paper towel was still white when I was done. I don't know if there was a problem with another batch, but these seem just fine.

title: Solid Product and Quality Build
text:
This platform bed works perfectly for a thicker mattress. The mattress sits at a good height and there's plenty of headboard remaining above it. The color is a very neutral gray, not to dark, light, cool, warm etc. Should go well with anything. The style makes a room look much more luxurious and put together. The fabric is a nice material; it doesn't feel cheap. A queen mattress should fit very nicely in on the slats. The slats are slightly recessed so the mattress doesn't move around, but they aren't too deep, so changing sheets isn't a hassle.

The frame itself is sturdy. The slats are a nice distance apart and they're all made of solid wood. The product info doesn't show it, but there IS a solid wood center support beam. It's actually two shorter center support beams, but I think it makes it more rigid. I've had the bed for almost a few weeks now and there's now signs of wear, no creaking, and no warping. I'm skeptical of wood as it ages, but so far it's a very solid porduct. Overall I'm satisfied.

title: Great for desk use!
text:
I've had this small space heater for a year now and have bought another for a gift. It is usually placed at my desk pointing at my hands while I work at my computer since my hands do get cold sitting for 8hrs+ a day lol.

There is no temperature control, but I control it by placing it closer or further away. The radius it directly blows hot air is maybe 1.5ft out (and heat rises so it's not a straight path outward). My room is large (~200sqft) so it doesn't make a huge difference in warming up the entire room unless I insulate it by closing the door and closing the blinds on my window.

I have used this outdoors at an event and was a life saver keeping me and my friends warm as we worked at an outdoor festival with 40-50F weather and 10mph wind. We placed it very close to us on a table and made such a huge difference!

There is a knock-over safety feature where if the button under is not pushed enough, it will shut off automatically. There is no timer function on this. Overall, I enjoy having this little device at my desk to keep my hands nice and warm.

title: Great couch for great price.
text:
Spent really long looking for an affordable couch that looked simple and clean. This one is great! It is somewhat meant for smaller light people, it won’t break if your heavy but I could see how it’s not comfortable if your really tall or heavy. But for most people it would be a great couch for an apartment or entrance room. It is a bit on the slimmer/smaller side, but saves a ton of space. The quality of the fabric I would say is 7/10, way better than Ashley, IKEA or Mor quality. Firmness is 6/10 pretty good, has not sagged over the past months.

The legs are tucked in the bottom of the couch so make sure to look hard! Also the wood legs are super nice and I love the tapered style, gives it that mid century modern touch.

My only complaint is that the couch seems to move around a lot when sitting both the couch itself and seat cushion. We just put 3M non-slip pads on the legs and this made it stay! The cushions we still haven’t figured out, it is not horrible by any means like you might need to move the cushion back once a day, but that’s it. What I am thinking of is adding Velcro strips between the couch frame and cushions to keep them still.

I would still highly recommend this couch for space savers, small families, apartment dwellers or just anyone looking for a good couch.

title: Too High, Too Stiff, Doesn't Recline, and the Armrests Don't Feel Right
text:
This is my new desk chair to spend all my waking time in, watching TV, listening to music, or working on my computer. It's important to me to have a chair that suits me and my body. First of all, I do not weigh anywhere near 500 pounds. I am maybe a third of that. I am 5 feet and 10 inches tall, and at its lowest setting, using the gas lift, my feet barely touch the floor. It is much too high, and that is because the seat has so much thick padding in it. Too much thick padding. If I were a person of size, I think I would want and need a less thick cushion to sit on so I could sit lower. My desk that I sit at has a slide-out keyboard tray, and when I go to type, my elbows press against the armrests. The armrests are not adjustable. My keyboard tray is at the standard height for typing. I have never had this problem before, that the armrests interfere with the movement of my elbows. This could be solved if the armrests were lower and I could rest my elbows on the armrests, but in this chair that doesn't work, because my fingers would be too far above the keyboard to touch the keys. When resting or watching TV, I would like to recline the chair. It unlocks, and will recline a tiny bit if I use all my strength to push the chair back - but it won't stay reclined, it pops right back up straight. I tried loosening the chair with the knob underneath, but it doesn't help.

Since my old chair is now at the curb, and was falling apart and held together with black Gorilla Tape, I suppose I must get used to this new chair. But I can predict that since this chair is the same kind of fake leather material, soon I will be buying more black Gorilla Tape to hold it together. All I can do is sigh. Maybe Santa Clause will bring me a chair better suited for me. I believe that with some simple changes, this chair would be better suited for me and also persons up to 500 pounds. For now, I can only say two stars.

title: Flimsy Shelf with Less Than Helpful Instructions--Arrived Damaged
text:
We have a variety of storage shelving units in our home. Most were purchased from Amazon and most were made by Origami. The Origami products are fabricated from steel, are collapsible, offer simple installation and great strength.

The AmazonBasics 5-Shelf Shelving Unit doesn't come close to matching the Origami shelves. True, the price for the AmazonBasics 5-Shelf Shelving Unit is much lower than the equivalent Origami unit (less than 1/2 of the cost.) However, the saying is true--"you get what you pay for." The AmazonBasics 5-Shelf Shelving Unit's construction is shoddy, the product is poorly manufactured and the installation itself is challenging.

The first hint that the AmazonBasics 5-Shelf Shelving Unit wasn't up to par occurred when I first opened the shipping carton. A myriad of little plastic clips intended to protect the shelving parts during shipment simply fell out of the box. The second hint became obvious when several of the plastic straps intended to hold the shelf parts together proved to have been previously cut. The third hint appeared when I noticed that a number of the shelves were bent. Obviously this is a product that is either poorly manufactured or improperly packaged for shipment.

The product is challenging to put together--not because it's particularly hard to do, but because the product is well so poorly thought out. The plastic clips that hold the shelves in place fly apart easily and are far from the best solution. Installation is also challenging because the multi-language instructions are subpar. Finally, the various parts are not labeled so you have to use a not so great series of diagrams in the instructions to identify parts. It's the only way you can tell what parts are to be installed in what order.

The shelves themselves are held together with nothing more than the flimsy plastic clamps that I mentioned above. They do not appear to be very sturdy and popped off very easily when assembling the shelves. It is necessary to lightly hammer the shelves on to the plastic clip with a wood mallet. Otherwise the clamps will not properly hold the shelves.

Amazon claims that, "Each shelf holds up to 350 pounds (evenly distributed)." In your dreams! I would not rely on the AmazonBasics 5-Shelf Shelving Unit to hold anything heavier than paper towels or toilet paper. I suspect that anything even remotely approaching 350 pounds (evenly distributed weight) would bring the entire unit using crashing down. It's that flimsy.

If I were Amazon, I would give some serious thought to selling this product under thier brand name. It's simply not up to typical Amazon quality--even when sold as AmazonBasics.

title: Beautiful And Well-Built: A Rivet Aiden Tufted Mid-Century Leather Chair Review
text:
The Rivet Aiden tufted mid-century leather chair, made in China comes in a large box and needs some minor assembly. The legs are stored in the interior of the seat, with zippered access. Assembly basically included unscrewing the legs from the interior and screwing them into the holes on the bottom of the chair. Then the rear pillow is set into place. The assembled chair measures 35” square and about 32” tall.

The rear pillow just rests into place without Velcro or anything to keep it in place. The pillow stays in place for the most part, but can easily be toppled over. The chair back and the pillow do have a fabric area to help reduce slippage. Velcro could be added to this area if pillow movement becomes an issue for you.

I should have measured my spot before selecting this chair. Now that I have the chair, I realized that it’s too deep for where I wanted to place it. I have an alternative spot where it fits, it’s just not where I initially intended to place the chair.

If you like mid-century modern furnishings, the Rivet Aiden tufted mid-century leather chair is a beautiful and well-built option to consider. The design is spot on, the chair is comfortable, and the leather brings it all together.

Hardwood frame

text:
We have a beach house which we rent out as a short term rental. We often get guests who are attending weddings so they will have dresses and formal clothing they need to hang. One of our bedrooms was probably built as an office, so it has no closets. This is the perfect solution-- it's unobtrusive and perfect for sitting out the towels we provide them on the bottom rack.

I put this together in about 20 minutes. Make sure you pay attention to which screws are what and separate them for each step. Some of the screws took some muscle to get in, they were too much for my cordless screwdriver but it only took a few minutes for each. My only issue was the screws that go into the middle part are recessed and it was difficult to hold the wrench on the hex nuts to tighten down well. I tried using some needle nose pliers and found out the "caps" on nuts are just cheap tin so I broke one off. No biggie, you don't really notice it but just FYI don't try to hold them the way I did. I ordered the two tier rack so shirts or children's clothing can be hung on the lower level and dresses can be hung on the back. I put some color coordinated hangers on them so it will be obvious what they are for. If the guests don't need to hang clothing they can still use this as a towel rack so it's a useful piece of furniture regardless. The white rack tubes are machined a little sloppily and so not perfectly smooth. It was very noticeable before putting it together, but I think once they were in place no one would pick up on it. The bamboo seems very strong and the base has enough weight on it I don't think this rack would be unbalanced unless someone hung heavy winter coats on one side. This rack would also look nice in a spa type setting to hang towels upon.

Don't forget you can use Amazon Smile when you shop to donate to your favorite charity! When you order via Smile, (smile.amazon.com) Amazon will donate to the charity of your choice when you make a qualifying purchase. I choose to help Soi Dog Foundation USA, who help dogs in Thailand. title: Very effective as a desktop heater
text: I have a multi-level home, and my office is on a level that has windows at ground level, meaning the room is partially in the ground. As you can imagine, this means it's cool in the summer and COLD in the winter. My fingers and toes tend to be ice-cold as a result, and because of sensory issues, if I get too cold, I cannot focus on my work. I used to have a bigger heater for under my desk, but it has recently become unreliable, so I needed something else. I got this because I planned to keep it on my desk so that my fingers could be warm. It works very well, and it keeps me plenty warm in a room that gets very cold. When my office door is closed, this little heater raises the heat in the room noticeably. If I leave to go to the bathroom, I notice the change in temperature when I walk back in - it's very nice. The heat is focused pretty much right out of the middle and it blows a decent amount of heat wherever directed. There's a switch on the bottom that turns it off if it gets picked up or pushed over. You do not have control over the temperature or intensity, so that's something to be aware of if that is a feature you're looking for - I have no complaints about this because my space is cold enough that it can blow hot air and it won't get too hot because the room is otherwise way too cold. I'm very pleased with this purchase and have thought about buying another for my craft room.

title: Here's how to assemble it, hope this saves someone some time!
text:
My washer and dryer aren't right next to each other and this is exactly what I needed. The wheels glide smoothly. It looks decent, if you care what your laundry baskets look like.

It's definitely sturdy if assembled correctly, but the instructions need to be better. It took me a while to figure it out because I have never assembled anything with nylon lock nuts before. The nuts included are nylon lock nuts -- metal nuts with a little plastic thing inside.

- When installing the screws into the bottom part, you do use the longer screws. Use pliers to hold the nut in place while using the Allen wrench (included) to turn the screw. The screw will push through that plastic thing inside the nut. The plastic thing actually helps lock everything in place.

- Because installing the screws and lock nuts requires two hands (one is holding the pliers and the other is turning the Allen wrench), you kind of need a second person to hold things in place. None of this requires a lot of strength, it's just kind of ungainly until you get it all together. A little kid could hold pieces for you while you are using the tools.

- When you're putting the top circle on, leave all the screws kind of loose until you've got it all in place, then tighten it up at the end. Otherwise you may find that you have to unscrew things in order to get that fourth pole in place. Learn from my fail.

- When you put the bag in, fold the top edge of the bag down over the metal circle a little bit at a time, and fold all the way around the circle before you start clipping it in place. If you try to start clipping it in place without folding it down first, it will seem like the top of the bag is too narrow.

- Enjoy not straining your back muscles moving wet laundry across your basement.

title: Easy & Perfect. A Great "Personal" Heater
text:
Puts out a surprisingly amount of heat for a small ceramic heater and is perfect a small area, like under a desk to keep your legs warm and your feet from turning into icebergs. Small and quiet, it does its job without any ado; there is only one speed and one heat setting - you flip the small switch on the back of the heater and there's nothing else be done except to bask in the warmth.

The heating unit is rated to use 500 watts when in use which translates into around 4.17 amps at 120 volts, so it adds a small amperage load on a standard 15 or 20 amp circuit. Unless there is other heavy draw equipment running, the little heater won't throw circuit breakers or blow any fuses when in use.

There is an internal shut-off control inside the heater that turns it off should the heater tip over, and given the heater's small size and light weight that's an important feature.

If placing the heater on a carpet or other flammable material, you might want to consider placing the heater on a flat noncombustible surface - something like a metal cooking pan, a metal tray, or something similar to keep the heater from sitting directly on a carpet or a rug.

Our "Amazon Basics" ceramic heater has been working very well and has proven to be a good purchase. If you need a little heater this one does the job.

The wand part of it has some heft, but the buttons feel loose and inaccurate. The attachment is light weight and feels like it'll break within the year. It has a weird thin rod that you attach into the wand, but then you have to wriggle things around quite a bit to get it to click shut. This will be a safety issue while working with lye.

If I had nothing to compare it to, I'd probably think it was ok, but I have a Cuisinart immersion blender, and there is simply no comparison.

(For reference, 80ish degrees is comfortable for me - but still, I can't even feel a difference in the air for at least an hour after turning on. I live in Texas, and lately it's been 40~60 degrees when I start up the unit.)

Takes a long time to heat up my bedroom, and I have everything covered. 4 stars for heating though, because it's only 500 watts. 5 stars if the fan had any kind of throughput.

A variable temperature control would have been amazing to have. I would happily pay an extra 5 dollars for that feature.

text:
Works well, just need to have the proper expectations for it. It’s a 500w heater, don’t be mad when it doesn’t heat your multi car garage as the only heat source.
I put one in each of my daughters rooms bc they have big windows and I found were getting around 5 degrees colder than the rest of the house on really cold nights.
With a temp sensor in each room and the heaters connected to smart plugs I setup automations that turn the heater on if the temp drops to 65, then turns it back off when it reaches 68 again (my house is set at 70)
As supplemental heat these work great. During the really cold nights I found it would kick on for about 20-30 min to raise the temp enough to trigger it to turn off and now both their rooms stay a consistent temp to the rest of the house. Didn’t want a heater that got super hot since it would be turning on/off without my input in a baby’s room or one that would really run up the bill so this 500w heater was perfect for how I wanted to use it. A+

text: These are great easy to use and clean. They hide foods with strong aromas. However, here is a tip I learned the hard way from my little microwaving lunch FAIL...Be careful when heating these in the microwave! Remove the top completely don't not just loosen. Do not recover your food directly after heat with locking tops. Turn the top upside down with the lock fasteners facing up or cover unlock with a paper towel between the container and the lid. title: Basic in the best way....
text:
Our ~9yr old Cuisinart is slowly starting to give up the ghost. It is one of those fancy models overly built with all the flashy functions one could think of and it had a high price to go with it. Thing you take for granted like a beep when you finished, built in water filtration system, timer, clock, temperature select, single cup serving, auto off function, auto start timers....you know....fancy.

The odd thing is over the years, we've found ourselves not using ANY of the extra functions and just using it to brew basic pots. You know...water in, coffee in, press start, wait for beep, pour, enjoy.

Then there's the AmazonBasics 12-Cup coffee Maker.....

When I received the box I honestly thought either it was something different or it was missing it was that light. I cautiously cracked open the box and took a look and....yep....there it was in all it's utilitarian glory.

No fancy dials. No super thick overly built build quality. No clock, no water filters, nothing.

The coffee maker overall just feels super light, super thin and will make you question the build quality, but in the end, its job is to brew coffee. no more; no less.

Just as basic as a coffee maker as one can get, it has an instruction manual but I'm not even sure why. You literally just pour the water in, fill the cup, turn it on.

After a minute, you hear the classic sounds of percolation and your hot coffee dripping into the VERY lightweight pot with a very thin lid in conjunction with a warming plate you can actually hear clicking on and off.

But you know what? It works.

It does EXACTLY what it sets out to do and that is brew you a pot of coffee within spec and that it does so admirably as the coffee tasted the same from the DapperDan2000. For our second cups, I did a pour over for intensity (same as I did with the Cuisinart SuperFancy 2000) and it tasted just as good.

It works in the most basic of ways...

...and that's all you can ask of it for the price.

5/5

title: Frothy & toasty!
text:
The first few times I tried using it, it started frothing & heating as soon as the pitcher hit the plugged in base. I think it remembers if someone previously stopped it mid froth/heating, and automatically starts up again as soon as it's plugged in, whether or not you press any buttons, and no matter how much time has passed.

Anyway, we've worked out the kinks since then, and now it only starts after we hit the proper buttons - not as soon as it's plugged in.

It makes a great frothy milk, and we're enjoying it in our coffee, ice cream bases, etc. The warming function gets it just warm enough to sip instantly without burning anyone. The pitcher & handle remains cool even after the milk is heated. Cleanup is a bit annoying, since the foamy milk sticks to the walls, but it's not the end of the world.

On the lazy side of things, if you only want froth or warming, but not both, you need to remove the small heating coil/frother piece as needed. Personally, I usually have no time or patience to do that, so anytime I want my milk to be heated only, I'm going to get it frothed too. It's an extra (small) step to remove the pieces otherwise.

Basically, I like the small size of the machine. It takes up very little counter space and is easy to store away, and works perfectly.

title: Love almost everything, but reluctantly returning it
text:
I love the quality of the piece (real wood!) and how wonderful it looks in my living room. I am returning it for one main reason: I can't use it for the purpose I intended, which was to use the table to eat from. I cannot get the table close enough to me to comfortably eat off. If there were no bottom shelf, I could pull it closer. That is the big problem I have. It's also an inch or two short to use it to eat off, for my comfort, anyway. The minor problem I have with it is that it annoys me to have to get up, go on the other side of the table, and pull the knob to lower the table. I could have lived with that.

The positives: it looks wonderful when put together. I could not find anything comparable in quality or looks for a similar price when trying to find a replacement. The storage area doesn't have hardware that takes up much room or is in an awkward location. Except for the last two screws, it was really easy to put together. Overall, it was still quite easy. It is packaged carefully, with the consumer in mind. The styrofoam is shrink-wrapped, so you don't get all those little annoying white balls of static all over the carpet. The open storage at the bottom is a good size for a variety of containers. It is a great height to put my phone on to have hands-free video calls. Have I mentioned how good it looks?

Assembly tip: While you're waiting for your table to arrive, get yourself a straight Allen wrench. The one that comes with the table has the standard short end and long end. Even the short end is a few millimeters too long to turn the four final screws without running into the bottom of the storage space. You can twist just over 1/4 turn before you have to remove it and reposition. For at least two of the screws, you will not be able to see to do that (your head won't fit in the opening), which makes it time-consuming and annoying to have to keep repositioning. If you can find a straight Allen wrench, you will be grateful.

Bottom line: I wish it either met my pseudo-dining table needs or I could justify another use for it.

title: Not Good for Wood Floors
text: These mats allow a scenario that will destroy your wood floor. Water runoff from your body will not only sit atop the mat but will run around the edges of the matt and seep in-between the floor and the matt. We would stand on these matts after coming in from the hot tub or pool to dry off. After towel drying, we would typically drop the towel on the mat soak up the water, and then deposit the towel in the laundry. It was not until a week later when we moved the matt for floor cleaning that we discovered that a lot of water had traveled around the round corners and settled under the matt, allowing our wood floors to soak up the water. We have sense had the floors repaired and now we put the matt down, use the matt, then pick it up again and lay it on its side until needed again.

title: UPDATED: Quality Bed, Missing Parts
text:
Edit: After having the bed for several months, I am updating my rating from one star to four. First, Amazon went out of its way to discount the price of the furniture due to the missing items. Second, once completed, this bed is well worth the $550 sticker price paid when it was purchased. I will note that even once I had the parts, it was a little difficult to attach the frame to the headboard. You will need to avoid attaching the support boards on one side of the frame until after you successfully mount it to the headboard, despite what the instructions tell you. Good luck and enjoy! See below for original post.

I would love to write a review regarding the actual finished product. However, the package came missing the nuts required to attach the legs to the support brace. While the product seems to be well made and worth the price, I will never recommend a product from this company. It is unacceptable to ship a product that requires assembly, without the essential items to assemble the product correctly.

Sure, I will be going to the local hardware store to purchase the parts and complete assembly, but the fact that I have to go out of my way to do so is pathetic after spending $550.

title: I REALLY wanted to like this, but spend the extra money for a name brand
text:
I always buy Amazon Basics products when they're available, but this one misses the mark. The suction power is good and is able to vacuum seal when it wants to. The major issue is it doesn't always close all the way, so it never creates a vacuum. The second reason I bought a new one is the bag seal/cut design is backwards and makes using the bag roll more complicated and time consuming.

I'll start with the locking issue. My first machine didn't lock on the left side. It seems to be a tolerance issue where my tab wasn't long enough to engage the locking hook. I exchanged it for a new one, and the next one worked great, for about 2 months. Now the right side doesn't lock. Yes, you can keep your hand on the lid and push down and make it work, but that's not an effective solution.

It has a strong enough vacuum that rivaled my previous FoodSaver, and when it catches, it does vacuum and seal well. But without it locking, it'll fail to seal multiple times until you set it perfectly. If you value your own time, or try to seal items back to back, this will frustrate you to a point where you buy a new one.

My other complaint is a design flaw. The seal strip and cut should be inversed. Meaning, if you set the length of the bag, you should be able to seal it so the end of the roll (your next bag) is already closed, and then use the built in cutter to cut the bag you're about to use. But this machine has the cutter closer to the bag roll than the heat strip. So to make a bag you have to pull the length you need, cut, put the bag back in, seal the bottom, and then fill and go.

My old food saver you would seal the end of the roll the first time you use it. Then pull out the length you need, hit seal, then cut. The cut would happen below the seal, so you have your bag set to the size you need, and your next bag already sealed on the bottom. The amazon one you can't do this, so the workflow for making the bag is more time consuming.

I gave this sealer to a friend who doesn't seal often, and bought a name brand for myself.

title: Nice quality hangers
text:
I was reluctant to buy another brand's velvet hangers on amazon because reviews mentioned that several hangers came already broken, or broke while attempting to hang a shirt on it for the first time.

I noticed these amazon basics hangers and knew I'd want to give them a try, not only for the lower price, but also for the great quality I associate with amazon.

All 50 arrived in perfect condition. No breaks, tears in the velvet, or damage. I spent about 30 minutes rehanging my clothes on these and dropped them multiple times in the process and had my cat (and self) step all over them with no problem.

Pros:
Easily hangs tank tops, strappy dresses
Very thin hangers save space
Lightweight and aren't straining my old house's closet rod like those clunky plastic hangers
Visually consistent and appealing
Metal top can be rotated for garment to hang in either direction in closet

Cons:
None so far

I gave it 4 stars because it is my first day using them, so I'll report back in a few months about the quality. The reason I came back to this page today was to order another box of 50.

Update 4/21/14: I've been using these hangers for the past 2 months with no issues. I hang dry all of my tops and dresses directly out of the washer, and the wet garments have not affected the velvet on these hangers. Another pro I've noticed is that the metal can be rotated, which is great because my boyfriend can't seem to hang anything in the proper direction, so I just spin the top around and everything faces the same direction in my closet.

Update 7/20/14: I've had these for 5 months with not a single issue. Not one broken hanger. I upped my review to 5 stars. Buying another set. I will not stop until everything I own is on one of these.

Final update 3/4/15: It's been over a year. Can't tell the new hangers from the old hangers. Boyfriend that hangs garments in the wrong direction is now fiance that hangs garments in the wrong direction. I still swivel the top.

title: OBSESSED
text:
I am obsessed with this sofa! It was a bit of a hassle dealing with shipping in the middle of Ms. Rona. Literally had my delivery date bounced around SEVERAL times. Thank goodness I had enough sense not to toss out my old sofa before this one arrived. Nonetheless, Amazon’s customer service was great with working me through the fiasco. The carrier’s customer service on the other hand was WHEW. The delivery man had excellent customer service though. I was just happy to receive my sofa by that point lol. The only assembly you have to do is screw the legs in. The only problem was they didn’t drill any pilot holes for the smaller screws on mine. Thankfully I have a power drill. I drilled them myself with some patience, and a little elbow grease. Something to think about just in case you get a sofa that doesn’t have the predrilled holes for the smaller screws too. It was packed so well, like they were trying to ship it to Heaven LOL.
The sofa is firm, but not uncomfortably firm. It’s more of a firm that makes it feel like the sofa will last, and it very well better for the price tag! Just don’t expect to sink into this sofa like a puffy one. The velvet is SO smooth, and feels like great quality.
Overall I think it’s a great sofa so far. I would recommend it to someone to purchase.

Also, I could not use the bed feature on the first night because the delivery service people failed to set-up the chair. It was dumped in my study without even removing the protective film.

The delivery service XPS held the chair at its facility from July 25 until I contacted amazon to explain the non-delivery on the promised date. Finally, it was delivered the last 56 miles a week after promised delivery date.

text:

I couldnt see spending $70+on the nespresso brand frother so I bought this one for half the cost. The frother itself does a good job at frothing the milk or creamers you choose. One thing is the more fat in the milk the better it whips up. I use half and half with a splash of non fat vanilla creamer and it does well.
The machine itself is very quick to froth and heat, about a minute. I like the fact the kettle is removable from the base for easy cleaning. I do have a couple minor issues with it but have no way of comparing it with another brand to see if its "normal". But in order to get the milk actually hot, you must run it thru a few times, especially if you fill the kettle to the max. If you only put a little milk then once or twice is fine. A full kettle ran one time will only heat the milk to room temp. It still froths nice but not hot. The other thing is I wish the pour spout was more defined so there is less mess when pouring. Again these are minor issues but should be noted. The couple times I heated milk for hot cocoa I ran it like 5 cycles. I actually added the cocoa right into the machine and it whipped up nicely. Just be advised you will need to remove the mixer attachment and clean the kettle well. Overall I am happy with the quality and especially the price. It has a nice satin, brushed aluminum outer finish with a non stick, easy to clean interior.

title: Solid wood
text:
This is a solid wood desk with drawers. The desk stands 39.25” off the ground, 39.25” wide, and 21.5” wide. The insides of the drawers are 10.5” wide, 13” long and 3” deep. The drawer handles are metal. The tips of the legs that contact the floor are plastic. All wood is solid except for the drawer bottoms, which appear to be veneer on some wood material, perhaps press board. Upon arrival, you need to attach the drawer handles with a Philips head screwdriver (not included), and the legs with an Allen wrench (included). You also need to insert the drawer stops by hand or with a rubber mallet (not included). The desk comes with 3 sheets of instructions in diagrams without words. The desk was made by Zhangzhou XYM Furniture Product Co. in China.

I am very pleased with the appearance and solid feel of this desk. It’s very hard to find a solid wood desk these days, but this definitely fits the bill. It has an elegant design with sharply defined corners, and the 2 drawers are quite useful. The only thing I don’t like about the desk are the handles. Although they are solid metal, they are rather blah and have fake screw heads on the front. If I can find substitute handles to fit, I will probably replace them because the appearance of these handles just doesn’t fit the elegance of the desk. And I’m still trying to figure out the drawer stops. The desk came with 4 wooden dowels as drawer stops, which the drawings show being inserted, 2 into the back of each drawer, 1 on each side, in the predrilled holes. And then they are supposed to catch on the other 4 dowels inserted in the 4 predrilled holes in the drawer slides. That’s 4 dowels, 8 holes. Am I supposed to cut the 4 dowels in half to get 8? For now I’ll just go without drawer stops and be careful about how I open the drawers. Overall, this is a very attractive solid wood desk.

title: Simple, basic non-stick whisks that work great and are easy to clean
text:

I use the the 8" and 10" whisks nearly every day for light baking and cooking with nonstick cookware, the 12" whisk is no less useful but I am only cooking for two so it doesn't get as much action as its brethren. There's nothing "commercial" in how I use them but they absolutely do the trick for whisking up ingredients, eggs, pancakes, brownies, sauces, they haven't let me down in the four months I've been using them. These look nearly identical to the cheapo whisk set I got a year ago at a discount chain, but these Amazon ones are vastly better for a simple yet utterly vital reason: these are well made enough so that the tines stay firmly in the handle during use and cleaning, which the cheapo ones absolutely do not.

These are silicone-coted wire balloon whisks attached to a simple handle with a generous hanging hook at the end and clean, subtle AmazonCommerical branding printed on the side. The black silicone coating makes it easy to see when I haven't cleaned them thoroughly, nobody wants pancake batter left in the tines - my cheapo set was rainbow colored silicone and I'd have to really study them to see when something was missed. Cleaning is as easy as any wire whisks, jam a sponge in between the tines and wipe, then wipe the outside, even the little 8" whisk is pliant enough to clean without troubles. I've not cleaned them via the dishwasher yet since they're easy enough to clean by hand, but it does say that option is there.

title: Pours great
text:
I am getting into pour over coffee brewing, but got this for both that and for my french press (and my wife's yerba mate).

This seems pretty well made, and comes with good instructions. The base has intuitive controls, but read the manual anyway. It makes a lot of beeping noises when using it, which is good for knowing when your water is ready, but can be a little noisy in the morning when turning it on while others are sleeping.

It is quite versatile with many standard settings for various types of tea (170-212F and in-between settings) and coffee (set to 205F). I also like the temperature hold feature. This lets me keep the water at 205F while allowing the grounds to bloom, then finishing the pour at the same 205 temperature. Temp seems pretty accurate (measured with ThermoPen). It's not super fast at getting there, but still faster than a traditional kettle.

The unit itself is comfortable to hold and operate, with a very smooth pour. The black metal looks great in the kitchen. Be aware its capacity is between 1/2 liter minimum and a 1 liter maximum. This is fine for 1 or 2 big mugs of liquid, which is 95% of my kettle usage.

It also lets you know when it needs to be descaled, and gives basic instructions for that (though I haven't gotten it to that point yet).

The only thing I wish it did differently is providing a lid that stayed attached when open (flip up style), or perhaps a handy place to keep the lid when not attached (a hook on the handle or something would be cool). Not a big issue obviously, but I was used to the flip up on my old kettle.

title: If you're keen on frustration, buy this brand of shelves; otherwise, try something else like Whitmor.
text:
I just spent an hour and a half unpacking, beginning to assemble, realizing the shelves were defective, then repackaging the whole thing to send back. The poles are too wide to fit the plastic sleeves that go between the poles and the holes in the shelves through which the poles pass. The sleeves are fine by themselves (without the poles) and fit fine by themselves in the holes, but the sleeves won't close around the poles, because the poles are just a bit too wide, so the poles with the sleeves on will not fit the shelves and the whole thing cannot be assembled.

This is an hour and a half I'll never get back, which is bad enough, but I probably should never have had to waste it in the first place. Yes, defects happen, but the package I received was taped up in that random way that says, "Someone already returned me once." In other words, this item was probably already bad for someone else, but I got sent it again anyway, so that the same package could waste not just one person's time, but two.

I bought a similar set of shelves from Whitmor, rather than Amazon Basics. Those were fine. Don't buy these.

title: Been a few years now
text:
I purchased this back in 2019 or 2018. It was down to this or a Stone And Beam sofa, another Amazon brand, but I ended up with this one.

Initially it's a great couch. It's very tiny, very suitable for a small apartment or living room. Over the years though there's been a few things that popped up. It pills badly. It stains badly. The cushion support starts to go especially the back cushions. It's impossible to clean the arms of this thing. The cushions slide out. The legs unscrew themselves somehow. Lastly the sofa material is coarse. Since it is tiny it's not high enough for me to put my head on.

I ended up purchasing the Lauren from Stone and Beam a year or two after this, and it's a much better couch for $200 more or so. It doesn't stain, it doesn't pill, it has enough height so you put your head on the couch, it's easy to clean, it's soft, nd the cushions are holding up, even though there's a dip in the middle of the back cushions.

I think a great starter couch but don't expect it to last more than 5 years. If you are a family, I would get something else but if it's just you, your partner and a pet then I would consider it.

I will say we love the ottoman. Use it every day and it's worth it.

title: Did not work, loose parts inside
text:
My daughter ordered this unit and through the box and paperwork out before trying it. It turns out the assembly was not completed. I could hear loose parts rattling inside and the fan appeared to be not bolted to the assembly. Obviously, they did NO testing after assembly!! I took it apart and found two screws rattling around loose inside. They were the two screws that hold the fan to the heater assembly. I attached the fan using the two screws but am still in the process of trying to assemble the complete unit. As others have noted, the wiring comes dangerously close to the heating unit. If I can get the unit assembled I will test it thoroughly before putting it to use. My recommendation is to NOT buy this unit. As noted, they obviously did not plug the unit in and test it before shipping. 0% product test.

Update a day later: I got it assembled okay, I did not alter any wiring but the fan would not turn on. The unit heated up but with no fan. Initially, some smoke came out. This may have been just due to the first time the heater was ever activated, burning off a coating of the heating element. I was able to get a return code and returned it to an Amazon drop-off. Very disappointed an "Amazon Basics" product has no quality control or unit testing.

title: Awesome pizza pan!
text:
So, I bought this pan to make New England "bar pizza" in our Breville countertop oven. I was concerned that it wouldn't fit, but it does! For those who want to cut the chase:
- I lightly season with avocado oil just before using.
- Made pizza and it came out without sticking. Would recommend putting dough into a cold pan and then baking for about 5-7 minutes before putting sauce and toppings on.
- Made grilled peppers, eggplant, artichokes, and tomatoes. Very little sticking.
- Cleanup has taken less than 5 minutes. HOT tap water and a stiff brush. Not too much scrubbing, just enough to get in between the ridges.

For those who want the unnecessary stuff:
I do a lot of product research before buying function-specific items like this pan. I looked at size (I didn't want to make little 12" pizzas), material (I didn't want non-stick coatings, so my choices were ceramic or cast iron), and cost (wasn't looking to break the bank on something that I knew would be a periodic "pizza phase". This perfectly fit all of my needs and had the added benefit of being able to double as a shallow grilling pan. It's not light (it is cast iron) but you can hold it with one hand if you need to. The little ridges on the bottom help a lot with stretching the dough to the edge and make nice little baby grill marks on food. Highly recommend!

title: Great Look, Comfortable - but longevity might not be it's strong suit
text:
Well it was a long winding road to get this couch, but I eventually did get it - but there is more.

Shipping:
The first time I ordered this couch it was guaranteed as a delivery date. A few days later the delivery date changed to 3 months out, so I canceled the order. Now Amazon customer service has been amazing through this whole process - and we worked on finding it when it was in stock to have it delivered. Finally it came to my house, signed for it - only to open the box and have it be the wrong color. I ended up keeping it since it matched better than I thought it would.

Product:

Now the couch is really pretty, clean lines, very comfortable - and at 6'5", it's great for lounging and does cover my long back when sitting upright. The fabric is really well put together, and the cushions are firm, but not like a brick - they are really comfortable. The assembly was easy (just the legs on the bottom) and I was ready to go. The design of this couch is fantastic and looks wonderful in my room!

I have cats, and surprisingly their little nails that get caught from time to time have not had any effect on the fabric (I thought it would be ruined by now), so the quality of that fabric is impressive.

A complaint I have had since I got it is that the back cushions seem to consistently push the seating cushions out a bit, requiring them to be pushed back into place a lot - but this is a minor gripe, and I may just get something to put underneath the cushions to hold them in place better.

Now the biggest issue started to crop up, is that the frame seems to have a creak when sitting on the right cushion - causing a really obnoxious sound to occur when I move, sit, or stand up from the couch (2 months after purchase). I thought since this has a 1 year warranty, I would see what can be done - come to find out, they don't have a lot of these in stock so they were unable to replace the couch for me.

Again - customer support has been nothing short of amazing on this and I feel like they righted the wrong on this...but it is upsetting that I am now with a creaky couch and have to go back out couch shopping again to replace this one.

title: Unit stopped working due to a poor quality switch - Video
text:
[[VIDEOID:2fa021bee64a480da889f8f101b936e1]] So this was a fine little heater until it wasn't. At some point, even though the power light was on, the fan and the heating element no longer did anything regardless of the position of the rotary switch.

I opened it up assuming I'd see some wire that had become loose and indeed, one of the wires from the switch was hanging free. The one labelled "L" on the switch. Not only was it loose, but the wire was covered with green copper corrosion.

So, I tried to simply push it back into the switch where it belongs, but it wouldn't stay in there. So, I opened up the switch (as you can see in the video), and the copper connecting "pressure plate" where the wire is supposed to be held in has corroded away.

Essentially, it's just a very cheap switch and the switch has failed. I don't know if the corrosion is due to too much heat, or just moisture in the environment. The unit never was in direct contact with water, so that wasn't it. It's a 125VAC switch, so we're lucky the wire just fell out instead of arcing or just getting hot and causing a fire.

All in all, it's AmazonBASICS for a reason... cheaply made for a cheap price. I wouldn't buy it again.

title: High quality at an excellent price
text:
April 19th Update: I ordered a second chair which I love just as much as the first. The quality and price of these chairs is clearly excellent. However, my delivery of the second chair was subpar and very different from the first. I ordered “room of choice”, in which the chair is supposed to be unboxed and placed in my room of choice. Instead, the entire gigantic dirty box was squeezed through my front door and dropped in my entry way, several hours earlier than they were even supposed to come. Now I have a mess to clean up, a giant chair to inbox and set up and drag where I want it, and a giant box to somehow get rid of. The first chair delivery was an excellent experience, with the delivery people unboxing, setting up and placing the chair exactly where I wanted it, making sure I was happy with it, and taking the box away for me. Amazon really needs to make sure their 3rd party large delivery carriers are all on the same page so one delivery (that should be exactly the same) isn’t so different from the next.

Original April 6th review: This chair has far exceeded my expectations. I ordered the swatch ahead of time, and the khaki color matched it perfectly. I was afraid of the khaki being too dark or yellowish but it isn’t- it’s a perfect lighter shade that is exactly what I was searching for. The slipcover fits perfectly and is a thick high quality material, and the chair is very comfortable. It’s a good size and can almost fit 2 smaller adults who are good friends. Yes, the legs are plastic but they are the color of a dark wood and are completely hidden so you’d only ever notice if you are cleaning underneath the chair. Don’t hesitate to buy this chair! It is comparable to Pottery Barn and MUCH higher quality than the somewhat similar looking chair at IKEA. I will be ordering another.

title: Beautiful dining table overall.
text: I was reluctant to purchase this dining table given the fact that at the time, it had zero customer reviews but decided to make the purchase since Stone & Beam is an Amazon brand backed by a 30-day return policy and a 3-year warranty. My experience with the purchase went smooth overall. The delivery was on-time and the shipping company brought the box into my dining area. The table, leaf, and base comes in one big box that weighed 160+ lbs. The item was packed well and there was no damage or missing parts which I was happy to see. Assembling it is essentially bolting the table top to the base which took about 30 minutes altogether. The color is stated as 'butterscotch' but the table is actually much darker in person - not quite walnut but close - which I actually prefer. Adding the leaf is very simple though it is not self-storing so you have to find a place to store it in a closet. I've had the table for about a week now and it seems sturdy enough but when you do knock on it with your knuckles, it doesn't have a solid sound but almost a hollow sound; not sure if it's because the hardwood top is thinner than my old table which was a thick piece of solid oak. Also, you can't see it in the pictures but the planked wood table top has little holes speckled throughout the top which lends to a rustic feel. Personally, I do not like this because I imagine tiny crumbs or water getting in there. Overall, it's a beautiful and versatile table, but it does have some downsides such as storing the leaf and the holes on the wood top.

Last thing is that the screws holding the seat cushions down are too long, very sharp, and will poke if you get the cushions compressed (such as if you kneel on the edge). All in all, not too bad for chairs in this price range. I expect them to last about five years before I need to replace them.
