title: A bit of a PITA to assemble, but once done it's great!
text:
Yes, I know it's a Basics item. Yes, I know it's not supposed to be all high class haute couture decor. BUT, for my purposes (a table for my game room) it works perfectly.

First the assembly - it's a bit of a pain in the tookus, though mostly at the end of the process. I appreciate that the components are kept fairly minimal, and the screws are (mostly) Phillips so the first 80% of the assembly went very quickly. The assembly isn't, to my mind, fully intuitive though so mind the instructions.

My difficulty came with attaching the table top portion to the leg assembly. You have four hex-key bolts to hold the two components together. Thing is, the bolts are tucked into the corners of the table top (inside the storage compartment) making them pretty difficult to get to. I ALWAYS use my impact driver for assembling things like this, and the angle of those bolts made getting the impact driver aligned a, well, frustrating experience. I tried using the included Allen wrench and that wasn't much better...the angle is such that you have to use the short end of the wrench and you only have room for a quarter turn before you have to remove and reseat the wrench.

Out of desperation I used a very long extension bit on the impact driver and that worked, though not to my liking....approaching at an angle like that greatly increases the risk of stripping the bolt. I managed it via that method, but again it wasn't my preference. A half an inch extra clearance on two sides of each bolt would have made the difference.

Once assembled, It's a good and sturdy piece. Certainly sturdy enough to work as a leg rest! Since this is for a game room I keep various gaming accessories (controllers, etc) in the storage compartment where there's plenty of room. It's great!

A note on the elevating top - it will lock into place when fully extended and you need to pull out the locking pin from the interior hinge before you can stow the top. I like that this makes for a very stable extended tabletop (certainly useful for using a laptop, as the top extends such that you have knee room underneath....) so no harm no foul...just a note.

One more note - this table is really quite heavy for its size, and fairly bulky to move when fully assembled. Assemble it in the place where you're going to put it and save your back muscles.

I think it's a very good table - solid materials, plenty of bolts to especially hold the lower assembly together, and the main body (table top/compartment) comes preassembled. Prepare for a little frustration on the last part of the assembly (forewarned is forearmed) and once you're past that you end up with a very good table. I like it.

title: Looks like it would be really comfortable, but it’s not. Looks are deceiving!
text:
This chair looks like it would be super comfortable, right? Alas, it isn’t. Maybe a tall person would have a different experience in it, but for me- barely 5’2”, sitting down on it as one normally sits on a chair, with knees at the front edge so you can have your feet flat on the floor strands me quite a distance from the back, so I’m sitting on it completely without any back support. It’s like sitting on an ottoman. And it’s nice, in that sense, but eventually one likes to lean back in a chair, and I can’t without weirdly bending backwards - by the time my shoulders make contact with the back of the chair, I look like I was interrupted in the middle of a backbend. Completely intolerable position for even two minutes.

It is a handsome looking chair, without question, but it is not at all a comfy chair, so while you find different positions to take on it, none of them are straightforward, chair-sitting positions that one would want to say, read a book, or have a cup of tea. If you’re looking for something stylish for a reception area, this might work well for you. If you are looking for something to relax into with a good book, this is not the chair for you.

title: Homemade Thick Crust Pizza - Look no further!
text: This pan is fantastic.  I have been making my own pizza for two years now... I am always looking to improve my process and as a result my pizza.  Up until this Christmas, I have solely made thin crust.  I decided to give a thick crust pan style pizza a go with this pan and was beyond thrilled with the results.  Homemade pizza is where this pan shines.  Others are using it for frozen pizza... I suppose that's a thing, but it's not exactly what the pan was intended for.  Others have mentioned rust issues.  This confuses me.  Simply put... don't put water on it.  Wipe it out when you are done... that's part of the seasoning process.  If you must use water, put it back in a warm oven for a while so that it can be completely dried out.  In short... If you take your pizza seriously, this is a tool you'll want to have in your arsenal.

title: Very comfy - just what I was looking for
text:
I was looking for a comfortable chair or couch that I could sit on that is cheap, comfy, easy to move around, and takes up little space. This AmazonBasics adjustable floor sofa was exactly what I was looking for.

It came in folded up in a big box that was easy to carry up a flight of stairs. I laid it flat and raised the back up to the angle I wanted - it locked and stayed locked. The couch itself feels very comfy and sturdy. From the pictures, I wasn't expecting too much in terms of support, but the cushions felt thick and comfortable. The exterior material is nothing fancy, but is easy to clean. I have it set up on a hardwood floor with no additional layers underneath and I've had no problems with the couch slipping or moving around while I'm using it. I especially like how I can easily lie it flat and hide it under the bed when I don't need it.

Overall, this is a quality and great looking floor sofa that is very easy to move around and use in a limited-space environment. Highly recommend!

title: Cast iron is great if you know what you’re doing
text:
Don’t buy cast iron if you don’t want to take the time to care for them. You guys showing how food sticks obviously are disillusioned with what cast iron is.
This isn’t a Teflon coated pan. The reason people use cast iron is the heat transfer process and this way it cooks food and the taste. I always use cast iron because I love how it holds heat. I can turn off my burner and it will continue to cook my steak or whatever without burning or over cooking it. I also can brown my steak or pot roast on the stove then transfer to the oven in the same pot. I love the taste of the food from cast iron’s. You do have to hand wash these. You boil with water if there’s something stuck on and it will come off easy. You have to oil them regularly. I oil after each use. These don’t scratch so you can scrub them with anything and they’re still perfect. They also last forever so you’ll never have to buy a new one. I got mine at a thrift store, no telling how old it is but it still looks brand new. I’m probably gonna buy this set as well. I also have a cast iron Wak that I cook in everyday. I absolutely love it.

title: Very happy with purchase!
text:
I read a ton of reviews to try to pick a slim hanger to get some more space in my closet, and these arrived this week and worked out great.

All hangers arrived in great condition. Other reviews said many arrived broken, but everything was in working order and made it in my closet with no issues.

Other reviews also mentioned that the black came off the hangers and they had to be pre soaked. I didn't see any of this, and put my clothes on these hangers on my white bed spread and didn't notice any black shedding.

The hangers are also definitely space saving. I had previously used the plastic hangers that come directly from the store, and this definitely gives you a bit more space in the closet. I attached a photo so you can see the difference between 25 of these hangers vs 25 of the regular store hangers in my closet - a definite difference!

As far as how sturdy they are, they've worked for all my blouses and cocktail dresses really nicely. The plus is that nothing slides off! I have one coat on one and it actually seems to be holding up nicely.

The only thing I would have liked is if the hanger heads swiveled, but they're not advertised as doing so, so I didn't expect that and am totally fine as is, and actually just repurchased it to change the rest of my closet hangers to these slimmer ones!

title: I threw out my plastic hangers SO quick
text:
I needed new hangers so I decided to go ahead and try the Amazon brand since they're known for their quality, and man, these are great.

You'd be surprised with how much space you'll save using these versus the standard, bulky plastic ones. These are very thin and light, and although I only bough one order of 50, they take up about the third of the space of the previous hangers I've had. I'm going to place my second order after writing this review.

I had no problems with the condition I received them in. They were packaged neatly in an easy to open cardboard box and the hangers themselves were placed in easy to rip open plastic in two bags of 25 each. They were all facing the same way and put together neatly so it was super easy to just take them out and begin hanging my clothes with them. There was barely any lint or debris on the hangers themselves when I received them or any noticeable defects. I've had them since July of last year and they're still doing great. I drop them all the time because of my clumsiness and I'll admit, there are some currently on the floor right now due to it being laundry day. I've stepped on them on accidentally, I've even laid down on one that was hiding between my comforter and they're still unbent and doing fine. If it was the plastic ones that I had before, it would've broken and stabbed me and I probably wouldn't be alive today to write this.

If I absolutely HAD to say something negative about them, it's that you have to remember these are velvet, so if you accidentally drop them on your carpet sometimes (like I do) you might have some fuzz get stuck to them. That's easily solved by getting a lint roller and running it over them a few times though. I haven't really noticed any lint from my clothes rubbing off on them either, so all in all it's definitely a good investment. Also, I know these can't hang folded pants, but amazon has the velvet hangers that have the bottom portion of the hanger as well as those little add on clips. I personally fold my pants, so I like these hangers best.

You save money, space, and your closet will look better visually by having slim, uniform hangers as opposed to mismatched, bulky, plastic hangers that break if you step on them and will become worn out and discolored over time. These are sturdy, but don't burden your clothes rack heavily and will hang everything wonderfully. What's even betters is that they're great for those articles of clothing that love to slide off the plastic hangers. The velvet holds them securely so that they won't drop off. No more waking up in the middle of the night scared shitless because you heard something fall inside your closet. That reason alone should have you adding this item to your cart.

After using them for half a year, they still look brand new and are still performing wonderfully. These are a wonderful price, the quality is great, and I assure you that using these will definitely make a difference for the better.

title: The specs are an absolute lie.
text:
We did not expect much from this sofa, but this sofa is literally made out of garbage. It's incredibly wobbly and uncomfortable. What really threw us for a loop, however, was when an upholsterer stripped the fabric and foam to expose the frame.

The bulk of the frame is 1x1 and 1x2 made of pine furring strips (not hardwood). The rest is compressed plywood or leftover parts like legs that have been shoved in for extra support. The sinuous springs are attached to the edge of the frame with lengths of separated zippers. The best part though: the side and back panels are made of cardboard!

Needless to say, we scrapped it once it was torn down, but Amazon should be ashamed of itself for selling such garbage with dishonest specifications.

title: Legs are Uneven
text: Love the style of these chairs, but after careful assembly following the directions, the legs on 5 of the 6 chairs I purchased are uneven. The legs are actually all the same length, but the bolt holes for attaching the rear legs to the seat bottom are higher on one side. This in turn causes one of the front legs to "kick" up. The worst one is shown in the photos: front leg is up 1/2 inch, the other photo shows the underside of the seat bottom where it is 1/4" out of alignment near where the bolt holes are.  I contacted Ashley to let them know their manufacturing drill jigs at their plant in Vietnam (where these chairs are made) were out of alignment, but their reply was to contact Amazon for resolution.  This rote response from Ashley made me think they wouldn't bother to correct the problem at their manufacturing plant so if I returned these chairs then any new chairs I received as replacements would likely have the same problem.  As another reviewer here wrote, I needed to nail soft foot pads on the bottom of the legs anyway so I put washers on the front leg of the 5 wonky chairs to shim them up level, but a 1/2" of washers on that one chair looks ridiculous. Oh well, nobody notices the chair feet anyway and the chairs look great otherwise and were very affordable.

title: Not 100% Real Down—Has foam
text:
[[VIDEOID:d764ec748061f0dd7fb325c5234cd8c9]] Pros: the size of the loveseat is perfect for what I needed, since I was using it to replace uncomfortable RV furniture. The cushions and the covers are removable. Fabric is soft and of decent quality. Color is true to the pictures—I ordered cream.

Cons: The MAIN reason this isn’t getting 5 stars is because it borders false advertising. It’s not real down in the cushions, it’s almost 4-5 inches of stiff foam and mayyybbee 1 inch of measly down filling on each side of the foam. When you sit down, it’s entirely too stiff to be down. I have a real down couch in my home, so perhaps that’s why I noticed a huge difference.

I intend to remove the foam and fill the internal case with a mix of shredded memory foam and down to get the feel I was hoping for.

Overall, the couch looks nice (I just got it, so I have yet to experience the pilling described in other reviews). It’s a great size for just me and my husband, BUT the feel of the couch was very disappointing. If you’re not used to real down, you’ll probably think it’s soft and perfectly fine, but my real down filled couch has me setting high standards for all my future (supposed) “down-filled” couches.

title: Caring for cast iron
text:
For all you people complaining about rust, cast iron has to be cared for in a certain way or it will rust. Here are some tips...
Wash cast iron by hand with a nylon bristle scrub brush. ...
Dry promptly and thoroughly with a lint-free cloth or paper towel.
Rub with a very light layer of cooking oil or our Seasoning Spray, preferably while the cookware is still warm.
Hang or store cookware in a dry place.

title: I’m heartbroken and angry!!!
text:
I have fibromyalgia and I wanted a super comfy down cushioned chair for my studio that was huge and wouldn’t add any pressure to places that were already hurting. I looked all over the internet and tried to find something that would be BOTH large enough for me to curl up in that would have down filled cushions- and I found this chair on Amazon. At the original price, it wasn’t as expensive as places like Pottery Barn and West Elm- but it was only slightly cheaper than the down filled chairs on Wayfair with the custom upholstery. And it’s a lot of money for a chair!!
But my husband knew I was looking at it, caught it on sale and surprised me with it.
When I first sat on it, it was quite firm- way more firm than I thought down would be, but I just thought maybe it was overfilled and it needed some break in time.

But no matter how I turned the cushions, it started compressing. I’m 5’10 and wear a 12/14 so I’m not a tiny girl, but I’m not massive either. I started looking at bags of down to add to my cushions, preparing myself mentally for having to cut open the inner cushion bag and sewing it up by hand afterwards (something I was NOT looking forward to) and I unzipped the cushion to see what kind of fabric I would be dealing with.

Imagine my delight when I saw a zipper!! Woohoo!! Now I can just stuff some more feathers in there and zip it back up!! Now imagine my dismay when I opened the zipper and saw that big block of hard foam sandwiched between two tiny layers of feathers!!! There is absolutely ZERO mention of foam in the cushions ANYWHERE. If there had been, I wouldn’t have wanted it and I would have kept looking. Now, this chair is waaaaaaaaayyyyyy past the return window and I’m going to have to figure out someway to make this cushion work for me until I can save up and get the chair I actually thought I was getting.

I will NEVER buy big items that matter from Amazon ever again.

text: I drink iced tea year round and love it in the hot summer.  I'd always boiled water and steeped tea bags in an old plastic pitcher.  When I saw this Iced Tea Maker, I thought I'd try it, even though I didn't think it would be much of an upgrade over my old boiling method.  Was I ever wrong!  How did I ever get along without this?!  It's so simple to use.  I just fill the reservoir with water, put tea bags in the basket and fill the pitcher with ice.  A press of the button and in less than 5 minutes I have cold iced tea!!  There is a switch on the front of the machine to select the darkness of the tea, as well.  Naturally I broke the glass pitcher after a few months, but I was able to substitute a plastic pitcher that I had and it fits perfectly.  I haven't used the infuser yet, because I prefer plain iced tea.  If you love iced tea, you have to try this machine!

title: Beautiful Space-saving Table
text: Made of sturdy material, this little gem was easy to assemble. You will need a Philips screwdriver, both long and short handle.  The screws are secured by grooved copper anchors. Make sure the groove is facing outward.  If the screw is hard to insert (as the anchor may not line up) use the groove to hold it in place or move on to another screw and come back to the problem screw later (best remedy I found). I noticed the springs bowed (something the instructions do not address).  Having the bow angle toward the hardware seemed to make it more secure.  For the inside screws, I found it easier to lay the table on the side and use  a short handle screwdriver. Top seemed to pop up at first but after putting something heavy on top of it (once it was fully constructed) the springs seemed to conform to the position and now I have no problems.  The hidden compartment measures 9 wide (edge to edge) and 5.5 deep. Sturdy and attractive table.  I love it.

text:
Let me preface my review by saying I’m not a Michelin chef; heck, I have a hard time working my way around an InstaPot, so when I tell you this is easy to use and makes a nice breakfast sandwich, that’s saying a lot. I would add that it took me a couple of tries to get my “preferred” choice, so you might want to play around with yours as well, but this is what I discovered. First, if you want to make an imitation Egg McMuffin, it’s best to put the cheese directly next to the English Muffin and the Canadian Bacon on the Cheese on the bottom, and when you crack the egg, it’s best to break the yolk and stir it around a bit to distribute it before you pout it on the plate and put the other half of the English Muffin on top.

I also discovered, at least for my taste, setting the cooking time for 6 1/2 minutes prepared the English Muffin better than shorter times as it was a “better bite” and the egg seemed to have been cooked a bit better. I also discovered that when you remove the Breakfast sandwich, if you turn it over (so the cheese is on top) and let it sit for a few moments, it will let everything settle and there’s a much less chance the Sandwich will drip.

Finally, whenever I made these Breakfast Sandwiches, I discovered my wife showed up to have a bite, which turned in to her eating half of the Sandwich, so now, whenever I decide to use this, I make two so she can have her own. It’s gotten to the point she’s started placing “special orders,” like changing out the cheese (try sliced white cheddar), put in bacon instead of Canadian Bacon, toast the English Muffin first and reduce the cooking time so the egg isn’t as well done...I’ve created a monster.

title: Drew the Short Straw - Twice!!!
text:
While I saw several negative reviews for the mattress, it appeared the positive far outweighed the negative. We received mattress several days later than expected with no reason given. When it arrived, the box was in terrible condition, but mattress appeared to be fine. Set up was easy and we opened up and began watching the progress. The manufacturer info said bed could take up to three days to expand to full 12”. We slept in guest bedroom for a week waiting, thinking cooler winter weather may be slowing progress. The main mattress never expanded beyond 10”, while two corners remained very hard and only expanded to 8”. The other two corners made it to 9”.

I called Amazon to ask for replacement thinking we got a lemon. Amazon service was amazing and agreed to send replacement for expedited shipping at no charge. Sadly, this was processed correctly, but I received another notice for delayed shipping. I don’t know if this is a manufacturer issue as this is my first product taking more than three days.

This time box was in great shape. We placed mattress on platform and went back to guest room. Sadly a week later we’re worse than the first. Mattress bottom is bowed, only one small section made it to 10”, two corners harder than before only expanded to 7”, other two corners 8” and still hard, and overall thickness is only 9”. I again called Amazon, this time requesting refund. I can’t say enough good about the service from Amazon. While we had high hopes for a mattress in a box, we’ve decided to go local and try the mattress’ out.

My suggestion, don’t purchase this brand. I’m sure there are many box mattress that are great, but can not recommend this.

title: Perfect Replacement Piston
text: If you're office chair piston has gone bad and you need something heavy duty, then this may be the one for you.  It all depends on your chair.  The piston I was replacing was about 3 inches shorter than this one in full extension and I was concerned I wouldn't be able to get the chair to go low enough.  Not to worry though, when I got it mounted in the 2-inch hole for the base, it sank in enough to give me the lowering range I wanted.  I then put the piston end into the bottom of the chair seat mechanism and that was that.  Made sure to put some lubricating oil on both ends in case I need to remove it in the future.  Using some anti-seize paste would be the best for this.  The chair does go higher than with the stock piston that came with the chair, but I'm 6' 2" so that's not necessarily a bad thing and it lowers to the preferred height as well.  I will update this review if the piston fails, but it seems to be quite sturdy out of the box.
